definition_zh: 睡眠；沉睡；打盹；沉寂；潜伏未动（如火山）；使沉睡
definition_en: a peaceful state of sleep, or a long period in which something is quiet and inactive
core_image: 一个人陷在软枕里安睡，呼吸平缓，四周静得能听见自己的心
scene: 山谷里的老钟停摆多年，屋顶积着厚灰，窗内的藤椅仍摊着一条毯子。The old mill slumbered beside the river while the town slowly woke.
sceneCN: 这里 slumber 是「沉睡、处于静止未动的状态」（第 2 个义项：事物长期安静、毫无活动）；句意：小镇慢慢醒来，而河边的老磨坊仍在沉睡。画面里能辨认的物件有停摆的钟、积灰的屋顶、摊着毯子的藤椅。

pos.zh: 名词：睡眠；沉睡；沉寂状态
动词：睡觉；安睡；静止不动；沉睡未醒
不及物动词：打盹；处于潜伏或不受注意的状态

collocations.zh: （某物）安卧在……之下；长眠于……之下

derivatives.zh: 由本词加形容词后缀 -ous 构成，义为「昏昏欲睡的；令人困倦的」
slumberous 的较古老变体拼写，义为「昏沉的；安静的」
由动词加 -er 构成，义为「安睡者」
由本词加 -y 构成的较旧形容形式，义为「瞌睡的」

senses.title: Ordinary sleep
senses.definition: the natural state of sleeping, especially when calm and unbroken
senses.definitionCN: 自然入睡的状态，尤指安静而连续的睡眠
senses.example: The baby drifted into slumber before the story ended.
senses.exampleCN: 故事还没讲完，婴儿就慢慢睡着了。
senses.why: The word descends from a verb meaning to sleep drowsily, so the plain act of sleeping is the oldest layer of meaning.
senses.whyCN: 这个词来自一个表示「昏昏睡去」的古英语动词，所以「睡觉」这一最朴素的动作是最早的义项层次。

senses.title: Long inactivity
senses.definition: a state in which something stays quiet, still, and inactive for a long time
senses.definitionCN: 事物长时间安静、静止、毫无活动的状态
senses.example: The factory came back to life after years of slumber.
senses.exampleCN: 沉寂多年后，这家工厂又重新开工了。
senses.why: Sleep already implies stillness, so the word easily transfers to places and institutions that are quiet for a season or a decade.
senses.whyCN: 睡眠本身就意味着静止，所以这个词很自然就迁移到一季或十年都静静无声的地点与机构上。

senses.title: A brief nap
senses.definition: a light, short period of sleep rather than a long one
senses.definitionCN: 轻微、短暂的睡眠，而不是长时间的安睡
senses.example: He took a slumber in the armchair after lunch.
senses.exampleCN: 午饭后他在扶手椅上打了个盹。
senses.why: The same verb also names dozing off in a chair, so the noun carries a light, brief flavour next to the heavy one.
senses.whyCN: 同一个动词也指在椅子上打瞌睡，因此名词在「沉沉大睡」之外另带一层「轻轻一晃就醒」的味道。

senses.title: Literary peace
senses.definition: a poetic or solemn word for peaceful rest, often used in verse and in eulogies
senses.definitionCN: 诗歌或庄重语境中对安静歇息的雅称，常用于诗行与悼词
senses.example: The poet praised the slumber of the quiet valley.
senses.exampleCN: 诗人赞美山谷安眠般的宁静。
senses.why: Because it was the literary word for sleep, it kept a solemn and poetic tone that plain sleep does not have.
senses.whyCN: 因为长期作为睡眠的文学用语，它保有一层 plain sleep 所没有的庄重与诗意。

senses.title: A mountain or volcano asleep
senses.definition: the inactive state of a volcano or landscape that has long been still
senses.definitionCN: 火山或地貌长期不再活动的状态
senses.example: Steam rose from the slumber of the snow covered peak.
senses.exampleCN: 那座积雪的山峰在半梦半醒间冒出热气。
senses.why: Natural writers personified volcanoes as sleeping giants, and slumber became the technical-lively word for dormancy.
senses.whyCN: 自然作家把火山比作沉睡的巨人，slumber 于是成了描述「休眠」的标准而有生命感的说法。

senses.title: To sleep soundly
senses.definition: to sleep, especially calmly and without waking
senses.definitionCN: 入睡，尤指平静地、不被打扰地睡着
senses.example: The house slumbered under a heavy blanket of snow.
senses.exampleCN: 房子在厚厚一层雪下静静安睡。
senses.why: The Old English verb slumerian meant to sleep dully or drowsily, and the modern verb keeps that calm slowness.
senses.whyCN: 古英语动词 slumerian 意为「昏沉地睡」，现代动词保留了这种缓慢而平静的节奏。

senses.title: To stay dormant
senses.definition: to be present but not active, noticed, or used for a long time
senses.definitionCN: 存在却长久不活动、未被注意或被搁置
senses.example: Old disputes slumbered in the family for a generation.
senses.exampleCN: 家族里的旧怨沉睡了一代人的时间。
senses.why: Anything that is quietly there but not acting looks asleep, so the verb covers dormant rivalries, funds, or talents.
senses.whyCN: 任何安静存在却不发作的东西看起来都处于沉睡状态，于是动词也覆盖潜伏的纷争、闲置的资金与埋没的才能。

senses.title: A party for teenagers
senses.definition: a party at which young guests stay overnight and sleep at the hosts home
senses.definitionCN: 一群年轻客人在主人家里过夜留宿的聚会
senses.example: She asked to hold her birthday slumber party in the garden.
senses.exampleCN: 她要求在花园里办她的生日睡衣派对。
senses.why: American English uses slumber in compounds for sleepovers, taking the word out of verse and into ordinary social life.
senses.whyCN: 美式英语用 slumber 构成指「留宿玩耍」的复合词，把这个词从诗歌带回了普通的社交生活。

senses.title: To send to sleep
senses.definition: to make a person or animal fall asleep, usually softly or by magic
senses.definitionCN: 使人或动物入睡，常指轻柔地或以一种奇妙的方式使之入眠
senses.example: The nurse slumbered the child with a quiet song.
senses.exampleCN: 护士用一首低低的歌哄孩子睡去。
senses.why: A few transitive uses make the verb causative, so slumber can also mean to put someone to sleep.
senses.whyCN: 少数及物用法让这个动词带上使役色彩，于是 slumber 也能表示「把某人哄睡」。

intro.en: Slumber comes from Middle English slumeren, from Old English slumerian, seemingly from a root of sleap and related to the sluggish verb slumberen; the deeper origin is uncertain.
intro.cn: slumber 来自中古英语 slumeren，源于古英语 slumerian，看来源自表「睡」的词根并与表「迟钝」的动词有关；更早的词源不确定。

items.en: A root *sluma- or *sluma meaning drowsiness is reconstructed, but only from the recorded Germanic forms, so it is called a reconstructed form.
items.cn: 学界重构出表示「昏沉」的词根 *sluma-，但它只能从已记录的日耳曼语形式反推，属于重构形式。

items.en: Slumerian means to sleep dully or be sluggish, beside slæp, the ordinary word for sleep.
items.cn: slumerian 意为「昏睡、迟钝」，与常用词 slæp（睡眠）并列。

items.en: Slumeren appears with the same sense, and the noun slumber is formed from the verb.
items.cn: slumeren 以同样含义出现，名词 slumber 由动词派生。

items.en: Slumber is recorded in verse and prose as a literary word for sleep and for drowsiness.
items.cn: slumber 见于诗歌与散文，作为表示「睡眠、困倦」的文学用语。

items.en: Writers extend it to quiet places, and slumbering becomes a standard word for a dormant volcano.
items.cn: 作家把它扩展到安静的地方，slumbering 成为描述休眠火山的常用说法。

items.en: The word keeps a literary tone except in American compounds such as slumber party.
items.cn: 除美式复合词 slumber party 等以外，这个词仍保持文学语调。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers sl- words that only share sound; the near-meaning group gathers quiet rest words with different levels of sleep.
note.cn: 形近组收了只共享读音的 sl- 系列词；近义组收了表示安静歇息的词，睡眠深浅各有不同。

entries.definition: A poor crowded district of a city; it merely looks similar and comes from another root.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「贫民窟、破败街区」；只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: A sharp drop in trade or prices, or to sit down heavily; it merely looks similar and comes from another root.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或动词，义为「暴跌、萧条」或「重重坐下」；只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning sleepy or causing drowsiness; formed from slumber plus the suffix -ous.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「昏昏欲睡的、令人困倦的」，由本词加后缀 -ous 构成。

entries.definition: The plain and commonest word for the regular state of rest; neutral in tone.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或动词，义为「睡眠、睡觉」，最普通、语气中性的词。

entries.definition: A short light sleep, especially one that happens by accident.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或动词，义为「打盹」，多指不知不觉的短暂浅睡。

entries.definition: A short sleep during the day, usually planned and refreshing.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「小睡、午睡」，多为白天的短睡，睡后精神恢复。

entries.definition: A state of calm rest, formal and often used of peace after effort.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「安歇、安宁」，语气正式，常指努力之后的平静。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the recorded Old English root and the phrases slumber really appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用有记录的古英语词根，以及 slumber 实际所在的搭配。

normal.en: Slumber sits beside sleep and keeps the older drowsy tone, so it sounds bookish.
normal.cn: slumber 与 sleep 并列，却带着更古老的困倦语气，所以听起来偏书面。

normal.en: Fall into a slumber is the standard verb phrase, and deep slumber is the usual noun phrase.
normal.cn: fall into a slumber 是标准动词词组，deep slumber 是常用名词词组。

normal.en: Slumbering volcano is technical but lively, and it fits written geology as well as poetry.
normal.cn: slumbering volcano 既专业又有画面，地质写作和诗歌都适用。

normal.en: Slumber party is American and means a sleepover, with no hint of drowsy old poetry.
normal.cn: slumber party 是美式说法，指留宿聚会，毫无古旧诗意。

normal.en: Do not confuse slumber with slumberous: one is the rest itself, the other describes how sleepy it feels.
normal.cn: 别混淆 slumber 与 slumberous：前者是歇息本身，后者描述那种困倦的感觉。

abstract.en: Picture a cat curled in a warm ring of light on the floor.
abstract.cn: 想象一只猫蜷在地面一圈暖光里。

abstract.en: Imagine a clock tower with its hands frozen at a quiet hour.
abstract.cn: 想象一座钟楼，指针停在一个安静的时辰。

abstract.en: Think of a giant sleeping under grass, breathing very slowly.
abstract.cn: 想象一位巨人在草地之下沉睡，呼吸极缓。

examples.en: The village slumbered through the long winter nights.
examples.cn: 整个冬天漫长的夜里，村庄都在沉睡。

examples.en: She fell into a deep slumber as soon as the light went out.
examples.cn: 灯一关，她就沉沉睡去。

examples.en: Old ambitions slumbered in him until the letter arrived.
examples.cn: 旧日的雄心在他心里沉睡，直到那封信寄来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「睡啦吧」——妈妈一说「睡啦吧」，孩子就蜷进枕头安静入眠；这只是读音联想，不是词源。

root: 古英语 slumerian（昏睡、迟钝）→ 中古英语 slumeren → 英语 slumber。一般认为与表「睡」的 slæp 相关，而且词义天生带「缓慢、昏沉」；更早的日耳曼语词根 *sluma- 属于重构形式，来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses all rest on one image of quiet sleep: the ordinary act, a long still period, a brief nap, a literary name for peace, a sleeping mountain, the verb for sleeping, the verb for staying dormant, an American sleepover compound, and a rare causative use.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项都围绕「安静的睡眠」这一意象：普通的睡觉动作、长久的静止、短暂的打盹、文学里的安眠、沉睡的山、表睡觉的动词、表潜伏的动词、美式的留宿复合词，以及少见的使役用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person sunk into a soft pillow, breathing slowly, with the whole room finally quiet.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人陷进软枕，呼吸缓慢，整个房间终于安静下来。

branches.en: THE PERSON: ordinary sleep and a short nap are the human core of the word.
branches.cn: 人身线：普通睡眠与短暂打盹，是这个词最贴近人的核心。

branches.en: THE THING: a still campus or a dormant fund is the same sleep seen in objects and institutions.
branches.cn: 事物线：安静的校园与闲置的资金，是睡眠投射到物件与机构上的样子。

branches.en: THE VERSE: poetry and eulogy use the word as a solemn name for peaceful rest.
branches.cn: 诗行线：诗歌与悼词用它作安歇的雅称，语气庄重。

branches.en: THE LAND: a sleeping mountain keeps the verb close to landscape and geology.
branches.cn: 地貌线：沉睡的山把动词与地貌、地质紧紧连在一起。

branches.en: THE TWISTS: the American sleepover compound and the rare causative use are the light and unexpected ends of the word.
branches.cn: 转折线：美式留宿复合词与少见的使役用法，是这个词最俏皮、最出人意料的两端。

intro.en: Slumber is Germanic rather than Latin: English builds its family with the suffixes -ous, -er and -y.
intro.cn: slumber 属日耳曼语而不是拉丁语来源；英语靠后缀 -ous、-er、-y 扩展出它的词族。

latinIntro.en: No Latin ancestor is recorded; the Old English verb slumerian is the documented source, so the Latin list stays empty.
latinIntro.cn: 没有可考的拉丁语来源，有文献记录的直接来源是古英语动词 slumerian，因此拉丁同源词表留空。

items.example: The Old English verb is the recorded source.
items.exampleCN: 这个古英语动词是有记录的来源。

items.example: Middle English keeps the same drowsy sense.
items.exampleCN: 中古英语保留了同样的昏沉义。

items.example: The noun is formed from the verb.
items.exampleCN: 名词由动词派生而来。

items.example: The verb keeps the calm pace of the old word.
items.exampleCN: 动词保留了古词那种平静的节奏。

items.example: The suffix -ous forms slumberous.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ous 构成 slumberous。

items.example: The suffix -er forms slumberer.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -er 构成 slumberer。

items.example: The suffix -y forms slumbery.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -y 构成 slumbery。

items.example: The compound is chiefly American.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词主要用于美式英语。

items.example: Slumbering is used of volcanoes and towns.
items.exampleCN: slumbering 常用于火山与城镇。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ous 构成，义为「昏昏欲睡的、令人困倦的」
由动词加 -er 构成，义为「安睡者」
slumberous 的古老变体拼写，义为「昏沉的、安静的」

definition_zh: 暴跌；跌价；萧条；衰退；（身体）重重坐下；颓然倒下；倒下时蜷伏的姿势；使跌落
definition_en: a sudden heavy fall in prices, sales, or performance, or the act of sitting or falling down heavily
core_image: 肩一垮、整个人重重塌降，随之而来的是一条向下滑落的曲线
scene: 季度报表摆在桌上，销售曲线的尾端突然垂直拉下一截；街角曾经排队的店铺如今只剩空招牌。Sales slumped sharply after the new tax was announced.
sceneCN: 这里 slump 是「（销售额、股价等）骤跌」（第 1 个义项：数量或价格突然大幅下降）；句意：新税公布后，销售额骤降。画面里能辨认的物件有下滑的销售曲线、空荡荡的店铺招牌和摊开的报表。

pos.zh: 动词：暴跌；大幅下降；重重坐下；颓然倒下
形容词：（作定语）萧条的；下跌的

collocations.zh: 大萧条（尤指二十世纪三十年代）

derivatives.zh: 由过去分词转为形容词，义为「瘫坐的；塌陷驼背的」
由现在分词转为形容词，义为「下滑中的；下跌的」
由本词加 -y 构成的少见形容词，义为「塌陷松软的」

senses.title: A sudden fall in numbers
senses.definition: a sharp and sudden reduction in sales, prices, or values
senses.definitionCN: 销售量、价格或数值突然而显著地下降
senses.example: The company reported a slump in sales last winter.
senses.exampleCN: 公司报告去年冬天销售额骤降。
senses.why: The word is recorded in the seventeenth century for sinking down, and the falling image later moved onto prices and figures.
senses.whyCN: 这个词十七世纪就有「陷落、下沉」的用法，下坠的画面后来才转移到价格与数字上。

senses.title: A depressed economy
senses.titleCN: 经济萧条期；不景气时期
senses.definition: a long period of weak trade, falling production, and high unemployment
senses.definitionCN: 贸易疲软、生产下降、失业率居高不下的较长时期
senses.example: Many families lost their savings during the slump.
senses.exampleCN: 那场萧条中，许多家庭失去了积蓄。
senses.why: If every figure slumps at once, the whole period gets named after the plunge, so a slump becomes a national condition.
senses.whyCN: 如果所有数字同时暴跌，整段时期就会被下坠的画面命名，于是 slump 变成一种全国性的状况。

senses.title: To drop sharply
senses.definition: for prices, sales, or levels to fall quickly and heavily
senses.definitionCN: 价格、销量或水平迅速而明显地下降
senses.example: Profits slumped by a fifth in one quarter.
senses.exampleCN: 利润在一个季度里下跌了五分之一。
senses.why: The verb carries the same heavy drop as the noun, with nothing soft or gradual about it.
senses.whyCN: 动词与名词共享同一种沉重的下坠，没有一丝缓慢或轻柔。

senses.title: To sit down heavily
senses.definition: to sit or drop into a seat with the whole body, as if strength has gone
senses.definitionCN: 整个人塌进座位里坐下，仿佛力气都用尽了
senses.example: She slumped into the chair and said nothing.
senses.exampleCN: 她一下子瘫进椅子里，一言不发。
senses.why: A body that loses strength drops instead of lowering itself, so the physical collapse is the oldest visual sense.
senses.whyCN: 失去力气的身体会往下坠而不是稳稳坐下，所以身体的塌落是这个词最古老的画面义。

senses.title: To lean or bend down
senses.definition: for a body, posture, or object to droop, sink, or lose its shape
senses.definitionCN: 身体、姿势或物体下垂、塌陷、失去轮廓
senses.example: The old barn roof was slumping under the snow.
senses.exampleCN: 旧谷仓的屋顶在积雪下塌陷下去。
senses.why: Anything without support slides downward, so roofs, shoulders, and even scaffolding can slump.
senses.whyCN: 任何失去支撑的东西都会向下滑，所以屋顶、肩膀甚至脚手架都可以用 slump 来描述。

senses.title: The posture after a fall
senses.definition: a heavy or limp body position at rest, with the back or side bent down
senses.definitionCN: 静止时沉重或瘫软的身体姿势，背部或一侧向下弯塌
senses.example: He lay in a slump against the wall.
senses.exampleCN: 他靠着墙瘫倒着。
senses.why: The heavy drop is caught as a frozen shape, so the noun also names the way the body lies afterward.
senses.whyCN: 沉重的下坠被定格成一个形状，因此名词也能指身体倒下后的姿态。

senses.title: To make something fall
senses.definition: to cause a value or a person to drop or be weakened, as in an old sports use
senses.definitionCN: 使数值或某人下降、削弱，见于较旧的用法（如运动语境中的一种说法）
senses.example: Bad weather slumped the harvest figures.
senses.exampleCN: 恶劣天气把收成数字拉低了。
senses.why: Rarer transitive uses let an outside force cause the fall, extending the verb beyond the subject itself.
senses.whyCN: 较少见的及物用法让外力成为下坠的原因，使动词的作用范围超出主语本身。

senses.title: Slumping as a trend
senses.definition: used before a noun to describe something in decline, especially an economy or a market
senses.definitionCN: 放在名词前，描述正在下滑的事物，尤指经济或市场
senses.example: Slumping demand closed two factories this year.
senses.exampleCN: 需求下滑，今年关掉了两家工厂。
senses.why: A present participle in front of a noun turns the movement into a label, so slumping demand names a trend, not one event.
senses.whyCN: 放在名词前的现在分词把动作变成标签，所以 slumping demand 指一种趋势，而不只是一次事件。

senses.title: Slump as a game score
senses.definition: a run of very poor results for a team or a player, chiefly in American English
senses.definitionCN: 球队或运动员一段持续不佳的表现，主要用于美式英语
senses.example: The striker broke his slump with two goals.
senses.exampleCN: 这名前锋打进两球，走出了低迷期。
senses.why: Sport borrowed the economic plunge for a run of low scores, so the same downward curve describes a losing streak.
senses.whyCN: 体育借用了经济上的下坠说法来描述连续低分，同一条下坠曲线因此也用来形容低迷期。

intro.en: Slump is a seventeenth-century English word of uncertain origin, apparently related to Scandinavian words for slipping or plopping down.
intro.cn: slump 是十七世纪的英语词，词源不确定，一般认为与斯堪的纳维亚语中表示「滑落、扑通落下」的词有关。

items.en: Forms in Norwegian and Danish such as slumpe mean to fall or happen by chance, and they are the likely source; the identification is not certain.
items.cn: 挪威语与丹麦语中的 slumpe 等词义为「跌落、偶然发生」，很可能是来源；但这一认定并不确定。

items.en: Slump is first recorded as a verb for sinking or slipping down heavily, especially of ice or snow.
items.cn: slump 最早作为动词出现，意为沉重地下沉或滑落，尤指冰或雪。

items.en: The verb extends to a person sitting down heavily, and the noun appears for that heavy fall.
items.cn: 动词扩展到人重重坐下的动作，名词也随之出现，指这种沉重的下落。

items.en: The economic sense, a fall in prices or trade, is recorded in the late nineteenth century and spreads quickly in newspapers.
items.cn: 表示价格或贸易下跌的经济义在十九世纪后期有记录，并很快在报纸上流行开来。

items.en: The economic depression of the period is widely called the Slump in British writing.
items.cn: 这一时期的经济萧条在英国文字中常被称为 the Slump。

items.en: Sport and commerce extend the word to a losing run, falling demand, and slumping figures.
items.cn: 体育与商业把词义扩展到连败低迷、需求下降与下滑的数字等用法。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers sl- words that only share sound; the near-meaning group gathers falls and slides with different weight.
note.cn: 形近组收了只共享读音的 sl- 系列词；近义组收了「下降、滑落」一类的词，分量与速度各不相同。

entries.definition: A poor crowded district of a city; it merely looks similar and comes from another root.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「贫民窟、破败街区」；只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: A literary word for sleep; it merely looks similar and comes from another root.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或动词，义为「睡眠」，属文学用语；只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: An adjective for someone sitting or standing with bent shoulders; formed from the past participle of slump.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「瘫坐的、驼背塌肩的」，由 slump 的过去分词转化而来。

entries.definition: A fall in amount or value; the most neutral word and does not carry the idea of heavy collapse.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或动词，义为「下降、下落」，最中性的词，不含沉重塌落的意思。

entries.definition: A very sharp fall, often sudden and steep, used of markets and shares.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或动词，义为「暴跌」，常指突然而陡峭的市场下挫。

entries.definition: A period of reduced economic activity, seen as a trend rather than one event.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「下滑、回落」，指经济活动减弱的一段时期，强调趋势。

entries.definition: A formal economic term for a fall in national output lasting more than a short period.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「经济衰退」，属正式的经济学术语，指国民产出持续下降。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real trading and posture phrases that slump appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用 slump 真实的商业与身体姿势搭配。

normal.en: A slump in sales is the most common noun phrase; the preposition in comes before the thing that fell.
normal.cn: a slump in sales 是最常见的名词搭配，介词 in 引出下跌的对象。

normal.en: Slump to a low and slump to a record high show how the verb takes targets.
normal.cn: slump to a low 与 slump to a record high 展示了动词如何接目标。

normal.en: Slump into a chair means sitting down as if all strength is gone.
normal.cn: slump into a chair 指像力气尽失般塌进椅子里。

normal.en: The Great Slump is British writing for the depression of the 1930s, much like the Great Depression.
normal.cn: the Great Slump 是英国文字里对二十世纪三十年代大萧条的称呼，类似 the Great Depression。

normal.en: Slump is chiefly a noun and a verb; as an adjective it is almost always slumping or slumped.
normal.cn: slump 主要作名词和动词；作形容词时几乎总是用 slumping 或 slumped 的形式。

abstract.en: Picture shoulders dropping an inch when the boss walks in.
abstract.cn: 想象老板走进来时，肩膀往下一沉。

abstract.en: Imagine a balloon losing air and sagging to the floor.
abstract.cn: 想象一只气球漏了气，慢慢塌到地上。

abstract.en: Think of a child dropping into a beanbag after a race.
abstract.cn: 想象孩子在赛跑之后一屁股陷进懒人沙发。

examples.en: Oil prices slumped to a five year low this week.
examples.cn: 本周油价跌至五年最低。

examples.en: He slumped onto the bed and fell asleep in his coat.
examples.cn: 他一下子塌到床上，穿着外套就睡着了。

examples.en: The slump hit small shops hardest.
examples.cn: 这场萧条对小型店铺的打击最重。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「斯兰普」听来像「塌啦扑」——肩一垮、价一塌，扑通往下坠；这只是读音联想，不是词源。

root: 来源不确定：一般认为是十七世纪英语从斯堪的纳维亚语借入，与挪威语、丹麦语中表示「跌落、偶发」的 slumpe 等词有关，原始义为沉重地下沉或滑落；没有可靠的拉丁语来源。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses all share one heavy downward motion: figures falling, an economy in decline, a market plunge, a body dropping into a seat, a roof sagging, a collapsed posture, a rarer causative use, a participle used as a label, and a sporting losing run.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项共享同一种沉重的下落：数字下降、经济行情下跌、市场急跌、身体塌进座位、屋顶塌陷、瘫倒的姿态、少见的使役用法、分词作定语，以及体育里的低迷期。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: shoulders dropping and a whole body sinking down, with a line on a chart sliding after it.
core.cn: 核心意象：肩膀一垮、整个人下沉，图表上一条线随之向下滑落。

branches.en: THE NUMBERS: figures and prices falling is the dominant economic sense.
branches.cn: 数字线：数字与价格下跌，是这个词最主要的经济义。

branches.en: THE PERIOD: a national slump and a team slump are both an extended run of poor results.
branches.cn: 时期线：全国性的萧条与球队的低迷，都是一段长时间的糟糕表现。

branches.en: THE BODY: sitting down heavily and lying in a collapsed heap are the physical core.
branches.cn: 身体线：重重坐下与瘫倒成一团，是这个词的身体核心。

branches.en: THE OBJECT: a roof or a shoulder that loses support sags in the same direction.
branches.cn: 物件线：失去支撑的屋顶或肩膀，朝着同一方向塌下去。

branches.en: THE FORMS: a rare causative verb and a participle used as a label extend the same drop grammatically.
branches.cn: 形式线：少见的使役动词与作定语的分词，把这个下坠在语法上延伸出去。

intro.en: Slump is Germanic in origin and English builds everything on it with -ed, -ing and -y; no Latin pieces are involved.
intro.cn: slump 源自日耳曼语系，英语只用 -ed、-ing、-y 在它上面构词，没有拉丁语部件。

latinIntro.en: The likely source is Scandinavian, not Latin, so the Latin list is left empty.
latinIntro.cn: 可能的来源是斯堪的纳维亚语而非拉丁语，因此拉丁同源词表留空。

items.meaning: to fall or happen by chance
items.example: The Scandinavian verb is the likely source.
items.exampleCN: 这个斯堪的纳维亚语动词很可能是来源。

items.example: The verb carries the physical drop.
items.exampleCN: 动词承载了身体性的下坠。

items.example: The noun extends the drop to trade.
items.exampleCN: 名词把下坠延伸到商业上。

items.example: The suffix -ed forms slumped.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ed 构成 slumped。

items.example: The suffix -ing forms slumping.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ing 构成 slumping。

items.example: The suffix -y forms slumpy.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -y 构成 slumpy。

items.example: Slumping before a noun names a trend.
items.exampleCN: 放于名词前的 slumping 表示趋势。

items.meaningCN: 二十世纪三十年代的大萧条
items.example: The proper name fixes the period in memory.
items.exampleCN: 这一专名把那段时期固定下来。

derivatives.zh: 由过去分词转为形容词，义为「瘫坐的、塌陷驼背的」
由现在分词转为形容词，义为「下滑中的、下跌的」
由本词加 -y 构成的少见形容词，义为「塌陷松软的」

definition_zh: 泥浆；稀浆；矿浆；饲料稀糊；（燃料与水泥的）悬浮浆
definition_en: a thick, wet mixture of a solid like powdered clay, cement or coal with water or another liquid
core_image: 一股灰褐色的稠泥沿斜坡缓缓流下，颗粒悬在液体里不沉
scene: 工地上，工人把石灰粉倒进搅拌机，又兑进水，机器转动后流出一大股灰色的稠泥。The workers poured a grey slurry into the moulds to form the concrete panels.
sceneCN: 这里 slurry 是「稀浆、泥浆」（第 1 个义项：固体粉末与水等液体混合成的稠浆）；句意为工人把灰色的泥浆倒进模具，用来浇铸混凝土板；画面里能看见搅拌机、水桶和模具。

pos.zh: 泥浆；稀浆；矿浆；（动物）饲料稀糊
把……制成稀浆；用稀浆涂抹或输送

derivatives.zh: 词根加 -like 构成，形容像稀浆一样稠而能流动的东西
由动词 slurried 转作形容词，意为已被制成稀浆或已浇上稀浆的

senses.title: A wet mixture of a solid and a liquid
senses.titleCN: 泥浆；稀浆（固体与水混合）
senses.definition: a thick mixture of water with powdered solid matter such as clay, chalk or cement, fluid enough to be pumped
senses.definitionCN: 水与黏土、白垩、水泥等粉末状固体混合成的稠浆，稠到成浆、又能被泵送
senses.example: The mason mixed sand and water into a smooth slurry.
senses.exampleCN: 砌匠把沙子和水调成均匀的稀浆。
senses.why: The oldest image is simply a wet paste: a solid loses its dry shape and becomes something that pours, but stays thick and opaque.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的画面就是一团湿糊：固体失去干燥的形状，变得可以倒出，却依旧稠厚、不透明。

senses.title: Liquid carrying ore or coal
senses.titleCN: 矿浆；煤泥（含矿物的悬浮液）
senses.definition: a suspension of finely crushed ore, coal or sand in water, moved through pipes in mining and power plants
senses.definitionCN: 磨细的矿石、煤或沙悬浮在水中形成的浆液，在矿山和电厂里用管道输送
senses.example: The plant pumps ore slurry through a pipe to the mill.
senses.exampleCN: 工厂用管道把矿浆泵送到选矿车间。
senses.why: Industry took the kitchen paste and made it flow: grinding the solid fine lets it hang in water, so it can be carried like a liquid.
senses.whyCN: 工业把这团糊搬到流水线上：固体磨得足够细，就能悬在水里，像液体一样被输送。

senses.title: Wet feed for farm animals
senses.definition: a thin, wet mash of grain meal left over from brewing or mixed for pigs, fed from a trough
senses.definitionCN: 酿造后剩下的稀麦糊，或专为猪等家畜调成的稀饲料，从食槽里喂食
senses.example: The farmer fed the pigs warm slurry from the still.
senses.exampleCN: 农场主把蒸馏器里温热的稀糊喂给猪。
senses.why: When brewing waste was kept instead of thrown away, the same thick liquid became animal feed: rich, wet and easily swallowed.
senses.whyCN: 酿酒的废稀糊被留下来喂养牲畜，这种稠液体于是变成饲料：有营养、湿软、好吞咽。

senses.title: Cement or clay suspended for use
senses.titleCN: 水泥浆；黏土浆（建筑用悬浮浆）
senses.definition: a runny suspension of cement, lime or fluidised clay used for grouting, tunnelling and fixing cracks in rock and soil
senses.definitionCN: 水泥、石灰或流态黏土悬浮而成的可流动浆液，用于灌浆、隧道施工以及封堵岩土裂缝
senses.example: Workers pumped cement slurry into the crack in the dam.
senses.exampleCN: 工人们把水泥浆泵进坝体的裂缝里。
senses.why: A slurry fills space the way water does but sets hard: poured into a gap, it takes the shape of the gap and then becomes solid.
senses.whyCN: 稀浆像水一样填满空隙，却能凝结变硬：灌进缝隙后先随缝成形，随后变成固体。

senses.title: A fuel or food suspension
senses.titleCN: 水煤浆等燃料浆；悬浮食品浆
senses.definition: a pumpable suspension of powdered coal, biomass or food solids in liquid, burnt or processed as one flowing stream
senses.definitionCN: 煤粉、生物质或食品固体悬浮在液体中的可泵送浆体，作为一股液流被燃烧或加工
senses.example: The boiler burns coal slurry instead of dry fuel.
senses.exampleCN: 这台锅炉烧的是水煤浆，而不是干燃料。
senses.why: Powder is awkward to handle but easy to suspend, so fuel and food makers turn dry solids into slurry to move them cheaply.
senses.whyCN: 粉末难以搬运却容易悬浮，因此燃料和食品行业把干固体做成浆体，以便廉价输送。

senses.title: Thin ice crystals in water
senses.definition: a flowing mixture of fine ice crystals and water, used to chill fish, produce and drinks quickly
senses.definitionCN: 细小冰晶与水混合而成的可流动浆体，用于快速冷却鱼、蔬果和饮料
senses.example: The fishmonger packed the catch in slurry ice.
senses.exampleCN: 鱼贩把渔获装在流化冰里保鲜。
senses.why: Ice ground fine enough melts into a slush that still flows and still chills: the slurry keeps the mixing image of solid and liquid.
senses.whyCN: 冰磨得足够细便化成仍能流动、仍能制冷的冰水浆，稀浆「固液混合」的画面在这里依旧成立。

senses.title: To turn a solid into a wet paste
senses.titleCN: 把……制成稀浆；以稀浆涂抹
senses.definition: to mix a solid such as food, clay or mineral powder with liquid until it becomes a slurry
senses.definitionCN: 把食物、黏土或矿粉等固体与液体混合，搅成稀浆状
senses.example: She slurried the flour and milk into a batter.
senses.exampleCN: 她把面粉和牛奶调成了面糊。
senses.why: The verb is the image in motion: take a dry solid, add liquid, and stir until the paste can flow.
senses.whyCN: 动词让画面动起来：拿一份干固体，兑入液体，搅到能流动为止。

senses.title: A liquid made thick and muddy
senses.titleCN: 浑浊的稠液；泥泞的混合液
senses.definition: a muddy or cloudy liquid in which suspended material makes it thick, opaque and hard to separate again
senses.definitionCN: 因悬浮物而变得稠厚、浑浊、难以再分离的泥泞液体
senses.example: After the storm the lane turned into a brown slurry.
senses.exampleCN: 暴雨过后，那条小路变成了一片褐色的泥沼泽。
senses.why: Stir water with mud or silt and you get the same texture outside the factory: the suspended solid turns clear water into a cloudy, heavy liquid.
senses.whyCN: 把泥或沙粒搅进清水，在工厂之外也能得到同样的质地：悬浮的固体让清水变成浑浊、沉重的液体。

intro.en: Slurry is first recorded in the fifteenth century as a local name for thin mud or wet mud, and English has used it ever since for wet solids that flow.
intro.cn: slurry 在十五世纪首次见诸记载，原指稀泥或湿泥，此后英语一直用它来表示能够流动的含固体的浆状物。

items.en: Schori, scurry and similar forms appear in the 1400s for wet, thin mud.
items.cn: 十五世纪出现 schori、scurry 等形式，指稀湿的泥。

items.en: Spellings shift freely between slory, slurrey and slurry.
items.cn: 拼写一度在 slory、slurrey、slurry 之间自由变动。

items.en: Slurry settles into its modern spelling for thin mud and slush.
items.cn: 到十八世纪，slurry 固定为现代拼写，指稀泥与泥水。

items.en: Brewing and farming extend it to wet mash and thin animal feed.
items.cn: 酿造业与农业把它扩展到湿麦糊和稀饲料。

items.en: Industry names any pumpable suspension of powder in water a slurry: cement, ore, coal and ice.
items.cn: 工业上把粉末悬浮于水中的可泵送浆体统称 slurry：水泥浆、矿浆、煤泥与冰浆。

items.en: The older form is often compared with Middle English sloor of similar meaning, though the exact link is uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为它与中古英语中意思相近的 sloor 有联系，但确切关系存疑。

note.en: Slurry belongs with slurry-like thick liquids such as pulp and grout, and with words that share its sl- beginning.
note.cn: slurry 与 pulp、grout 这类稠厚浆体同场，也和以 sl- 开头的词形式相近。

entries.definition: to speak indistinctly, or a slighting remark
entries.definitionCN: 含混不清地说话；含沙射影的话（只是拼写相近，词源不同）

entries.definition: to drink with a noisy sucking sound
entries.definitionCN: 大声吸着喝（只是拼写相近，词源不同）

entries.definition: thick soft mud or waste
entries.definitionCN: 稀泥；淤泥；污质（与 slurry 拼写相近，来源关系不确定）

entries.definition: a soft wet mass of crushed material
entries.definitionCN: 纸浆；果肉；软烂的湿泥状物

entries.definition: a thin mortar used to fill gaps and joints
partly melted snow or soft wet mixture

normalIntro.en: Slurry is a dry powder that has been wet enough to flow: the closer look at the letters sl- also ties it to slippery, sludgy things.
normalIntro.cn: slurry 是加足水就能流动的干粉；开头的 sl- 也让它和滑溜、泥泞有关联。

normal.en: Slurries is the plural, and the verb forms are slurried and slurrying.
normal.cn: 复数是 slurries，动词形式为 slurried 与 slurrying。

normal.en: A slurry pump moves thick mixtures that an ordinary water pump cannot handle.
normal.cn: slurry pump 用来输送普通水泵无法应付的稠浆。

normal.en: In mining, ore is ground fine and carried as slurry through pipes.
normal.cn: 矿业中把矿石磨细后，以矿浆形式用管道输送。

normal.en: Cement slurry is poured into cracks and gaps to set hard.
normal.cn: 水泥浆灌入裂缝和空隙，随后凝结变硬。

normal.en: Compare sludge: sludge is unwanted wet waste, while slurry is usually a mixture made for use.
normal.cn: 对比 sludge：sludge 是废弃的湿污物，slurry 通常是特意调制的浆体。

abstract.en: Picture grey mud sliding down a ramp, thick but still moving.
abstract.cn: 想象灰色的泥浆顺着斜坡流下，稠厚却仍在流动。

abstract.en: Picture a pipe carrying orange ore water toward a mill.
abstract.cn: 想象一根管道把橙色的矿浆运往选矿厂。

abstract.en: Picture a trough of warm, wet mash while pigs push in to eat.
abstract.cn: 想象食槽里温热的稀糊，猪群挤着来吃。

examples.en: The builder mixed a slurry of lime and sand for the old wall.
examples.cn: 泥瓦匠为这面老墙调了石灰与沙子的浆。

examples.en: Mine water carries fine slurry to the settling ponds.
examples.cn: 矿水把细矿浆带到了沉淀池。

examples.en: Early each morning the pigs were fed a warm slurry.
examples.cn: 每天清早，猪群都会得到一份温热的稀糊饲料。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「死拉里」——调得太稠、死劲拉也拉不动的泥浆；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 来源不确定：最早见于十五世纪，写作 schori、scurry 等形式，指稀泥、湿泥；一般认为与中古英语中表稀泥的 sloor 有联系，但确切词源未能确定。十八世纪后固定为 slurry，十九世纪扩展为饲料稀糊，二十世纪成为工业用语。

sensesIntro.en: Slurry starts as wet mud, grows into any solid suspended in liquid, and is finally named for its texture rather than its purpose.
sensesIntro.cn: slurry 从湿泥起步，扩展为任何悬浮于液体中的固体，最后又回到以质地而非用途命名的稠浊液体。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: grey mud that is thick enough to hold its shape for a moment, yet fluid enough to pour.
core.cn: 核心意象：灰泥稠到能短暂保住形状，却又稀到可以倒出。

branches.en: THE PASTE: the basic wet mixture of powder and water, for building or food.
branches.cn: 糊浆线：粉末与水混合的基本形态，用于建筑或食物。

branches.en: THE PIPELINE: ore, cement and coal are ground fine and carried through pipes as slurry.
branches.cn: 管道线：矿石、水泥与煤被磨细，以泥浆形式经管道输送。

branches.en: THE TROUGH: brewing waste turned into wet feed for animals.
branches.cn: 食槽线：酿酒的废料变成喂养牲畜的湿饲料。

branches.en: THE COLD LINE: fine ice in water gives a slurry that chills food without damaging it.
branches.cn: 低温线：水中的细冰构成稀冰浆，可在不损伤食材的情况下快速冷却。

branches.en: THE ACT AND THE MESS: the verb stirs a solid into paste, and stirred-up water becomes muddy slurry again.
branches.cn: 动作与浑浊线：动词把固体搅成浆，搅浑的清水又变回浑浊的泥浆。

intro.en: Slurry has no clear Latin family; its word-building rests on the English plural and -ed forms and on compounds such as slurry pump.
intro.cn: slurry 没有明确的拉丁语词族，它的构词依靠英语复数、-ed 形式以及 slurry pump 一类复合词。

latinIntro.en: There is no reliable Latin ancestor of slurry, so the source is left open and no Latin entries are listed.
latinIntro.cn: slurry 没有可靠的拉丁语源头，因此不列拉丁同源词。

items.meaning: a thick wet mixture of solid and liquid
items.meaningCN: 固体与液体混合的稠浆
items.example: Slurry is the base word of the family.
items.exampleCN: slurry 是这个词族的基词。

items.example: The plant handles two slurries at once.
items.exampleCN: 这家工厂同时处理两种泥浆。

items.example: They slurried the powder before pumping it.
items.exampleCN: 他们先把粉料调成浆，再泵送出去。

items.meaning: the act of making a slurry
items.example: Slurrying takes steady stirring.
items.exampleCN: 调浆需要持续搅拌。

items.meaning: a pump built for thick mixtures
items.example: A slurry pump handles grit without jamming.
items.exampleCN: 泥浆泵能应付砂粒而不卡住。

items.meaning: a clay-based barrier built in a filled trench
items.example: The tunnel was sealed with a slurry wall.
items.exampleCN: 隧道用泥浆墙封了起来。

items.meaning: a flowing mix of fine ice and water
items.example: Slurry ice cools fish faster than crushed ice.
items.exampleCN: 流化冰比碎冰更快冷却鱼货。

items.example: Coal slurry is burnt as a liquid fuel.
items.exampleCN: 煤泥像液体一样被燃烧。

items.meaning: forming nouns of texture and state
items.meaningCN: 构成表质地与状态的名词词尾
items.example: The final -y belongs to the old noun form itself.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -y 属于这一古名词形式本身。

definition_zh: 邋遢的；不整洁的；衣着随便的；（旧时）举止轻浮的
definition_en: untidy, dirty and careless in dress or habits, or, in older use, of loose morals
core_image: 一间久未收拾的屋子：碗碟堆在水池，衣服散落一地
scene: 客人突然上门，屋主慌忙把堆在水池里的碗塞进柜子，沙发上还堆着没叠的衣服。The landlord was shocked by the sluttish kitchen left by the previous tenants.
sceneCN: 这里 sluttish 是「邋遢的、不整洁的」（第 1 个义项：房间杂乱、疏于整理）；句意为房东被前租客留下的邋遢厨房惊呆了；画面里能看见水池里的碗碟、地上的衣服和灰尘。

pos.zh: 邋遢的；不整洁的；衣着不整的；（旧时）轻浮的
以 sluttishly 的形式表「邋遢地」

derivatives.zh: -ish + -ness 构成，义为「邋遢、不整洁」
形容词去 -ish 后回到的原名词，旧义为邋遢的人
不同词根，但义场相同，指邋遢、懒散

senses.title: Untidy and unclean in a room or place
senses.definition: dirty and untidy, so that a room looks neglected and badly cared for
senses.definitionCN: 又脏又乱，使房间显得被忽视、缺乏照料
senses.example: They refused to rent the flat after seeing the sluttish kitchen.
senses.exampleCN: 看到那间邋遢的厨房后，他们拒绝租下这套公寓。
senses.why: The old noun slut meant a dirty or slovenly person, so a place that looks like that person lives there takes the same adjective.
senses.whyCN: 古英语名词 slut 指邋遢懒散的人，于是「像是这种人住过的地方」也用同一个形容词来形容。

senses.title: Careless in dress and habits
senses.definition: dressing carelessly or living with little order, so that clothes and habits look neglected
senses.definitionCN: 穿戴随意、生活缺乏条理，衣服与习惯显得被忽视
senses.example: He grew sluttish after months of working from home.
senses.exampleCN: 在家办公几个月后，他变得不修边幅。
senses.why: Applied to people, the word keeps the older sense of a careless keeper of one own things: clothes left on the floor, meals skipped, hair unbrushed.
senses.whyCN: 用来形容人时，它保留旧义「不爱惜自己东西的人」：衣服扔在地上，饭也糊弄，头发不梳。

senses.title: Of loose morals, in older use
senses.definition: in older texts, describing a woman as sexually loose or forward, now considered very offensive
senses.definitionCN: 旧时文本中形容女子举止轻浮、行为放荡，如今被视为极具冒犯性
senses.example: The novel uses sluttish only for its comic servant characters.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说只用 sluttish 形容滑稽的仆役角色。
senses.why: The same root already carried the idea of a disorderly person, and by the late Middle Ages moral or sexual disorder was added to the dirt and mess.
senses.whyCN: 这个词根本已含「不守秩序的人」，到中古英语晚期，又在这个「脏乱」之上叠加了道德或性的放荡。

senses.title: Shabby and poorly made
senses.definition: of clothes, furniture or work, badly finished, stained or put together with little care
senses.definitionCN: 形容衣物、家具或活儿做得粗糙、有污渍、毫无用心
senses.example: The stitching on the coat was tight and sluttish.
senses.exampleCN: 这件外套的针脚又紧又潦草。
senses.why: Untidiness passes from the person to the person output: what is made without care looks as neglected as a dirty room.
senses.whyCN: 邋遢从人传到人的出品上：不用心做出来的东西，看上去和脏屋子一样被忽视。

senses.title: Neglected and untended
senses.titleCN: （庭院、地方）无人打理的；荒疏的
senses.definition: of a garden, yard or building, left with weeds, litter or repairs undone until it looks worn out
senses.definitionCN: 形容花园、院子或建筑杂草丛生、垃圾遍地、该修的没修，显得破败
senses.example: The sluttish garden had not been weeded all summer.
senses.exampleCN: 那个无人打理的花园整个夏天都没除过草。
senses.why: This narrows the first sense to neglect over time: not a single messy evening, but weeks of no one bothering.
senses.whyCN: 这是第一个义项在时间上的延伸：不是一时弄乱，而是好几个星期都没人管。

senses.title: Sloppy in speech or manners
senses.definition: careless and without polish in what one says or how one behaves, as if rules did not matter
senses.definitionCN: 说话做事马虎、不加修饰，仿佛规矩都无所谓
senses.example: His sluttish remarks upset the whole family.
senses.exampleCN: 他那些随随便便的话惹恼了全家人。
senses.why: Once the word means careless, it can leave the body and the room behind and describe careless words and careless manners too.
senses.whyCN: 一旦词义只是「不上心」，它就可以离开身体与房间，去形容随便说的话和散漫的举止。

senses.title: In literary description of weather or landscape
senses.definition: in older descriptive prose, wet, muddy and disorderly, as with sleet, puddles and dripping eaves
senses.definitionCN: 旧时描写性文字中形容潮湿、泥泞而杂乱，如雨雪、水洼与滴水的屋檐
senses.example: A sluttish wind blew sleet against the shutters.
senses.exampleCN: 一阵凌乱的风夹着雨雪打在百叶窗上。
senses.why: The adjective is a picture of disorder, and a muddy wet day is disorder written on the whole landscape rather than on one room.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词本是一幅「乱」的画面，而风雨泥泞的一天正是把这种乱写满整片风景，而不只是写在一间屋子里。

senses.title: Used as a disparaging word for a woman
senses.titleCN: （贬义）对女子的侮辱性称呼用法
senses.definition: the adjective used to insult a woman by suggesting she is dirty, lazy or of loose morals, and now best avoided
senses.definitionCN: 用这个形容词侮辱女性，暗示她脏、懒或放荡，现代用语中最好避免
senses.example: Editors now avoid sluttish where a neutral word would do.
senses.exampleCN: 编辑如今会用中性的词，而避开 sluttish。
senses.why: The old moral sense of the noun was almost entirely pinned on women, and the adjective inherited that slant along with the older dirt meaning.
senses.whyCN: 名词的旧道德义几乎全扣在女性身上，形容词继承了这种偏向，也继承了旧有的「脏」义。

intro.en: Sluttish is the Middle English noun slut, a dirty or slovenly person, with the suffix -ish meaning of the kind of.
intro.cn: sluttish 由中古英语名词 slut（邋遢、懒散的人）加上后缀 -ish（具有……性质的）构成。

items.en: Slut is recorded from around 1400 in the sense of a dirty, untidy person.
items.cn: slut 约自十四世纪见于记载，义为肮脏、邋遢的人。

items.en: Slut is still used for a kitchen maid or a slovenly man.
items.cn: 中古英语中 slut 仍指厨房女仆或不修边幅的人。

items.en: A moral sense of loose conduct grows, and sluttish follows it as an adjective.
items.cn: 十六至十七世纪，指放荡的道德义渐生，sluttish 作为形容词随之出现。

items.en: Sluttish is used for dirty rooms, shabby clothes and neglected gardens.
items.cn: 十七世纪，sluttish 用于形容脏乱的房间、破旧的衣服和无人打理的花园。

items.en: The noun slut narrows sharply to an offensive insult, while the adjective survives chiefly in literary and old-fashioned use.
items.cn: 现代英语中名词 slut 大幅窄化为侮辱语，形容词则主要残存于文学与旧式用法中。

note.en: Sluttish sits with words for dirt and neglect such as slovenly and untidy, and looks like the noun slut from which it grew.
note.cn: sluttish 与 slovenly、untidy 等表示脏乱的词同场，外形上则明显连着它的来源名词 slut。

entries.definition: an untidy person, or, offensively, a woman of loose morals
entries.definitionCN: 邋遢的人；侮辱语中指放荡的女人

entries.definition: the quality of being untidy or careless
dirty and untidy, especially of a woman or a home
entries.definitionCN: 邋遢的、懒散的（由 slattern 派生，与 slut 只是形义相近，词源不同）

entries.definition: careless and untidy in dress or habits
not neat or well arranged
dirty and unpleasant, often through neglect
entries.definitionCN: 肮脏的；污秽的（多因疏于打理）

normalIntro.en: Sluttish is slutt plus ish: the old noun for a careless, dirty person, wearing the suffix of having that nature.
normalIntro.cn: sluttish 是 slutt 加 ish：一个古名词表「邋遢的人」，再戴上表「具有……性质」的后缀。

normal.en: The noun is slut, the adjective is sluttish and the abstract noun is sluttishness.
normal.cn: 名词是 slut，形容词是 sluttish，抽象名词是 sluttishness。

normal.en: The suffix -ish means having the qualities of, as in childish and foolish.
normal.cn: 后缀 -ish 表示「具有……性质」，如 childish 与 foolish。

normal.en: Use it for places and habits: a sluttish kitchen, sluttish housekeeping.
normal.cn: 它常修饰地方与习惯：a sluttish kitchen、sluttish housekeeping。

normal.en: Compare sluttish and slovenly: both mean untidy, but slovenly is still neutral today.
normal.cn: 对比 sluttish 与 slovenly：两者都表示邋遢，但 slovenly 今天仍是中性词。

normal.en: The modern noun has become a very offensive insult, so in speech use untidy or slovenly instead.
normal.cn: 现代名词已变成极具冒犯性的侮辱语，口语中应改用 untidy 或 slovenly。

abstract.en: Picture unwashed dishes rising in the sink and clothes on the floor.
abstract.cn: 想象水池里堆起没洗的碗碟，地上散落着衣服。

abstract.en: Picture someone going out in a stained shirt with uncombed hair.
abstract.cn: 想象有人穿着带污渍的衬衫、头发也没梳就出门。

abstract.en: Picture an old novel where a maid is called sluttish by a sneering master.
abstract.cn: 想象一本旧小说里，主人在讥讽地称女仆 sluttish。

examples.en: Guests often remark on the sluttish state of the shared kitchen.
examples.cn: 客人常提起公用厨房那副邋遢模样。

examples.en: The more sluttish his habits became, the less he noticed the mess.
examples.cn: 他的生活习惯越邋遢，就越注意不到屋里的乱。

examples.en: Victorian writers sometimes used sluttish where a modern editor would write untidy.
examples.cn: 维多利亚时期的作家有时用 sluttish，而现代编辑会写 untidy。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「斯拉提什」——斯拉提什先生回家从不收拾，袜子到处扔；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 中古英语 slut（约十四世纪，邋遢懒散的人）+ 古英语后缀 -isc（现代 -ish，「具有……性质的」）→ sluttish。词根 slut 的更深来源不确定；道德义约在十六至十七世纪附加其上。

sensesIntro.en: Sluttish begins with a dirty, untidy person and spreads outward to rooms, clothes, work, habits and even weather, while the older moral sense now survives only in reading.
sensesIntro.cn: sluttish 从「邋遢的人」出发，扩展到房间、衣物、手工、习惯甚至天气，而旧的道德义今天只残留在阅读中。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sink full of unwashed dishes and clothes left where they fell.
core.cn: 核心意象：水池堆满没洗的碗碟，衣服丢在掉下来的地方。

branches.en: THE PLACE: a room or garden where no one has tidied for a long time.
branches.cn: 场所线：很久没人整理的房间或花园。

branches.en: THE PERSON: careless dress and careless daily habits.
branches.cn: 人物线：穿着随意、日常习惯马虎。

branches.en: THE MORAL SLANT: a very offensive old judgement aimed at women.
branches.cn: 道德偏向线：一种极具冒犯性的旧式评判，主要指向女性。

branches.en: THE WORK AND THE WORDS: shabby things and careless speech share the same lack of care.
branches.cn: 手工与言词线：粗劣的物件与散漫的言语都源于同样的不上心。

branches.en: THE WEATHER: wet, muddy disorder written across the landscape.
branches.cn: 天气线：潮湿泥泞的混乱铺满整片风景。

intro.en: Sluttish is built in English from an old native noun and a native suffix, not from Latin.
intro.cn: sluttish 由英语本土的古老名词与本土后缀构成，并非来自拉丁语。

latinIntro.en: The base slut has no reliable Latin equivalent, so no Latin entries are listed for this family.
latinIntro.cn: 词根 slut 没有可靠的拉丁语对应词，因此不列拉丁同源词。

items.example: Slut is the base noun of the family.
items.exampleCN: slut 是这个词族的基词。

items.example: The suffix -ish turns the noun into an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ish 把名词变成形容词。

items.example: Sluttish describes places and habits.
items.exampleCN: sluttish 形容地方与习惯。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms the adverb sluttishly.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 构成副词 sluttishly。

items.example: He left the room sluttishly uncleaned.
items.exampleCN: 他邋里邋遢地没把房间收拾干净。

items.example: The suffix -ness forms sluttishness.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ness 构成 sluttishness。

items.example: Sluttishness was the only charge against him.
items.exampleCN: 人们对他唯一的指责就是邋遢。

items.meaningCN: 现代侮辱语，使用时须非常谨慎
items.example: The modern noun is rarely printed without comment.
items.exampleCN: 现代名词很少在无说明的情况下印出。

items.example: Slovenly comes from a different root and stays neutral.
items.exampleCN: slovenly 来自另一词根，语义仍属中性。

definition_zh: 天花（一种烈性传染病）
definition_en: a severe and often deadly disease caused by the variola virus, marked by fever and a rash of pocks
core_image: 皮肤上密布的脓疱，病退后留下一个个凹陷小坑
scene: 旧时城镇里，同一户人家的几个孩子接连发烧，起初像普通感冒，随后脸上和身上冒出成片的红斑与水疱。By the time the doctor arrived, the boy was covered in the first spots of smallpox.
sceneCN: 这里 smallpox 是「天花」（第 1 个义项：由天花病毒引起的烈性传染病）；句意为医生赶到时，男孩身上已布满天花初起的斑点；画面里能看见病床、诊包和成片的红疹。

pos.zh: 天花的；天花疫苗的（作定语，如 smallpox vaccination）

forms.label: 不可数病名，一般不用复数

derivatives.zh: smallpox + -ed 构成，意为「长满天花痘疤的」（较少用）
与词根 pock 同源，指脓疱与痘疤，也是 cowpox、chickenpox 的词尾
pock + marked 构成，形容脸上留有凹陷的痘疤

senses.title: The disease caused by variola virus
senses.titleCN: 天花（由天花病毒引起的烈性传染病）
senses.definition: a highly infectious human disease caused by the variola virus, with high fever and a rash that turns into pus-filled pocks
senses.definitionCN: 由天花病毒引起的高度传染性人类疾病，表现为高热和最终变成脓疱的皮疹
senses.example: Vaccination wiped out the disease once known as smallpox.
senses.exampleCN: 接种疫苗消灭了曾被称为天花的这种疾病。
senses.why: Pock means a bump on the skin, and small marks it as less deadly than the great pox: the name is the pocks, and their size marks which disease is meant.
senses.whyCN: pock 意为皮肤上的凸起，small 则把它与更致命的大痘区分开：名字说的就是「痘」，而「小」标明了是哪种痘。

senses.title: The rash stage with pocks
senses.definition: the stage of illness when the fever drops and the pocks appear on the face, chest and arms, later leaving scars
senses.definitionCN: 发热消退、痘疹在面部、胸部和手臂出现的阶段，痘退后留下疤痕
senses.example: The pocks of smallpox left deep scars on her face.
senses.exampleCN: 天花痘疹在她的脸上留下了深疤。
senses.why: The skin is where the name lives: pocks are what you see, so smallpox can also name the visible rash itself in descriptions of an illness.
senses.whyCN: 名字正落在皮肤上：痘是看得见的，因此在病情描述里，smallpox 也可以指冒出体表的这些痘本身。

senses.title: The smallpox epidemic as a historical force
senses.titleCN: （历史上的）天花疫情；天花大流行
senses.definition: outbreaks of the disease seen as social events, which killed rulers, emptied towns and changed the course of wars and colonies
senses.definitionCN: 把这种病的暴发视为社会事件：它夺走君主的性命、让城镇空无一人，也改写战争与殖民地的走向
senses.example: Smallpox decided the fate of kings as surely as armies did.
senses.exampleCN: 天花像军队一样决定过国王的命运。
senses.why: A disease that kills millions stops being only a medical term and becomes a chapter of history, so the uncountable name turns into an event.
senses.whyCN: 一种能杀死数百万人的疾病已不只是医学术语，而成为历史的一章，因此这个不可数的病名可以指向一场事件。

senses.title: The virus behind the disease
senses.definition: in looser medical writing, the variola virus itself, as in the last stocks of smallpox kept in laboratories
senses.definitionCN: 在较宽松的医学写作中直接指天花病毒本身，如实验室保存的最后一批毒株
senses.example: The last frozen smallpox sits in two high-security labs.
senses.exampleCN: 最后一批冷冻保存的天花病毒存放在两间高度戒备的实验室里。
senses.why: The disease name gets transferred to its cause, as with many illnesses, so the word can point to a laboratory sample.
senses.whyCN: 病名常被转指病因，这在许多疾病上都发生，于是这个词也能指实验室里的毒株。

senses.title: A scarred face as a legacy
senses.titleCN: 天花痘疤；用病名代指满脸痘痕（旧）
senses.definition: in older writing, the marks left by the disease, and thus a pockmarked face described by the illness that caused it
senses.definitionCN: 旧时文字中指甲病留下的印记，因而也用病名直接形容一张长满痘疤的脸
senses.example: The old portrait shows a queen whose face bears smallpox.
senses.exampleCN: 那幅旧画像里，女王脸上带着天花痘痕。
senses.why: If the pocks are the disease, the marks left on a body can name the illness too: the scar tells which fever came.
senses.whyCN: 既然痘就是这种病，留在身上的印痕也可以指病名本身：看疤痕就知道是哪场高烧来过。

senses.title: A byword for an eliminated scourge
senses.titleCN: （喻）已被根除的最大祸害；瘟疫的代名词
senses.definition: used figuratively for something terrible and widespread that has at last been wiped out, as in the smallpox of an old evil
senses.definitionCN: 喻指曾经横行、终于被清除的巨大祸害，如某种旧恶的「天花」
senses.example: Some writers hope poverty will one day follow smallpox.
senses.exampleCN: 有些作家希望贫穷有朝一日也步天花后尘而消失。
senses.why: Smallpox is the first human disease ever wiped out, so its name has become a symbol of a victory over a scourge.
senses.whyCN: 天花是人类第一个被彻底消灭的疾病，它的名字因此成了「战胜大祸」的象征。

senses.title: An archaic spelling, small-pox
senses.titleCN: 旧拼写 small-pox 对应写法
senses.definition: the older hyphenated spelling small-pox, kept in old books and quoted in historical writing today
senses.definitionCN: 旧有的带连字符拼写 small-pox，见于旧书，如今多在历史写作中引用
senses.example: The diary spells it small-pox with a hyphen.
senses.exampleCN: 那本日记把它拼作带连字符的 small-pox。
senses.why: Earlier English often joined two-word names with a hyphen before they fused, so the hyphen is a fossil of an older writing habit.
senses.whyCN: 早期英语中，由两词组成的名称融合前常用连字符连接，所以这个连字符是旧书写习惯留下的化石。

intro.en: Smallpox is small plus pock, the English word for a skin bump, and it was coined to set this disease apart from the far deadlier great pox.
intro.cn: smallpox 由 small 与 pock（皮肤上的凸起）构成，造词是为了把这种病与远为致命的「大痘」区分开。

items.en: Pocc, related to Dutch and German forms, names a pustule or skin bump.
items.cn: 古英语 pocc 与荷兰语、德语中的形式相关，指脓疱或皮肤凸起。

items.en: The pox comes to mean syphilis, known then as the great pox.
items.cn: pox 在十五、十六世纪逐渐指梅毒，当时称作大痘。

items.en: Small pockes names variola to contrast with the great pox.
items.cn: small pockes 这一说法用于指天花，以与大痘相对。

items.en: The two words fuse into the single spelling smallpox.
items.cn: 两个词融合为一个写法 smallpox。

items.en: Smallpox is officially declared eradicated in 1980, the first human disease wiped out worldwide.
items.cn: 一九八零年天花被正式宣布根除，成为首个在全球被消灭的人类疾病。

note.en: Smallpox belongs with other pox diseases and their vaccines, and looks like a set of small- compounds built on the same word.
note.cn: smallpox 与各类「痘」病及疫苗同场，外形上也像一族以同一个词为词尾的 small 复合词。

entries.definition: weak beer, or figuratively something trivial
entries.definitionCN: 淡啤酒；引申为无足轻重的事（与 smallpox 只是 same first word，意义无关）

entries.definition: light conversation about unimportant matters
entries.definitionCN: 闲聊；寒暄（只是拼写相近，词源不同）

entries.definition: a pustule or the scar it leaves
entries.definitionCN: 脓疱；痘疤（与 smallpox 同根）

entries.definition: a mild disease of cattle used to make the smallpox vaccine
entries.definitionCN: 牛痘（一种牛类轻症，用于制造天花疫苗）

entries.definition: a mild infectious disease with a blistering rash, unrelated to smallpox
entries.definitionCN: 水痘（一种轻症痘病，与天花无关）

entries.definition: a bacterial disease once called the great pox
entries.definitionCN: 梅毒（旧时称作 the great pox）

normalIntro.en: Smallpox is literally the small pox: the little pocks on the skin, named against the great pox.
normalIntro.cn: smallpox 字面就是「小痘」：皮肤上的小脓疱，是相对于「大痘」而得名。

normal.en: Pock means a bump on the skin, the same word seen in cowpox and chickenpox.
normal.cn: pock 意为皮肤上的凸起，cowpox 与 chickenpox 中也是这个词。

normal.en: Smallpox is an uncountable name, so it takes a singular verb and no article in most use.
normal.cn: smallpox 是不可数病名，多数情况下配单数动词、不用冠词。

normal.en: Cowpox was the mild disease that made the first smallpox vaccine possible.
normal.cn: 牛痘是制成第一支天花疫苗的轻症疾病。

normal.en: The World Health Organization declared smallpox eradicated in 1980.
normal.cn: 世界卫生组织于一九八零年宣布天花已被消灭。

normal.en: In writing, use pockmarked for a scarred face and keep smallpox for the disease itself.
normal.cn: 写作时，形容痘疤遍布的脸用 pockmarked，smallpox 仍指这种病本身。

abstract.en: Picture rows of raised red pocks across a sick child cheeks and chest.
abstract.cn: 想象生病孩子脸颊与胸口布满成排的红色痘疱。

abstract.en: Picture an old photo of a face with deep pock scars after the fever.
abstract.cn: 想象一张旧照片，脸上是高烧之后留下的深深痘疤。

abstract.en: Picture a map where one town after another goes dark during an outbreak.
abstract.cn: 想象疫情中一座又一座市镇在地图上变暗。

examples.en: Smallpox killed more people than many wars of the same era.
examples.cn: 在同年代，死于天花的人比许多战争造成的还多。

examples.en: The campaign to vaccinate against smallpox lasted more than a century.
examples.cn: 为对抗天花而接种疫苗的运动持续了一百多年。

examples.en: Historians still debate how much smallpox reshaped colonial settlements.
examples.cn: 历史学家至今仍在争论天花在多大程度上改变了殖民定居点。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「死猫扑克」——死猫抱着扑克牌，脸上身上全是小痘印；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: small + pox：古英语 pocc（脓疱、皮肤凸起，与荷兰语、德语同族）→ 中古英语 pox 转指梅毒，俗称 the great pox → 十六世纪以 small pockes 与「大痘」相对，指天花 → 十七世纪合写为 smallpox。pocc 的更深词源存疑。

sensesIntro.en: Smallpox names the disease first, then its rash, then the historical disaster, the virus, the scars, and finally any scourge that has been wiped out.
sensesIntro.cn: smallpox 先指这种病，再指它的痘疹，继而指历史上的惨祸、病毒、疤痕，最后泛指被彻底消灭的祸害。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a body covered in raised pus-filled pocks that leave deep pits when they heal.
core.cn: 核心意象：身体布满凸起的脓疱，病愈后留下深坑。

branches.en: THE ILLNESS: the variola infection named for its small pocks.
branches.cn: 疾病线：以「小痘」命名的天花感染。

branches.en: THE SKIN: the rash itself and the scars it leaves behind.
branches.cn: 皮肤线：痘疹本身以及它留下的疤痕。

branches.en: THE HISTORY: epidemics that changed the world, and the first disease ever wiped out.
branches.cn: 历史线：改写世界的天花疫情，以及首个被彻底消灭的疾病。

branches.en: THE CAUSE: the virus kept in laboratories after the disease vanished.
branches.cn: 病因线：疾病消失后仍保存在实验室里的病毒。

branches.en: THE SPELLING: the hyphenated old form that survives in old texts.
branches.cn: 拼写线：旧文本中带连字符的旧写法。

intro.en: Smallpox is a plain English compound of small and pock, with pock the real building block shared by cowpox and chickenpox.
intro.cn: smallpox 是 small 与 pock 构成的普通英语复合词，真正的构词单位是 pock，它与 cowpox、chickenpox 共用。

latinIntro.en: The word is native English, but pock has no reliable Latin ancestor, so no Latin entries are listed.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词是英语本族词，pock 也没有可靠的拉丁语源头，因此不列拉丁同源词。

items.example: Small marks which disease is meant, not its severity.
items.exampleCN: small 标明所指的是哪种病，而非轻重。

items.example: Pock is the heart of the compound.
items.exampleCN: pock 是这个复合词的核心。

items.example: The pox once meant syphilis.
items.exampleCN: pox 曾指梅毒。

items.example: Smallpox was declared eradicated in 1980.
items.exampleCN: 天花于一九八零年被宣布消灭。

items.meaning: the same word before it was fused
items.example: Old letters write small-pox with a hyphen.
items.exampleCN: 旧信件把 small-pox 写作带连字符的形式。

items.example: The suffix -ed gives smallpoxed.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ed 构成 smallpoxed。

items.example: Smallpoxed is rare but recorded.
items.exampleCN: smallpoxed 少见但有记载。

items.example: Pockmarked builds on the same pock.
items.exampleCN: pockmarked 同样由 pock 构成。

items.example: Cowpox supplied the first vaccine.
items.exampleCN: 牛痘提供了第一支疫苗。

items.example: Chickenpox is unrelated to smallpox.
items.exampleCN: 水痘与天花无关。

items.meaning: the act of giving a vaccine
items.example: The word vaccination comes from Latin vacca, a cow.
items.exampleCN: vaccination 来自拉丁语 vacca，意为牛。

latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语 vacca 带来了 vaccine 一词。

latinEntries.example: Varius is behind the virus name variola.
latinEntries.exampleCN: varius 是病毒名 variola 的来源。

definition_zh: 涂抹；弄脏；诽谤；污点
definition_en: to spread a thick substance over a surface, or to damage a person or group with false claims
core_image: 手指把一层黏稠的东西抹在玻璃上，留下模糊一片
scene: 孩子吃完果酱，随手在餐巾纸上抹了一把。After the jam, the child smeared a sticky line across the paper napkin.
sceneCN: 这里 smear 是「涂抹、抹上」（第 1 个义项：把黏稠物抹在表面）；句意：吃完果酱后，孩子在一张餐巾纸上抹出一道黏糊糊的痕迹。

collocations.zh: 被污名化；被贴上污点证据

derivatives.zh: smear 加施事后缀 -er，指涂抹东西的人或说人坏话的人
smear 加形容词后缀 -y，义为「黏糊糊的；易抹开的」
be-（使）+ smear，义为「涂抹；弄脏」，偏书面
现在分词转名词，指涂抹动作或抹黑行为

senses.title: To spread a thick substance on a surface
senses.definition: to put a thick, soft, or sticky substance on a surface and spread it roughly
senses.definitionCN: 把黏稠、柔软或发黏的东西抹在表面上并大致摊开
senses.example: She smeared butter on the warm bread.
senses.exampleCN: 她把黄油抹在温热的面包上。
senses.why: The oldest English use is to coat or anoint with oil, and the core image is a hand rubbing a sticky layer over something.
senses.whyCN: 英语最早的用法是涂油、敷油，核心意象就是手把黏稠的一层东西搓抹到别的东西上，所以「涂抹」是词义的原点。

senses.title: To make something dirty with a mark
senses.definition: to leave a dirty or greasy mark on something by touching or rubbing it
senses.definitionCN: 因触碰或摩擦而在某物上留下脏污或油腻的痕迹
senses.example: The boys smeared mud all over the kitchen floor.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们把厨房地板弄得满是泥巴。
senses.why: Once the spreading act lands on an unwanted surface, the effect is a dirty mark, so the verb shifts from coating to staining.
senses.whyCN: 当涂抹动作落在不该弄脏的地方，结果就是一道脏痕，于是动词从「敷上」滑向「弄脏」，同一条动作链换了个视角。

senses.title: To damage a reputation with false claims
senses.definition: to damage the reputation of a person or group by spreading false or unfair statements
senses.definitionCN: 散布虚假或不公平的说法，损害某人或某群体的名誉
senses.example: Critics accused the paper of smearing the young scientist.
senses.exampleCN: 批评者指责这家报纸抹黑那位年轻科学家。
senses.why: A smear on a clean surface is a stain that will not wipe off easily, so attacking someone reputation became a verbal smear.
senses.whyCN: 干净表面上的污渍不易擦掉，名誉被攻击也像被抹上一层洗不掉的脏东西，因此「口头涂抹」引申为诽谤抹黑。

senses.title: A mark of grease or dirt
senses.definition: a dirty or greasy mark left on a surface, especially glass
senses.definitionCN: 留在表面上、尤指玻璃上的油污或脏痕
senses.example: There was a smear of lipstick on the glass.
senses.exampleCN: 玻璃杯上有一道口红印。
senses.why: The noun simply names the trace left behind once the spreading hand has moved away, making the action into a visible object.
senses.whyCN: 手抹过之后留下的痕迹就是名称本身，动作结束变成了可看见的具体物体，于是动词用法分出名词「污迹」。

senses.title: A sample spread on a slide
senses.definition: a thin layer of a substance or cell sample spread on a glass slide for examination
senses.definitionCN: 涂在玻璃载玻片上供检查的薄层物质或细胞样本
senses.example: The nurse took a cervical smear during the checkup.
senses.exampleCN: 护士在体检时取了宫颈涂片。
senses.why: Laboratory work uses the same physical act, spreading cells thinly on glass, so the technical noun grew directly from the literal spreading sense.
senses.whyCN: 实验室把细胞薄薄地抹在玻璃片上，动作与日常涂抹完全相同，因此医学中的「涂片」直接从「抹开」这一具体义发展出来。

intro.en: Smear comes from Old English smierwan, to anoint or coat with grease, from a Germanic root meaning fat or grease.
intro.cn: smear 源自中古英语 smeryen，更早作古英语 smierwan，意为「涂油、敷油」，词根属日耳曼语，表示「油脂」。

items.en: A reconstructed root meaning grease or fat lies behind smearing words in several Germanic languages.
items.cn: 构拟的日耳曼语词根义为「油脂」，多门日耳曼语的「涂抹」类词都由它派生。

items.en: Smierwan means to anoint or coat with oil or grease.
items.cn: 古英语 smierwan 意为涂油、敷油。

items.en: The verb settles into the form smere and later smere with the modern vowel.
items.cn: 中古英语中动词写为 smeryen，之后与同源的 smere（油脂）互相影响而稳定下来。

items.en: The verb extends from anointing to coating any sticky or dirty substance.
items.cn: 近代英语中，动词从敷油扩展到涂抹任何黏稠或脏的东西。

items.en: Modern English adds the figurative attack on reputation and the medical slide sample.
items.cn: 现代英语又扩展出「诽谤抹黑」的比喻义和医学上的「涂片」义。

note.en: Smear is a spreading verb first and an attack verb second, close to smudge, spread, and daub in form and meaning.
note.cn: smear 首先是「涂抹」动作，其次才是「攻击名誉」，形式上与 smudge、spread、daub 相近，意义上与这些词共享「弄上痕迹」的画面。

entries.definition: a dirty mark that has been rubbed and blurred
entries.definitionCN: 被蹭开、变模糊的脏痕；与 smear 拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: wet and easily spread or marked
to cover or stain with something wet or dirty
entries.definitionCN: 涂抹；弄脏（加了前缀 be- 的同源动词）

entries.definition: to open out a substance over an area
to coat something carelessly with paint or mud
to make a false spoken statement that damages reputation

normalIntro.en: Smear always involves a sticky layer moving over a surface, whether that surface is bread, glass, or a reputation.
normalIntro.cn: smear 的核心永远是「一层黏东西被抹过表面」，表面可以是面包、玻璃，也可以是名誉。

normal.en: Smear and smudge both start with sm- and both leave a blurry mark.
normal.cn: smear 与 smudge 都以 sm- 开头，都会留下模糊的痕迹。

normal.en: A smear campaign is a campaign that spreads dirt on people instead of policy.
normal.cn: a smear campaign 就是往人身上抹脏东西、而不是讨论政策的竞选。

normal.en: A smear test spreads a thin sample of cells on a slide.
normal.cn: a smear test 是把薄薄一层细胞样本涂在载玻片上检查。

normal.en: Smear takes -ed for the past and -ing for the action, with no doubling of the final consonant.
normal.cn: smear 的过去式是 smeared，现在分词是 smearing，词尾辅音不双写。

normal.en: Compare spread: spread opens a layer out, smear presses it on messily.
normal.cn: 对比 spread：spread 是把一层东西摊开，smear 是胡乱按上去。

abstract.en: Picture a knife gliding across toast and leaving a glossy trail.
abstract.cn: 想象刀子在吐司上滑过，拖出一道油亮的光泽。

abstract.en: Picture a muddy handprint on a white wall after the wall was meant to stay clean.
abstract.cn: 想象一面本该干净的墙上，被泥手按出一个印子。

abstract.en: Picture a word whispered about someone and sticking to them like grease.
abstract.cn: 想象关于某人的一句话被传开，像油污一样黏在身上甩不掉。

examples.en: He smeared sunscreen across his arms before the hike.
examples.cn: 徒步前他把防晒霜抹在手臂上。

examples.en: Opponents tried to smear the mayor with stories that turned out to be false.
examples.cn: 对手试图用后来被证明是假的传闻抹黑市长。

examples.en: A greasy smear covered the window after the repair.
examples.cn: 维修之后窗户上留下一道油腻的抹痕。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「死抹」——拿起东西死命往表面一抹，就是涂抹；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 smierwan（涂油、敷油）← 日耳曼语构拟词根，义为「油脂」→ smere（油脂）→ 英语 smear，核心义「把黏稠物抹在表面上」，再引申为弄脏、诽谤与涂片。

sensesIntro.en: Smear starts as the act of spreading grease on something, then names the dirty mark left behind, and finally turns the mark into both a medical sample and a figurative attack.
sensesIntro.cn: smear 先指把油或黏稠物抹上去的动作，再指抹完留下的脏痕，最后把这道痕迹分别变成医学的涂片和比喻意义上的抹黑攻击。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand rubbing a sticky layer across a clean surface.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手把黏稠的一层东西抹过干净的表面。

branches.en: Coating a surface with a sticky layer is the physical starting point.
branches.cn: 把黏稠物敷到表面上是最初的具体动作。

branches.en: The same spreading act on the wrong surface produces dirt and mess.
branches.cn: 同样的涂抹落在不该弄的地方，就变成弄脏。

branches.en: A stain on a reputation is an attack made with words.
branches.cn: 名誉上的污渍，就是用言语进行的攻击。

branches.en: Once the hand moves away, what remains is the visible smear.
branches.cn: 手移开之后，留在原处的那道痕迹就是名词义。

branches.en: Both a greasy mark and a lab slide are thin layers of material spread on a smooth surface.
branches.cn: 油腻的痕迹与实验室涂片都是薄薄一层物质被抹在光滑表面上。

intro.en: Smear is a native Germanic word, with a noun of its own and a productive -y adjective, smeary.
intro.cn: smear 是本土的日耳曼语词，有同源名词 smere，并借助 -y 构成形容词 smeary。

latinIntro.en: Latin has no ancestor of smear, but unguere, to anoint, is its closest semantic match.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语没有 smear 的同源词，语义最接近的是 unguere（涂油、敷油）。

items.example: Smear the cream evenly over the skin.
items.exampleCN: 把乳霜均匀地抹在皮肤上。

items.example: Sam meaning is kept in dialect words for grease.
items.exampleCN: 方言里仍保留表示「油脂」的说法。

items.example: A smear of oil showed on the glass.
items.exampleCN: 玻璃上有一道油痕。

items.meaning: a person or thing that does something
items.example: The suffix -er forms smearer.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -er 构成 smearer。

items.example: Smearer names a person who spreads either cream or lies.
items.exampleCN: smearer 既指涂东西的人，也指造谣的人。

items.example: The suffix -y forms smeary.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -y 构成 smeary。

items.example: The smeary surface caught every fingerprint.
items.exampleCN: 黏糊糊的表面沾满了指纹。

items.example: The prefix be- forms besmear.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 be- 构成 besmear。

items.example: Besmear adds a sense of covering completely.
items.exampleCN: besmear 多了一层「涂满全表面」的意思。

latinEntries.meaning: to anoint, to smear with oil
latinEntries.example: Unguere is the closest Latin meaning to smear.

latinEntries.example: Linere covers a surface with a thin layer.

definition_zh: 冶炼；熔炼；熔化的；嗅到；小胡瓜鱼；smell 的过去式与过去分词
definition_en: to melt ore in order to get metal out of it, or the past tense and past participle of smell
core_image: 炉门打开，矿石在高温里化成发亮的金属水流出来
scene: 老工厂里，工人把铁矿石和焦炭一起送进高炉，准备炼出铁水。The workers fed iron ore and coke into the furnace to smelt the metal.
sceneCN: 这里 smelt 是「冶炼、熔炼」（第 1 个义项：用高温从矿石中把金属分离出来）；句意：工人们把铁矿石和焦炭送进高炉，准备把金属炼出来。

pos.zh: smell 的过去式与过去分词（闻；嗅）

collocations.zh: 她闻到烟味（smell 的过去式）
一股洋葱味（smell 的过去式，较文学）

derivatives.zh: smelt 加施事后缀 -er，指冶炼厂或冶炼工
现在分词转名词，指冶炼、熔炼过程

senses.title: To melt ore to get metal
senses.definition: to heat ore strongly in a furnace so that the metal in it melts out and can be separated
senses.definitionCN: 在炉中高温加热矿石，使其中金属熔出并与杂质分离
senses.example: People have smelted copper in this valley for centuries.
senses.exampleCN: 几个世纪以来，人们一直在这一带的山谷里炼铜。
senses.why: The metal verb grows out of the furnace work of melting something down; the ore must be heated until the metal separates from the waste.
senses.whyCN: 冶炼义来自炉火熔化东西的作业：矿石必须加热到金属与废渣分离，所以核心画面是「熔化后分离」。

senses.title: The past tense of smell
senses.definition: the simple past form of smell, used to say that someone noticed a smell
senses.definitionCN: smell 的过去式，表示某人闻到了某种气味
senses.example: She smelt the coffee before she sat down.
senses.exampleCN: 她坐下前先闻了闻咖啡。
senses.why: This is simply the regular past of smell in British English, where the mouth-year spelling kept the old form.
senses.whyCN: 这是英式英语中 smell 的规则过去式，口耳相传保留了较老的 -t 形式，与冶炼义没有关系。

senses.title: The past form of smell in British use
senses.titleCN: smell 的过去分词（英式变体）
senses.definition: a past participle used in British English as an alternative to smelled
senses.definitionCN: 英式英语中与 smelled 并用的过去分词形式
senses.example: The room had smelt of paint for weeks.
senses.exampleCN: 这间屋子的油漆味已经持续了好几周。
senses.why: British speakers often use this form after have or be when the smell is finished or still hanging in the air.
senses.whyCN: 英式说话者常在 have 或 be 之后用它描述已经散去或仍停在空气里的气味，是同一个 smell 词的另一形态。

senses.title: The past form of smell as a copula
senses.titleCN: 闻起来；发出……气味（smell 的过去式）
senses.definition: the past form of a linking verb meaning to give off a particular smell
senses.definitionCN: 系动词用法的过去式，意为散发出某种气味
senses.example: The milk smelt sour, so we threw it out.
senses.exampleCN: 牛奶闻起来发酸，我们把它倒了。
senses.why: As a linking verb, smell describes what something seems to be; this form reports that impression in the past.
senses.whyCN: smell 作系动词时描述某物给人的印象，这个形式只是把这印象放到过去叙述。

senses.title: A small silver fish
senses.definition: a small silvery food fish found in northern seas and in fresh water
senses.definitionCN: 一种生活在北方海域和淡水中、体型小、银白色、可食用的鱼
senses.example: They fried a basket of smelt for supper.
senses.exampleCN: 他们炸了一篮胡瓜鱼当晚饭。
senses.why: The fish name comes from a separate Germanic word for a small river fish, and it only happens to match the metal verb in spelling.
senses.whyCN: 鱼名来自另一个表示小型河鱼的日耳曼语词，只是碰巧与冶炼动词拼写相同，所以这一义项与核心意象无关，属于同形异义。

senses.title: Being melted or refined
senses.definition: used as an adjective for metal that has been melted or purified in a furnace
senses.definitionCN: 作形容词，指在炉中熔化或提炼过的金属
senses.example: The smelt lead was poured into moulds.
senses.exampleCN: 熔化的铅被倒进模具里。
senses.why: As an adjective, the word keeps the furnace picture: metal that has already passed through heat and is now a purified solid.
senses.whyCN: 作形容词时仍保留高炉画面：金属已经过高温处理，如今是提纯了的固体。

senses.title: The past participle in British use
senses.titleCN: 被闻到；散发出气味（smell 的过去分词）
senses.definition: the past participle form of smell used in British English after have or be
senses.definitionCN: 英式英语中跟在 have 或 be 之后使用的 smell 过去分词
senses.example: The fish had smelt strong even through the ice.
senses.exampleCN: 即使隔着冰，那条鱼的气味也很冲。
senses.why: This is the same British past form as the previous sense, used in perfect and passive patterns.
senses.whyCN: 这是与前一个义项相同的英式过去形式，用在完成时与被动结构里，仍是 smell 的词形变化。

intro.en: Smelt is a doublet: the metal verb has a Germanic origin related to melt, while the smell verb is a form of smell, and the fish is a separate Germanic word.
intro.cn: smelt 其实是三股来源：炼金义的动词与 melt 同源，属日耳曼语；闻嗅义是 smell 的变体；鱼名则是另一个独立的日耳曼语词。

items.en: A reconstructed root related to melt gives the sense of making something soft or liquid by heat.
items.cn: 日耳曼语构拟词根与 melt 同源，表示用高温使物体变软、熔化。

items.en: Related smelting words in Middle Dutch and Old Norse show the ore-refining meaning in the region.
items.cn: 中古荷兰语与古诺尔斯语中相关的冶炼词，显示这一带的矿石提炼用法。

items.en: Smelt enters English as a metallurgical verb for melting ore.
items.cn: 中古英语晚期，smelt 作为冶金动词进入英语，专指熔炼矿石。

items.en: Smell carries the smelling sense, and the form smelt later appears as its past tense.
items.cn: 古英语 smell 承载「闻」的意义，后来其过去式出现 smelt 这一形式。

items.en: British English keeps smelt for the past, and American English prefers smelled; the fish name lives alongside both.
items.cn: 现代英式英语保留 smelt 作过去式，美式英语多用 smelled；鱼名则与之并行存在。

note.en: Smelt is easy to confuse with smell and melt, and the fish and the metal verb are unrelated in meaning though identical in spelling.
note.cn: smelt 容易与 smell、melt 混淆；而鱼名与冶炼义的动词虽然拼写相同，意义上却毫无关系。

normalIntro.en: Remember smelt by its furnace picture: ore plus heat equals metal plus waste, and the same spelling also serves the past of smell.
normalIntro.cn: 用高炉的画面记住 smelt：矿石加高温等于金属加废渣；而同一个拼写还兼任 smell 的过去式。

normal.en: Smelt the ore means heating it until the metal comes out.
normal.cn: smelt the ore 就是把矿石加热到金属分离出来。

normal.en: A smelter is the place and the worker that smelt metal.
normal.cn: smelter 既指冶炼厂，也指冶炼工。

normal.en: Smelt and melt share the same root, with the s added at the front.
normal.cn: smelt 与 melt 同源，只是在前面多了一个 s。

normal.en: In British English, smelt is the usual past of smell; Americans say smelled.

abstract.en: Picture a red-hot furnace mouth and a trickle of bright metal.
abstract.cn: 想象通红的炉口，一线明亮的金属流出来。

abstract.en: Picture a plate of fish and an oven in the same word, linked only by spelling.
abstract.cn: 想象同一个词里同时装着一盘鱼和一座炉子，连接它们的只有拼写。

abstract.en: Picture a grammarly past tense sitting on a shelf next to a bar of ore.
abstract.cn: 想象一道过去式的语法标签和一块矿石摆在同一个架子上。

examples.cn: 这家工厂从二十世纪初就在这里炼铜。

examples.en: She smelt the soup and added a little salt.
examples.cn: 她尝了闻汤的味道，又加了一点盐。

examples.en: The warehouse smelt of oil and old wood.
examples.cn: 仓库里有一股机油和陈年木头的味道。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「死闷特」——矿石在炉里闷得特热，金属就化了出来；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 三股来源：① 冶炼义与 melt 同源，属日耳曼语，核心义「用高温把矿石里的金属熔出来」；② 闻嗅义为 smell 的变体，用作过去式与过去分词；③ 鱼名为另一独立的日耳曼语词。

sensesIntro.en: Smelt first names the furnace work of getting metal from ore, then serves as a past form of smell, and separately names a small fish and a melted state.
sensesIntro.cn: smelt 首先指从矿石中炼出金属的炉中作业，随后又作为 smell 的过去形式出现；另外它还是一个独立的鱼名，以及「熔化状态」的形容词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a furnace door opens and melted metal flows out of crushed ore.
core.cn: 核心意象：炉门打开，熔化的金属从碎矿石里流出来。

branches.en: Mining and metalworking use the word for extracting metal from ore.
branches.cn: 采矿和冶金用这个词表示从矿石中提炼金属。

branches.en: The smell verb borrows the same spelling and sound, with a different past form meaning.
branches.cn: 「闻」义借用同样的拼写与读音，过去式表达的是不同的意思。

branches.en: British English uses this form after have or be.
branches.cn: 英式英语在 have 或 be 之后使用这一形式。

branches.en: The fish is a separate coinage that merely looks identical.
branches.cn: 鱼名是另一个独立的词，只是看上去一模一样。

branches.en: The adjective describes metal that has passed through the furnace.
branches.cn: 形容词描述已经过炉子处理的金属。

intro.en: Smelt builds a small family around itself with -er and -ing, while its other uses are simply homographs.
intro.cn: smelt 借助 -er、-ing 组成自己的小词族，而其他用法只是同形异义词。

latinIntro.en: No Latin ancestor exists for the metal verb, but Latin has words for melting and refining metals.
latinIntro.cn: 冶炼义没有拉丁同源词，但拉丁语中有表示金属熔化与提纯的词。

items.meaning: one who or that which does

items.meaning: a plant or person that smelts

items.exampleCN: 矿石耗尽后，冶炼厂关闭了。

items.example: Smell supplies the past form smelt in British use.
items.exampleCN: smell 在英式用法中提供过去式 smelt。

items.example: Melt shares the root behind smelt.
items.exampleCN: melt 与 smelt 共享词根。

definition_zh: 烟雾；雾霾；烟雾状大气污染
definition_en: a thick mixture of smoke and fog or of polluted air that hangs over a city
core_image: 城市上空糊着一层厚厚的灰黄色浓雾，看不清远处的高楼
scene: 冬天的清晨，整座城市被一层灰黄的浓烟笼罩，连对面楼顶都看不清。In winter mornings a thick brown smog hangs over the whole city.
sceneCN: 这里 smog 是「烟雾、雾霾」（第 1 个义项：烟与雾混合成的大气污染）；句意：冬天的清晨，一层灰褐色的浓雾笼罩着整座城市。

derivatives.zh: smog 去 -g 加形容词后缀 -y，义为「烟雾弥漫的」
smog 加否定后缀 -less，义为「无烟雾的」
smog 与 buster（对付者）拼合，指治理雾霾的车辆或设备

senses.title: Polluted air over a city
senses.definition: a low, thick cloud of polluted air that hangs over an area, often making it hard to breathe or see
senses.definitionCN: 低空弥漫的厚重污染空气，常让人呼吸困难、视线模糊
senses.example: Smog covers the city on windless winter days.
senses.exampleCN: 在无风的冬日，雾霾笼罩着这座城市。
senses.why: Smog was coined by blending smoke and fog, so the word was born already describing a mixture that hangs over a place.
senses.whyCN: smog 由 smoke（烟）与 fog（雾）混合而成，出生时就带着「悬在某地上空的混合物」这层意思。

senses.title: The original mixture of smoke and fog
senses.definition: a mixture of smoke and fog, especially the thick yellowish haze of early industrial cities
senses.definitionCN: 烟与雾的混合，尤指早期工业城市那种浓重发黄的雾
senses.example: Victorian London was famous for its choking smog.
senses.exampleCN: 维多利亚时代的伦敦因令人窒息的烟雾而闻名。
senses.why: In the nineteenth century fog was smoke-filled and dark, and the blend made that exact scene the maning of the word.
senses.whyCN: 十九世纪的雾里全是煤烟，天色发暗，造词者正是针对这一画面造出这个拼合词，所以它的本义就是烟与雾的混合。

senses.title: Haze from vehicle exhaust
senses.titleCN: （车辆尾气形成的）光化学烟雾
senses.definition: a brown haze caused mainly by exhaust from cars and trucks reacting in sunlight
senses.definitionCN: 主要由汽车和卡车尾气在阳光下反应形成的褐色烟雾
senses.example: Photochemical smog is worst where traffic is heaviest.
senses.exampleCN: 交通最繁忙的地方光化学烟雾最严重。
senses.why: Once factories stopped burning coal, the visible smoke source moved to exhaust pipes, but the haze looked the same, so the old word stayed.
senses.whyCN: 工厂不再烧煤之后，看得见的烟源转移到了排气管，但天上的浑浊没有变，于是旧词继续沿用。

senses.title: A period or spell with smog
senses.definition: a particular occasion or stretch of time when polluted air builds up, used with an article or a number
senses.definitionCN: 污染空气聚集的一段特定时间，常与冠词或数量搭配使用
senses.example: The city declared a smog alert for the whole weekend.
senses.exampleCN: 市政府整个周末都发布了雾霾预警。
senses.why: When a mixture becomes a recurring event, speakers count it and name it with an article, turning the mass word into a countable spell.
senses.whyCN: 当这种混合物变成反复发生的事件时，人们会去计数、加冠词，于是不可数的物质名词长出了可数的「一段时间」义。

intro.en: Smog is a modern blend of smoke and fog, coined in England in 1905 and made famous by nineteenth-century London air.
intro.cn: smog 是现代英语中由 smoke（烟）与 fog（雾）混合造出的词，一九零五年在英格兰出现，并因十九世纪伦敦的空气而广为人知。

items.en: Smoke and fog both come from Old English smocian and fogga, with Germanic roots.
items.cn: smoke 与 fog 都源于古英语，smoke 相关词形 smocian，fog 则为 fogga，词根属日耳曼语。

items.en: Coal smoke mixes with river fog in London and other industrial cities, so writers describe thick smoke-fog.
items.cn: 十九世纪伦敦及其他工业城市的煤烟与河雾混合，作家们开始描述浓重的「烟雾」。

items.en: Des Voeux proposes smog as smoke plus fog while debating the deadly dark fog of London.
items.cn: 德斯·沃克斯在讨论伦敦致命的黑雾时，把 smoke 与 fog 拼合提出 smog 一词。

items.en: Smog spreads worldwide as the word for the death of clean air in cities.
items.cn: 二十世纪中叶，smog 在全球流行，成为城市空气变脏的代名词。

items.en: Photochemical smog of the late twentieth century makes smog almost a synonym for urban air pollution.
items.cn: 二十世纪后期出现的光化学烟雾，让 smog 几乎等同于城市空气污染。

note.en: Smog is a blend word, close to smoke and fog in form, and close to haze and mist in meaning.
note.cn: smog 是一个混合词，形式上紧贴 smoke 与 fog，意义上则与 haze、mist 共享「看不清的浑浊空气」的画面。

entries.definition: cloudy grey air produced by burning
a thick cloud of water drops near the ground
full of or covered with smog
