a thin cloud of moisture in the air
harmful substances in air, water, or ground

normalIntro.en: Smog is literally smoke plus fog, so every meaning of the word grows from seeing a city through a dirty grey lens.
normalIntro.cn: smog 字面上就是 smoke 加 fog，所以这个词的所有义项都从「透过灰浑的镜片看城市」这一画面展开。

normal.en: Smog is a blend of smoke and fog, one of the classic portmanteau words.
normal.cn: smog 是 smoke 与 fog 的混合词，是经典的拼合词之一。

normal.en: A smog alert means the air outside is unhealthy, so people should stay indoors.
normal.cn: a smog alert 意味着外面的空气不健康，人们最好待在室内。

normal.en: The word appeared in England at the start of the twentieth century.
normal.cn: 这个词二十世纪初出现在英格兰。

normal.en: Smoggy is the adjective, built with -y from the noun.
normal.cn: smoggy 是对应的形容词，由名词加 -y 构成。

normal.en: Compare haze: haze can be natural and thin, smog is polluted and thick.
normal.cn: 对比 haze：haze 可以是自然界的薄霭，smog 则是厚重且受污染的。

abstract.en: Picture a row of skyscrapers cut off at the knees by a yellow wall.
abstract.cn: 想象一排高楼被一堵黄灰色的墙齐膝切断。

abstract.en: Picture a chimney and a riverbank fog meeting in the middle of the sky.
abstract.cn: 想象烟囱的烟和河岸的雾在半空中相遇。

abstract.en: Picture people wearing masks because the clouds came down to street level.
abstract.cn: 想象云层降到街道的高度，人们只好戴上口罩。

examples.en: The smog made it impossible to see the hills beyond the river.
examples.cn: 雾霾让人看不见河那边的小山。

examples.en: Old photographs show the smog of Victorian London at midday.
examples.cn: 老照片里能看到维多利亚时代伦敦正午时的浓雾。

examples.en: Officials issued a smog warning and asked drivers to use public transport.
examples.cn: 官员发布了雾霾预警，并要求司机改乘公共交通。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「死穆哥」——雾霾天闷得人一动不想动，城市像被蒙上一层灰；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 现代英语拼合词：smoke（烟）+ fog（雾）→ smog，一九零五年前后由英国卫生官员德斯·沃克斯提出，核心义「烟与雾混成的一片浑浊空气」，后扩展为一切城市空气污染。

sensesIntro.en: Smog begins as the literal mixture of smoke and fog, grows into the general word for polluted city air, then splits into the vehicle-born haze and the countable spell of bad air.
sensesIntro.cn: smog 起初专指烟与雾的混合，随后泛指被污染的城市空气，再由它分出机动车排放形成的光化学烟雾，以及可数的一段雾霾天气。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a grey-yellow blanket of dirty cloud lying over a whole city.
core.cn: 核心意象：一整座城市上空压着一层灰黄色的脏云。

branches.en: The everyday sense names polluted air that hangs low and thick.
branches.cn: 日常义项泛指低空浓重悬浮的污染空气。

branches.en: The original sense is the old mixture of coal smoke and river fog.
branches.cn: 本义是当年煤烟与河雾的混合物。

branches.en: Traffic replaces the factory smoke in the modern haze.
branches.cn: 现代烟雾里，汽车尾气取代了工厂的煤烟。

branches.en: A build-up of bad air can be announced, counted and reported as an event.
branches.cn: 污染空气的积聚可以被发布、计数、播报成一个事件。

branches.en: All three senses share a low, visible layer that blocks the view.
branches.cn: 三个义项都共享「低空、可见、挡住视线」的一层。

intro.en: Smog is a portmanteau word rather than a classic root word, and English builds smoggy and smogless on top of it.
intro.cn: smog 不是经典词根词，而是拼合词；英语又在它上面造出 smoggy 与 smogless。

latinIntro.en: Latin does not have smog, which is a modern English coinage, though it has words for smoke and for thick air.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语没有 smog，它是现代英语的创词；不过拉丁语有表示烟与厚重空气的词。

items.example: Smoke from coal fires filled the streets.
items.exampleCN: 煤火冒出的烟弥漫在街道上。

items.example: Thick fog hid the other bank of the river.
items.exampleCN: 浓雾遮住了对面的河岸。

items.example: Smog was coined for a very specific kind of city air.
items.exampleCN: smog 是为一种特定的城市空气造出来的。

items.example: A heavily smogged city can look almost like night.
items.exampleCN: 雾霾极重的城市看上去几乎像夜晚。

items.meaning: full of, having the quality of
items.example: The suffix -y forms smoggy.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -y 构成 smoggy。

items.example: Visibility falls sharply on smoggy days.
items.exampleCN: 雾霾天能见度急剧下降。

items.example: The suffix -less forms smogless.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -less 构成 smogless。

items.example: Planners promised a smogless urban future.
items.exampleCN: 规划者承诺一个没有雾霾的城市未来。

items.meaning: a device or vehicle against smog
items.meaningCN: 防治雾霾的装置或车辆
items.example: Smogbuster joins smog with an agent noun.
items.exampleCN: smogbuster 把 smog 与施事名词拼在一起。

items.meaning: an official warning about bad air
items.example: A smog alert starts before schools reopen in some cities.
items.exampleCN: 有些城市在开学前就会发布雾霾预警。

latinEntries.example: Fumus lies behind the English word fume.
latinEntries.exampleCN: fumus 是英语 fume 的来源。

latinEntries.example: Nebula links to the English word for cloudy air.
latinEntries.exampleCN: nebula 与英语中表示浑浊空气的词相关。

definition_zh: 使窒息；闷死；用厚厚的覆盖物盖住；抑制、压制（情绪或问题）；厚厚地涂抹
definition_en: to kill or stop someone from breathing by covering the face or by giving too little air, to cover something thickly with another substance, or to hold back feelings and keep them from showing
core_image: 一层厚厚的、不透气的东西蒙住口鼻，让人喘不上气
scene: 厨房里油锅起火，有人慌慌张张地把一块湿布整个盖在火上。Someone in the kitchen flung a wet cloth over the burning pan to smother the flames.
sceneCN: 这里 smother 是「闷灭、扑灭」（第 2 个义项：用覆盖物完全盖住并阻止其继续）：盖住火焰，不让空气进入，火就闷灭了；句意：厨房里有人慌慌张张地把一块湿布盖在起火的锅上，要把火闷灭。

pos.zh: 使窒息；闷死；闷灭（火）；厚厚地覆盖或涂抹；抑制（情绪）；压制（问题）
闷得透不过气；感到窒息

collocations.zh: 把担忧压下去不让人看见

derivatives.zh: 由动词加 -ing 构成，义为「令人窒息的」
由过去分词转作形容词，义为「被闷住的；涂得满满的」
动词加施动者后缀 -er 构成，义为「闷死他人的人」

senses.title: To stop breathing by covering the face
senses.definition: to kill a person or animal by covering the nose and mouth or by other means that stop the breathing
senses.definitionCN: 捂住所覆盖对象的口鼻或用其他方式，使某人或某动物停止呼吸而死亡
senses.example: The attacker tried to smother her with a pillow.
senses.exampleCN: 袭击者试图用枕头闷住她。
senses.why: The Old English root smorian already means to choke or suffocate, and to smother keeps that blocking of the air at its centre.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 smorian 本来就表示「使窒息」，闷住口鼻就是阻断空气，这正是词根最早的意义。

senses.title: To put out a fire by cutting off air
senses.definition: to put out a fire or a flame by covering it so completely that no air can reach it
senses.definitionCN: 把火或火焰完全盖住、让空气无法进入从而将其闷灭
senses.example: Cooks smother a pan fire with a lid or a damp cloth.
senses.exampleCN: 厨师会用锅盖或湿布把锅里的火闷灭。
senses.why: Fire needs air just as lungs do, so the same choking action that kills a flame becomes the second sense.
senses.whyCN: 火和人一样需要空气，所以「掐断空气」这一动作换个对象，就成了扑灭炉火的义项。

senses.title: To cover thickly with something
senses.definition: to cover a surface so thickly with a substance, or with too much of it, that the surface is hidden
senses.definitionCN: 用某种物质厚厚地盖住某个表面，甚至多得把表面遮没了
senses.example: She smothered the toast in bitter marmalade.
senses.exampleCN: 她把吐司涂满了苦味柑橘酱。
senses.why: Blanketing a surface until nothing shows through copies the image of a blanket over a face, so the word extends to food and surfaces.
senses.whyCN: 把表面盖到什么都露不出来，沿用的是「毯子盖脸」的画面，于是词义扩展到食物和器物表面。

senses.title: To hold back an emotion or reaction
senses.definition: to stop yourself from showing a feeling, a smile, or a sound such as a laugh or a yawn
senses.definitionCN: 克制自己不表露某种情绪、笑容或笑声、哈欠等声音
senses.example: He smothered a laugh behind his hand.
senses.exampleCN: 他用手挡住嘴，强忍住笑。
senses.why: A laugh that is smothered is held down the way a fire is, and what would break out is kept under cover.
senses.whyCN: 被憋住的笑就像被盖住的火，本来要冒出来的东西被压在了覆盖物下面。

senses.title: To give too much protection or attention
senses.definition: to give someone, especially a child, so much care and attention that they cannot act freely or grow
senses.definitionCN: 对某人（尤指孩子）给予过多关心和保护，使其无法自由行动或成长
senses.example: The boy was smothered by a mother who never let him play outside.
senses.exampleCN: 母亲把他护得太紧，从不让他到外面玩。
senses.why: To smother a child is to wrap it so tightly in care that the care itself becomes suffocating, the image of O1 turned into feeling.
senses.whyCN: 对孩子的过度保护像一层盖得太严的毯子，关心本身变成了让人透不过气的重量，是窒息画面的情感引申。

senses.title: To suppress problems or ideas
senses.definition: to stop an idea, a criticism, or a problem from being heard or from growing
senses.definitionCN: 使某种想法、批评或问题无法被听见或无法发展
senses.example: Poor staffing in the clinic smothered the voices of patients.
senses.exampleCN: 诊所人手不足，病人的声音被压了下去。
senses.why: Because anything covered cannot be seen or heard, smother also means to silence an opinion before it spreads.
senses.whyCN: 被盖住的东西自然看不见、听不到，所以这个词也用来表示在意见传开之前就把它压下去。

senses.title: To feel unable to breathe
senses.titleCN: 感到窒息；闷得透不过气
senses.definition: to feel unable to breathe, especially in a hot room or a crowd
senses.definitionCN: 尤指在闷热的房间或拥挤的地方感到喘不过气
senses.example: In that packed, airless hall she felt smothered.
senses.exampleCN: 在那个拥挤又憋闷的大厅里，她只觉得透不过气。
senses.why: Seen from the inside, the choking action becomes one more experience that the person goes through.
senses.whyCN: 从经历者的角度看，原本由外物造成的窒息感变成了自己亲身承受的体验。

intro.en: Smother goes back to Old English smorian, to choke or suffocate, and Old English already used it for putting out a fire by covering it.
intro.cn: smother 可追溯到古英语 smorian（使窒息），古英语时代就已用它表示「用覆盖物把火闷灭」。

items.en: Smorian means to choke or smother, and a related form names thick smoke.
items.cn: smorian 意为使窒息、闷死，另有一个相关词形指浓烟。

items.en: Smorien keeps the choking sense and also covers putting out a fire.
items.cn: smorien 保留了窒息义，同时用于表示扑灭火焰。

items.en: The word widens to food and surfaces hidden under too thick a layer.
items.cn: 词义扩展到食物和表面被过厚的物质盖住的情形。

items.en: Smother comes to mean holding back a laugh, a sound, or a feeling.
items.cn: smother 开始表示憋住笑声、声音或情绪。

items.en: Modern English adds the figurative senses of too much care and of silenced ideas.
items.cn: 现代英语增加了「过度保护」和「压制意见」这些引申义。

note.en: Smother sits with the breathing and fire words suffocate, stifle, and choke, and with the quieter cover words in its look-alike group.
note.cn: smother 与表示呼吸和火相关的 suffocate、stifle、choke 相邻，也与其形近组里的「遮盖」类词相邻。

entries.definition: to stop something from developing or being expressed
to burn slowly without a bright flame
causing a feeling of not being able to breathe
a female parent
entries.definitionCN: 母亲，只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: to die or be unable to breathe for lack of air
to be unable to breathe because something is blocking the throat
to hold back or put down by force

normalIntro.en: The Old English root already meant to choke, so every use of smother is a layer that shuts air out.
normalIntro.cn: 古英语词根已经是「使窒息」，所以 smother 的每个用法都是一层把空气挡在外面的东西。

normal.en: To smother a fire is to cover it until the air is gone.
normal.cn: smother a fire 就是用覆盖物把火盖到没有空气为止。

normal.en: Food that is smothered in sauce is buried under it.
normal.cn: 涂满了酱汁的食物等于被酱汁埋住。

normal.en: A smothered laugh is one that you hold back behind your hand.
normal.cn: 被憋住的笑，是你用手挡着压下去的笑。

normal.en: Compare suffocate: suffocate is the medical, physical word, while smother often names the covering action.
normal.cn: 对比 suffocate：suffocate 偏医学和生理，smother 更强调「盖上去」这个动作。

normal.en: Remember the phrase smothered in cream for things covered too thickly.
normal.cn: 记住 smothered in cream 这个说法，用来记「盖得太厚」。

abstract.en: Imagine a hand pressed over a mouth so that no air can pass.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手掌压在嘴上，一丝空气都透不过去。

abstract.en: Picture a blanket falling over a burning pan.
abstract.cn: 想象一条毯子落在起火的锅上。

abstract.en: See a piece of toast disappearing under far too much jam.
abstract.cn: 想象一片吐司被太厚太多的果酱盖得看不见了。

examples.en: Wet leaves smothered the young plants in the garden.
examples.cn: 湿透的叶子把花园里的幼苗盖死了。

examples.en: She smothered a smile when the lecture went on too long.
examples.cn: 讲到拖得太长时，她忍住没笑出来。

examples.en: The small room felt smothering in the summer heat.
examples.cn: 夏天的小房间闷得让人喘不过气。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「撕没的」——厚厚的东西整个盖上来把缝隙撕没了，人就透不过气；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 smorian（使窒息、闷死）→ 中古英语 smorien → 英语 smother，核心义「盖住并断绝空气」；与 suffocate、stifle 属同一「窒息」语场，来源上无拉丁同源词。

sensesIntro.en: Smother begins with the physical blocking of the breath, moves on to the covered fire and covered surfaces, and then turns inward to held emotions, over-protection, silenced ideas, and the feeling of suffocation.
sensesIntro.cn: smother 从「捂口鼻使窒息」的物理动作出发，扩展到「盖住火焰」与「厚盖表面」，再向内延伸为抑制情绪、过度保护、压制意见和自身的窒息感。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thick, airless layer pressed over a mouth and nose.
core.cn: 核心意象：一层厚重不透气的东西蒙住口鼻。

branches.en: The physical choking of a person is the oldest sense.
branches.cn: 对人身呼吸的直接阻断，是最古老的义项。

branches.en: Fire and food are covered in the same way that a face is covered.
branches.cn: 火和食物被盖住的方式，与盖住一张脸的方式相同。

branches.en: What cannot come out is held under, so laughter and opinions are smothered too.
branches.cn: 出不来东西都被压在下面，所以笑声和意见也会被闷住。

branches.en: Too much protection presses in on a child until the care itself stifles.
branches.cn: 照顾过多会像厚毯子一样压住孩子，关心本身把人闷坏了。

branches.en: Being smothered from outside and feeling smothered from inside share the same airless pressure.
branches.cn: 从外面被闷住与从里面感到窒息，承受的是同一种缺空气的压迫感。

intro.en: Smother is a native Old English word with no Latin root; its English family is small, built on the verb through -er, -ing, and -less.
intro.cn: smother 是古英语本族词，并没有拉丁词根；它的英语词族较小，是在动词上加 -er、-ing、-less 等词尾构成的。

latinIntro.en: Because smother has no Latin ancestor, the Latin entries keep only the borrowed adjectives and prefixes that describe the same choking idea.
latinIntro.cn: 由于 smother 没有拉丁语祖先，拉丁同源部分只保留借自拉丁语、描述同一「窒息」概念的形容词和前缀。

items.meaning: to choke or kill by covering the face
items.example: Smother is the basic English verb.
items.exampleCN: smother 是基本英语动词。

items.example: The suffix -er forms smotherer from the verb.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -er 由动词构成 smotherer。

items.example: Smotherer names the person who does the act.
items.exampleCN: smotherer 指做出这一动作的人。

items.example: The suffix -ing forms smothering from the verb.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ing 由动词构成 smothering。

items.example: Smothering describes an airless room.
items.exampleCN: smothering 形容没有空气的房间。

items.example: The suffix -ed makes the past participle smothered.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ed 构成过去分词 smothered。

items.meaning: covered so thickly that it is hidden
items.example: Smothered food is buried under sauce.
items.exampleCN: 被 smother 过的食物埋在酱汁下面。

items.example: The rare form smotherless means without choking.
items.exampleCN: 罕用形式 smotherless 意为不致窒息的。

items.meaning: to choke or stop the breath of
items.example: Latin suffocare gives English suffocate.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语 suffocare 构成英语 suffocate。

items.example: Suffocate is the Latin side of the same idea.
items.exampleCN: suffocate 是同一概念在拉丁语这一支的对应词。

definition_zh: 走私；偷运；偷偷带进或带出；私自夹带
definition_en: to take goods or people secretly into or out of a place, especially in a way that breaks the law, or to carry something in secretly where it is not allowed
core_image: 把东西藏在衣服里层或货物夹缝中，人装作若无其事地走过检查口
scene: 旅客把几块罕见的鸟蛋用毛巾包好，塞进随身背包的夹层里，想混过海关。The traveller tried to smuggle rare eggs through customs in the lining of a backpack.
sceneCN: 这里 smuggle 是「走私、偷偷带过」（第 1 个义项：违法地秘密运入或运出）：东西藏在包的内层，人照常排队过关；句意：这名旅客想把罕见的鸟蛋藏在背包夹层里混过海关。

pos.zh: 走私（货物）；偷运；偷偷携带
走私（较少用，多见于旧式或方言说法）

collocations.phrase: smuggle sth out of the country

derivatives.zh: 动词加 -ing 名词化，义为「走私（活动）；走私行为」
动词加施动者后缀 -er，义为「走私者；走私犯」
由过去分词转作形容词，义为「偷运来的；走私的」

senses.title: To move goods in or out illegally
senses.definition: to take goods secretly into or out of a country or place, usually to avoid paying tax or because the goods are forbidden
senses.definitionCN: 秘密地把货物运入或运出某国或某地，常为逃税或运送违禁品
senses.example: They tried to smuggle cigarettes across the border.
senses.exampleCN: 他们试图把香烟走私过境。
senses.why: The Dutch and Low German root means to creep or sneak, so the first sense is goods slipping past the lawful checking point.
senses.whyCN: 源自荷兰语和低地德语的词根意为「悄悄爬行、溜」，所以第一个义项就是货物从合法的检查关口旁边「溜」过去。

senses.title: To bring people across borders secretly
senses.definition: to take people secretly into or out of a country, especially people who are not allowed to enter
senses.definitionCN: 秘密地把人运入或运出某国，尤指运送不被允许入境的人
senses.example: The lorry driver was paid to smuggle refugees into the port.
senses.exampleCN: 这名卡车司机收钱把难民偷运进港口。
senses.why: Once the pattern of slipping past the border is fixed, it can carry people as easily as goods.
senses.whyCN: 一旦「绕过边境」的用法固定下来，运送对象就可以从货物扩展到人。

senses.title: To carry something in secretly
senses.definition: to carry something secretly into a place where it is forbidden, such as a prison, a school, or an exam room
senses.definitionCN: 把某物偷偷带进禁止携带物品的地方，如监狱、学校或考场
senses.example: A visitor smuggled a phone into the prison inside a loaf of bread.
senses.exampleCN: 一名探视者把手机藏在一只面包里带进了监狱。
senses.why: The border shrinks to any guarded doorway, and the sense becomes the small-scale secret carrying of an object.
senses.whyCN: 边境缩小成任何有人看守的门口，词义就变成了小规模地偷偷携带物品。

senses.title: To hide something in what you carry
senses.titleCN: 夹藏；偷塞（进入包裹、衣物）
senses.definition: to hide something inside an object, a bag, or a piece of clothing so that it is not noticed
senses.definitionCN: 把东西藏进某件物品、包或衣服里，使它不被发现
senses.example: He smuggled a small note into his jacket sleeve.
senses.exampleCN: 他把一张小纸条藏进了外套袖子里。
senses.why: Concealment is the method behind the act, and English uses the same verb for the hiding itself.
senses.whyCN: 藏匿是这一动作背后的手段，英语索性用同一个词来指「藏」这个环节。

senses.title: To move things in secretly at a distance
senses.titleCN: 偷偷运送；私运（尤指长距离、成规模）
senses.definition: to transport things secretly over a distance, often as part of an organised trade
senses.definitionCN: 秘密地把东西运送一段距离，常是有组织的交易的一部分
senses.example: Cheap timber was smuggled down the river to the coast.
senses.exampleCN: 廉价木材被偷偷沿河运到海边。
senses.why: When smuggling is organised, the word names the whole long journey rather than a single crossing.
senses.whyCN: 当走私成为有组织的活动时，这个词指的就是整段长距离运输，而不只是一次过关。

senses.title: To do smuggling as a way of living
senses.definition: to earn money by smuggling, used without a direct object or with smuggler as the subject
senses.definitionCN: 以走私谋生，常不带宾语，或主语就是走私者
senses.example: The families have smuggled along this coast for three generations.
senses.exampleCN: 这些家族在这条海岸线上已经走私了三代人。
senses.why: A repeated activity becomes a trade, so the verb gains an intransitive, occupational use.
senses.whyCN: 反复进行的活动变成一门营生，于是这个词就有了不及物的、表示职业的用法。

intro.en: Smuggle is of Low German origin, with a verb meaning to creep or sneak that is recorded in Dutch and Low German in the seventeenth century.
intro.cn: smuggle 源自低地德语，其荷兰语和低地德语中的动词义为「悄悄爬行、溜」，最早见于十七世纪。

items.en: A Low German verb with the sense of creeping quietly underlies the word, and its earlier form is uncertain.
items.cn: 一个意为「悄悄爬行、溜」的低地德语动词是这个词的底子，更早的词形则不确定。

items.en: The Dutch and Low German verb is recorded with the sense of moving secretly.
items.cn: 荷兰语和低地德语中这个词的词义被记录下来，指秘密移动的方式。

items.en: English smuggle appears first, meaning to bring in goods secretly and illegally.
items.cn: 英语 smuggle 最早出现时，意为秘密违法地带入货物。

items.en: The verb extends to people and to anything carried secretly into a guarded place.
items.cn: 词义扩展到人，以及任何被偷偷带进受看守场所的东西。

items.en: Modern English uses smuggle for organised trade, and smugglers appear in news and law.
items.cn: 现代英语用 smuggle 指有组织的走私贸易，走私者一词也频繁出现在新闻与法律中。

note.en: Smuggle shares its sneaking image with the look-alike words below, and its legal trade meaning with contraband, traffic, and bootleg.
note.cn: smuggle 与下面的形近词共享「偷偷摸摸」的意象，与 contraband、traffic、bootleg 共享「违法交易」的核心意义。

entries.definition: a person who takes goods or people in or out secretly
the activity of carrying things in or out secretly
too pleased with yourself
entries.definitionCN: 自满的，只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: goods brought in or out illegally
to buy and sell illegal goods
to make or sell something illegally

normalIntro.en: The core of smuggle is sneaking, so it always pairs with something hidden going past a border or a guard.
normalIntro.cn: smuggle 的核心是「偷偷摸摸」，所以它总与藏起来的东西绕过边境或看守搭配。

normal.en: Smuggle goods through customs is the classic use.
normal.cn: smuggle goods through customs 是最典型的用法。

normal.en: The noun smuggler keeps the -er ending for the person.
normal.cn: 名词 smuggler 用 -er 词尾指人。

normal.en: Smuggle people is about borders, while smuggle a phone is about a guarded room.
normal.cn: 偷运人强调边境，偷偷带手机强调有人看守的房间。

normal.en: Compare contraband: smuggle is the act, contraband is the goods.
normal.cn: 对比 contraband：smuggle 是动作，contraband 是被偷运的货物。

normal.en: Remember the phrase smuggled abroad for goods that leave a country quietly.
normal.cn: 记住 smuggled abroad 这个说法，指货物悄无声息地流出境外。

abstract.en: Picture a suitcase whose lining is cut open and filled with folded notes.
abstract.cn: 想象一只行李箱的内层被剪开，里面塞满叠好的纸币。

abstract.en: See a lorry whose spare tyre is packed with cigarettes.
abstract.cn: 想象一辆卡车的备胎里塞满了香烟。

abstract.en: Watch a note slide out of a shoe in a prison visiting room.
abstract.cn: 想象在监狱会客室里，一张纸条从鞋里滑了出来。

examples.en: The gang smuggled ivory through three ports.
examples.cn: 这个团伙经由三个港口走私象牙。

examples.en: Smugglers hide the goods in the false bottoms of old crates.
examples.cn: 走私者把货物藏在旧木箱的假底里。

examples.en: She smuggled extra batteries into the overnight camp.
examples.cn: 她偷偷带了几节备用电池去参加夜营。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「私马够」——私底下把马够着牵过关卡，不为外人所知；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 低地德语中意为「悄悄爬行、溜」的动词（荷兰语有同族说法）→ 英语 smuggle（走私，十七世纪），核心义「偷偷溜过关卡」；更早的词形不确定，来源上无拉丁同源词。

sensesIntro.en: Smuggle starts with goods slipping past a border, extends to people and to any guarded doorway, and finally becomes a trade that runs over long distances.
sensesIntro.cn: smuggle 从货物偷偷越过边境开始，扩展到人和任何有人看守的门口，最后固定为一种长距离的职业性活动。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: something hidden against the body, moving past a guarded check point.
core.cn: 核心意象：东西贴身藏着，从有人看守的检查口旁溜过去。

branches.en: Goods that cross a border secretly are the core sense.
branches.cn: 悄悄越过边境的货物是核心义项。

branches.en: People taken across borders follow the same secret route.
branches.cn: 被运过边境的人也走同样的秘密路线。

branches.en: The border becomes any guarded doorway, and hiding something is the method.
branches.cn: 边境缩小成任何有人看守的门口，藏匿物品则是其手段。

branches.en: Long secret trips turn the verb into a description of transport.
branches.cn: 长距离的秘密运输使这个动词带上了「水陆运送」的意味。

branches.en: Repeated illegal crossings settle into a living and a trade.
branches.cn: 反复的违法越境最终固化成一种营生和职业。

intro.en: Smuggle is a Low German loan with no Latin root; its English family grows from the verb with -er, -ing, and -ed.
intro.cn: smuggle 是借自低地德语的词，没有拉丁词根；它的英语词族是由动词加 -er、-ing、-ed 构成的。

latinIntro.en: The Latin side of smuggling vocabulary comes from contraband and traffic, which describe illegal trade; smuggle itself has no Latin ancestor.
latinIntro.cn: 与走私相关的拉丁语部分来自 contraband 与 traffic，它们描述违法交易；smuggle 本身并没有拉丁语祖先。

items.example: Smuggle is the base verb.
items.exampleCN: smuggle 是基础动词。

items.example: The suffix -er forms smuggler from the verb.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -er 由动词构成 smuggler。

items.example: Smuggler names the person behind the act.
items.exampleCN: smuggler 指做出这一行为的人。

items.example: The suffix -ing forms smuggling as a noun.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ing 使 smuggling 成为名词。

items.example: Smuggling is now a crime in the law.
items.exampleCN: smuggling 如今在法律上是一项罪名。

items.example: The suffix -ed makes the participle smuggled.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ed 构成分词 smuggled。

items.example: Smuggled goods are seized at the port.
items.exampleCN: 走私货物在港口被查获。

items.example: The prefix contra- joins bannum in contraband.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 contra- 与 bannum 合成 contraband。

items.example: Contraband is what smugglers carry.
items.exampleCN: contraband 就是走私者携带的东西。

items.example: Latin bannum means a ban or a prohibition.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语 bannum 意为禁令。

definition_zh: 零食；小吃；（少量）点心；吃零食
definition_en: a small amount of food eaten between main meals, or a small quick meal, and the verb meaning to eat such food
core_image: 手边一小袋东西，随手抓一把塞进嘴里，两口就吃完
scene: 午休时，办公室里几个人从抽屉里翻出一袋坚果，一边聊天一边嚼。At lunch break, a few people in the office pulled a bag of nuts out of a drawer and snacked while they chatted.
sceneCN: 这里 snack 是「吃零食」这个动作（第 2 个义项：两餐之间吃点小东西）：不是正餐，随手抓一把坚果边聊边吃；句意：午休时，办公室里几个人从抽屉里翻出一袋坚果，一边聊天一边吃。

derivatives.zh: 动词加施动者后缀 -er，义为「爱零食的人；爱加餐的人」
动词加 -ing 名词化，义为「吃零食这一行为」
名词加 -y 构成，义为「像零食的；适合当零食的」（口语）

senses.title: A small amount of food between meals
senses.definition: a small amount of food, such as fruit, nuts, or biscuits, eaten between the main meals of the day
senses.definitionCN: 在两顿正餐之间吃的一小份食物，如水果、坚果或饼干
senses.example: She keeps a healthy snack in her school bag.
senses.exampleCN: 她的书包里总放着一份健康零食。
senses.why: The verb snack comes from the Dutch and Low German snakken, to snap at food like a dog, so a snack is the little bite you take on the side.
senses.whyCN: 动词 snack 源自荷兰语和低地德语的 snakken，指像狗一样猛地咬一口，所以 snack 就是正餐之外「咬一口」的那份东西。

senses.title: To eat a little between meals
senses.definition: to eat a small amount of food instead of, or between, proper meals
senses.definitionCN: 不吃正餐或在正餐之间，只吃少量的东西
senses.example: The children snacked on fruit after swimming practice.
senses.exampleCN: 游泳训练结束后，孩子们吃着水果当零食。
senses.why: The noun gives the English verb its action: to have a small bite rather than a full meal.
senses.whyCN: 名词义给了动词以动作：只是小咬一口，而不是坐下来吃一顿正餐。

senses.title: A small informal meal
senses.titleCN: 便餐；小吃（一顿简单的饭）
senses.definition: a small, simple meal eaten quickly, often standing or on the move, instead of a full one
senses.definitionCN: 在站着或赶路时快速吃的一顿简单小餐，代替一顿正式饭
senses.example: We grabbed a snack at the station before the train.
senses.exampleCN: 上火车之前，我们在车站匆匆吃了点东西。
senses.why: When the small bite stands in for a whole meal, the word shifts from side food to a light main event.
senses.whyCN: 当这「小咬一口」顶替了一整顿饭时，词义就从附带的小食变成了一顿轻便的主餐。

senses.title: A quick bite to keep you going
senses.definition: a small item eaten to stop hunger for a short time, especially in a busy schedule
senses.definitionCN: 为暂时压住饥饿而吃的少量东西，尤见忙碌的日程中
senses.example: A banana was her only snack before the long exam.
senses.exampleCN: 漫长考试前，她只拿一根香蕉垫了垫肚子。
senses.why: Snacking is eating for immediate energy rather than for a meal, so the sense narrows to a stopgap bite.
senses.whyCN: 吃零食图的是马上补充能量而不是正经吃饭，于是这个义项收窄成「应急垫一垫」。

senses.title: Snack food as a category
senses.definition: small packaged foods made for casual eating, such as nuts, crisps, and biscuits
senses.definitionCN: 为随意食用而制成的小包装食品，如坚果、薯片和饼干
senses.example: The shop sells both canned drinks and snacks.
senses.exampleCN: 这家店既卖罐装饮料，也卖零食。
senses.why: Many small bites sold the same way merge into one commercial name for a category of food.
senses.whyCN: 许多以同样方式出售的小食合在一起，就成了一个食品大类的统称。

intro.en: Snack is linked to Dutch and Low German words for snapping at something, and it entered English in the fifteenth century as a bite or a small share.
intro.cn: snack 与荷兰语和低地德语中表示「猛地咬住」的词相关，十五世纪进入英语时意为「一口；一小份」。

items.en: Snakken is used of an animal that snaps or snatches at food.
items.cn: snakken 用于形容动物猛地咬住或抢食的样子。

items.en: The same meaning is recorded in Dutch, and the word crosses into English from this group.
items.cn: 荷兰语中记录了这一意义，这个词正是由这一组语言进入英语的。

items.en: English snack first names a bite or a small share of food.
items.cn: 英语 snack 最早指一口食物或一小份食物。

items.en: The noun settles into its modern sense of a small bite between meals.
items.cn: 名词义固定为现代义：正餐之间吃的一小口。

items.en: The verb snack follows the noun, and snack food names a whole category.
items.cn: 动词 snack 由名词引申而来，而零食类别则以 snack food 这样的说法命名。

note.en: Snack keeps the idea of snapping a little food, and it sits close to the look-alike words snap, snag, and snuck, as well as to the everyday words for light food.
note.cn: snack 保留了「猛地咬一小口」的意思，与形近的 snap、snag、snuck 容易混，也与表示「轻便小食」的常用词意义相邻。

entries.definition: to break suddenly, or to bite quickly
a hidden problem or a small trouble
a past form of sneak in American English
entries.definitionCN: 悄悄溜走的过去式（美式），只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: a person who likes eating between meals
a small amount of food eaten quickly
a special food or pleasure

normalIntro.en: Snack is the snap of a small bite: something quick, small, and taken on the side of a meal.
normalIntro.cn: snack 的核心是「猛地咬一口」：快、小、在正餐之外吃。

normal.en: A snack is something small eaten between meals.
normal.cn: snack 指正餐之间吃的一小份东西。

normal.en: To snack on fruit is to eat fruit as a snack.
normal.cn: snack on fruit 就是拿水果当零食吃。

normal.en: Snack food and snacks name whole categories on a shelf.
normal.cn: snack food 和 snacks 合起来指货架上一整类零食。

normal.en: Compare to eat a meal: a snack is smaller and quicker than a meal.
normal.cn: 对比吃一顿饭：snack 比正餐更小、更快。

normal.en: Remember the phrase a quick snack for something grabbed on the way.
normal.cn: 记住 a quick snack 这个说法，指路上随手拿来吃的点心。

abstract.en: Picture a hand slipping into a bag of nuts in a desk drawer.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手伸进抽屉里的坚果袋。

abstract.en: See crumbs on a keyboard after a few minutes in front of the screen.
abstract.cn: 想象在屏幕前吃了几分钟，键盘上就撒满了碎屑。

abstract.en: Imagine a sandwich held in one hand at a station platform.
abstract.cn: 想象在站台上，一只手拿着一个三明治匆匆吃。

examples.en: Please bring a snack and a bottle of water for the trip.
examples.cn: 请为这趟出行带一份零食和一瓶水。

examples.en: We snacked on biscuits while the film was running.
examples.cn: 电影放映时我们嚼着饼干。

examples.en: The cafe sells snacks and hot drinks all day.
examples.cn: 这家咖啡馆全天供应零食和热饮。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「思那克」——想着那包小零食，忍不住偷嚼几口；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 中古低地德语 snakken（猛地咬、抢食，与荷兰语同义）→ 十五世纪进入英语 snack（一口；一小份）→ 现代英语「零食；吃零食」，核心义「正餐之外的小咬一口」；来源上无拉丁同源词。

sensesIntro.en: Snack begins with a small bite taken on the side, becomes the verb that names that bite, and widens to a light meal, a stopgap bite, and finally a whole category of food.
sensesIntro.cn: snack 从「正餐之间小咬一口的那份东西」出发，变成表示这个动作的动词，再扩展为一顿便餐、临时垫肚子的加餐，最后成为整类零食的统称。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small handful of food grabbed and eaten between proper meals.
core.cn: 核心意象：正餐之间随手抓一把食物塞进嘴里。

branches.en: The small bite on the side is the base noun sense.
branches.cn: 正餐之外的一小口，是名词最基本的义项。

branches.en: The same small bite is also an action, the verb sense.
branches.cn: 同一份「小咬一口」也是一个动作，即动词义项。

branches.en: A bite big enough to stand in for a meal, or just enough to stop hunger, becomes a light meal.
branches.cn: 大到可以代替一餐、或刚好能压住饥饿的一口，就成了一顿便餐。

branches.en: Many small bites sold together become a commercial category.
branches.cn: 许多小食放在一起出售，就形成了一整个商业品类。

branches.en: All these senses keep the same pattern of quick, small eating outside a proper meal.
branches.cn: 这些义项共享同一模式：在正餐之外，快而少地吃东西。

intro.en: Snack is a Low German loan, and its English family grows from the noun and verb with -er, -ing, and -y.
intro.cn: snack 是借自低地德语的词，它的英语词族是在名词和动词上加 -er、-ing、-y 形成的。

latinIntro.en: Snack has no Latin root; the Latin entries below are the related light-food words, built from the same small-eater idea.
latinIntro.cn: snack 没有拉丁词根；下面的拉丁同源部分是与「小量吃食」相关的词，由同一「少而小地吃」的概念构成。

items.meaning: a small amount of food between meals
items.example: Snack is the base noun.
items.exampleCN: snack 是基础名词。

items.meaning: to eat a little between meals
items.example: The verb snack comes from the noun.
items.exampleCN: 动词 snack 由名词引申而来。

items.example: The suffix -er forms snacker from the verb.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -er 由动词构成 snacker。

items.example: Snacker is informal and common in magazines.
items.exampleCN: snacker 口语色彩较浓，常见于杂志。

items.example: The suffix -ing forms snacking as a noun.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ing 使 snacking 成为名词。

items.meaning: the habit of eating between meals
items.example: Snacking between meals is now common.
items.exampleCN: 两餐之间吃零食如今很常见。

items.example: The suffix -y forms snacky from the noun.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -y 由名词构成 snacky。

items.meaning: like a snack, suitable for snacking
items.meaningCN: 像零食的；适合当零食的
items.example: Snacky foods are easy to eat with one hand.
items.exampleCN: 适合当零食的食物单手就能吃。

items.example: Latin merenda gives the old word for a light afternoon meal.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语 merenda 留下了表示下午加餐的古老说法。

items.example: The suffix -culum once marked a small portion of food.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -culum 曾用来标记一小份食物。

latinEntries.meaning: a taste or a slight taste of something

definition_zh: 偷偷地走；潜行；偷偷地做；告密；偷偷摸摸的人
definition_en: to move or do something quietly and secretly so that nobody notices, or a person who does this or tells on others
core_image: 贴着墙根的影子：压低身子，一点声音也不带地挪过去
scene: 深夜的宿舍走廊里，他贴着墙根悄悄走向门口，生怕吵醒室友。He tried to sneak out of the dormitory before the door was locked.
sceneCN: 这里 sneak 是「偷偷地走」（第 1 个义项：悄悄移动）；句意：他想在门锁上之前偷偷溜出宿舍。图中可辨识物件：走廊、墙、门口、微光。

collocations.zh: 悄悄地接近；冷不防地靠近

derivatives.zh: 由基础词加 -y 构成，义为「鬼鬼祟祟的；阴险的」
由动词加 -er 构成，指走路无声的软底鞋，也指穿这种鞋的人
现在分词转作形容词，义为「暗自的；隐隐的」，如暗自的怀疑
由 sneaky 加 -ly 构成，义为「偷偷摸摸地」
由 sneaky 加 -ness 构成，义为「鬼祟；偷偷摸摸」

senses.title: To move quietly and secretly
senses.definition: to move stealthily and quietly in order to avoid being seen or heard
senses.definitionCN: 为了不被看到或听到而悄悄地、鬼祟地移动
senses.example: The cat sneaked along the fence and vanished into the hedge.
senses.exampleCN: 猫沿着栅栏悄悄走过，钻进树篱不见了。
senses.why: The word began as an old verb for creeping along close to the ground, so the body-shaped stealth image is the oldest layer.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初是表示「贴地爬行」的古动词，所以最古老的层面就是压低身子、不出声移动的身体画面。

senses.title: To do something secretly
senses.definition: to do something without permission or without letting other people know
senses.definitionCN: 未经允许或不让他人知道地做某事
senses.example: She sneaked a quick look at the answers under the desk.
senses.exampleCN: 她在课桌底下偷偷瞄了一眼答案。
senses.why: Once the stealthy movement is established, the same idea transfers from the body to the action: anything done out of sight fits.
senses.whyCN: 一旦「悄悄移动」的画面立起来，这层意思就从身体动作转到行为本身：任何背着人做的事都套得进去。

senses.title: To tell on someone
senses.definition: to inform an adult or authority about a small or secret wrongdoing
senses.definitionCN: 向大人或当权者报告别人小错或隐秘的过失
senses.example: He sneaked on his classmates and told the teacher who had skipped class.
senses.exampleCN: 他把同学的事告给了老师，说出了谁逃了课。
senses.why: Reporting is also done behind someone back, so the stealthy core image easily extends to a person who creeps to the teacher.
senses.whyCN: 告密同样是背着当事人去做的，所以「悄悄」这个核心画面自然延伸到溜到老师跟前说话的人。

senses.title: A person who creeps or tells
senses.definition: a person who moves or behaves in a sly, secretive way, or who informs on others
senses.definitionCN: 行动鬼祟或告发他人的人
senses.example: The teacher called him a sneak for telling tales about his friends.
senses.exampleCN: 老师因为他告朋友的状，叫他告密鬼。
senses.why: English loves to turn a stealthy action into a person noun, so the creeping verb also names the creeping person.
senses.whyCN: 英语喜欢把「动作」直接转成「做事的人」，所以这个表示潜行的动词也用来指潜行的人。

senses.title: Secret or unexpected
senses.definition: done secretly or happening suddenly and without warning
senses.definitionCN: 秘密进行的，或突然发生、事先没有征兆的
senses.example: We took a sneak look at the birthday cake before the party.
senses.exampleCN: 派对开始前我们偷偷看了一眼生日蛋糕。
senses.why: The adverb-like use in fixed phrases freezes the secrecy into an adjective, and from sudden secrecy grows the sense of surprise.
senses.whyCN: 在一些固定说法里它像副词一样修饰动作，把「秘密」凝固成形容词，而「突然的秘密」又生出「出其不意」。

senses.title: A peep without being noticed
senses.definition: a quick or stolen look at something
senses.definitionCN: 快速地或偷着看上一眼
senses.example: Have a sneak at the menu before you choose a table.
senses.exampleCN: 挑座位之前先偷瞄一眼菜单。
senses.why: If the whole point of sneaking is not being caught, a single stolen glance is the smallest complete act of sneaking.
senses.whyCN: 潜行的全部要点是不被抓住，所以「偷瞄一眼」就是潜行这件事最小的完整动作。

senses.title: To creep into a place or state
senses.definition: to move something into or out of a place quietly, or to let a feeling spread unnoticed
senses.definitionCN: 悄悄把某人某物带进或带出某处，或让某种感觉不知不觉地蔓延
senses.example: A warm smile sneaked into her face as he finished the story.
senses.exampleCN: 他讲完故事时，一丝温暖的笑容悄悄爬上她的脸。
senses.why: The path of a sneaking body is a corridor into and out of a place, so anything that arrives unnoticed can follow the same path.
senses.whyCN: 潜行者的路线就是进出某处的一条通道，于是任何「悄悄到来」的东西都能沿着同一条路线出现。

intro.en: Sneak is a word of uncertain origin, first recorded in the sixteenth century; some scholars connect it with English snack and snatch.
intro.cn: sneak 来源不确定，最早见于十六世纪，有学者把它与英语的 snack 和 snatch 联系起来。

items.en: Older forms such as snican record creeping or crawling, and the exact origin of the word remains uncertain.
items.cn: 更早的形式如 snican 记录过爬行、潜行，但确切来源不确定。

items.en: Sneak appears in writing for the first time, describing someone creeping along quietly.
items.cn: 英语里 sneak 最早见于文字记录，描写有人悄悄爬行。

items.en: The verb spreads from creeping feet to secret looks and secret acts.
items.cn: 这个动词从「悄悄挪动的脚」扩展到「偷偷看」和「偷偷做」。

items.en: A person who creeps or tells is called a sneak, and sneaker names a soft silent shoe.
items.cn: 鬼祟行事或告密的人被称为 sneak，而软底无声的鞋被称为 sneaker。

items.en: Modern English adds phrases such as sneak peek and sneaking suspicion.
items.cn: 现代英语又增加了 sneak peek、sneaking suspicion 之类短语。

note.en: Sneak sits between creep and steal as a word of quiet motion, close to its family sneaker, sneaky and snacks.
note.cn: sneak 在表示「悄悄移动」的词群里，位置介于 creep 与 steal 之间，与同一词族的 sneaker、sneaky 以及 snacks 相邻。

entries.definition: a soft shoe with a rubber sole that makes almost no sound
entries.definitionCN: 软底胶底鞋，走起来几乎没有声音

entries.definition: behaving in a secret or dishonest way
secret and not openly expressed
entries.definitionCN: 暗自在心里的，没公开表达的

entries.definition: a small quick meal eaten between main meals
to grab something quickly, especially in a rough way
to move slowly and quietly, especially along the ground
entries.definitionCN: 缓慢而无声地移动，尤指贴着地面

entries.definition: to move somewhere quietly and carefully so that nobody notices
entries.definitionCN: 悄悄而小心地移到某处，不引人注意

entries.definition: to wait quietly in a hidden place, ready to move
entries.definitionCN: 藏在隐蔽处静静等候，伺机而动

entries.definition: to move somewhere quickly and quietly, often without being seen
entries.definitionCN: 快速静悄悄地移动，常不被看见

normalIntro.en: Sneak is a word of quiet motion: the feet do the work, and the eyes learn to do the same.
normalIntro.cn: sneak 是关于「无声移动」的词：先是脚在动，后来眼睛也学会这样。

normal.en: Sneak out means to leave a place secretly.
normal.cn: sneak out 表示偷偷离开某处。

normal.en: Sneak up on someone means approach without being heard.
normal.cn: sneak up on 某人表示不出声地靠近。

normal.en: Sneak a look means take a quick secret glance.
normal.cn: sneak a look 表示快速而隐蔽地看一眼。

normal.en: A sneaker is a quiet shoe, and a sneaking suspicion is a feeling kept quiet in the mind.
normal.cn: sneaker 是一双安静的鞋，而 sneaking suspicion 是压在心里的感觉。

normal.en: Compare creep: creep suggests slow crawling, sneak adds the intention of not being caught.
normal.cn: 对比 creep：creep 偏缓慢爬行，sneak 更强调「不想被抓住」的意图。

abstract.en: Picture a shadow sliding along a wall at the end of the corridor.
abstract.cn: 想象走廊尽头有一道影子贴着墙滑过去。

abstract.en: Imagine a hand lifting a book from a shelf and putting it back without a sound.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手从书架上拿下书，又悄无声息地放回去。

abstract.en: Think of a whisper passed from mouth to ear along a row of desks.
abstract.cn: 想象一排课桌上，一句耳语从一张嘴传到一只耳朵。

examples.en: They sneaked into the garden to watch the fireflies.
examples.cn: 他们悄悄溜进花园去看萤火虫。

examples.en: Nobody likes a sneak who reports every mistake.
examples.cn: 没人喜欢一个见错就打小报告的人。

examples.en: The magazine gave readers a sneak peek at the new model.
examples.cn: 杂志让读者抢先看了一眼新款车型。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「斯ni克」——斯文地、捏着脚尖、克住声音：这就是偷偷地走；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语旧动词 snican（爬行、潜行）一般认为同源，但现代拼写与确切来源仍不确定；一些学者把 sneak 与英语 snack、snatch 联系起来，可视为「悄无声息」这一核心义扩展开来，形成 sneak out、sneak peek、sneaker 等词族。

sensesIntro.en: Sneak starts as a quiet creeping step, then becomes secret action, then a creeping person, and finally a look, a sudden jolt and a smile that arrives unseen.
sensesIntro.cn: sneak 从「静静地挪一步」开始，接着是「背着人做」，再是「鬼祟的人」，最后又落在一瞥、突然的震颤和悄悄出现的笑容上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a shadow pressed against a wall, moving without a sound.
core.cn: 核心意象：贴墙的影子，一点声音也不带地挪动。

branches.en: Creeping along quietly is the oldest and most physical sense.
branches.cn: 悄悄爬行是词义最古老、最具体的一层。

branches.en: Doing a thing out of sight is the action sense.
branches.cn: 背着人做事，是动作层面的义项。

branches.en: Both the act of telling and the person who tells are built from the secrecy of the movement.
branches.cn: 告密这个动作和告密的人，都由「秘密移动」生长出来。

branches.en: The quick look, the sudden jolt and the silent smile all share one direction: something arrives before you can see it coming.
branches.cn: 偷看的一眼、突然的震颤、无声的笑容都朝同一个方向：有东西在你察觉之前就到了。

branches.en: A stolen glance and a creeping feeling are both small pieces of the same silent approach.
branches.cn: 偷瞄一眼与悄悄蔓延的感觉，都是同一种无声接近的一小块。

intro.en: Sneak has no useful modern prefix or suffix, and the English family grows from sneaker, sneaky, sneaking and sneaking about.
intro.cn: sneak 没有可拆的现代前后缀，英语词族由 sneaker、sneaky、sneaking 等派生词组成。

latinIntro.en: Sneak has no secure Latin source, so only native English forms are listed here.
latinIntro.cn: sneak 没有可靠的拉丁语来源，所以此处只列出英语本族词形。

items.meaning: to make a small sharp cut sound
items.example: Nicknamed from the sound of a quiet cut, snick kept the whisper of the letters sn.
items.exampleCN: snick 借的是轻轻一割的声音，保留了 sn 两个字母的细响。

items.meaning: a long body without legs that slides along the ground
items.meaningCN: 无腿、贴地滑行的长身动物
items.example: Snake shares the creeping letters, but it is a different word.
items.exampleCN: snake 共享「爬行」的音形，却是另一个词。

items.meaning: to move or act quietly and secretly
items.example: Sneak is the base verb of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: sneak 是整个词族的基础动词。

items.meaning: a person or thing that does
items.example: The suffix -er makes sneaker, the quiet shoe.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -er 构成 sneaker，指安静的鞋。

items.example: The suffix -y makes sneaky, full of stealth.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -y 构成 sneaky，充满鬼祟。

items.example: Sneakily means in a sneaky manner.
items.exampleCN: sneakily 表示鬼鬼祟祟地。

items.example: Sneaking can name the act and describe a hidden feeling.
items.exampleCN: sneaking 既能指这个动作，也能描述隐藏的情绪。

items.meaning: an early secret look at something
items.example: Sneak peek joins the verb to a small secret view.
items.exampleCN: sneak peek 把动词与小小的一瞥连在一起。

items.meaning: an advance showing before the public opening
items.example: Sneak preview describes a showing before everyone else.
items.exampleCN: sneak preview 指在众人之前放映。

definition_zh: 势利的；爱慕虚荣的；摆架子的；装腔作势的
definition_en: behaving as if people of a higher class, wealth or taste are better than others, and looking down on those judged ordinary
core_image: 抬起下巴、只和「同类」搭话的人：目光越过别人的头顶
scene: 同学聚会上，一位新来的客人只和穿名牌的人聊天，对端茶的服务员却连一句谢谢都不愿说。The snobbish guest would not even smile at the waiter.
sceneCN: 这里 snobbish 是「势利的」（第 1 个义项：按出身与财富分等级看人）；句意：这位势利的客人连对服务员笑一下都不肯。图中可辨识物件：聚会餐桌、名牌手袋、托盘。

pos.zh: 装腔作势的；附庸风雅的

derivatives.zh: 加 -ish 之前的基础词，义为「势利眼；自命不凡的人」，本词由它构成
由 snob 加 -ery 构成，义为「势利；势利的言行」
由本词加 -ly 构成，义为「势利地」
由本词加 -ness 构成，义为「势利的性格」
非同一词源，义为「目中无人的；自高自大的」，常与 snobbish 通用

senses.title: Looking down on people of lower rank
senses.definition: treating people with less money or lower social rank as if they do not matter
senses.definitionCN: 把金钱较少、社会地位较低的人当作无足轻重
senses.example: The snobbish waiter ignored us because we were not wearing suits.
senses.exampleCN: 那个势利的侍者因为没穿西装就不理我们。
senses.why: The base word snob shifted from a word for an ordinary person to a word for someone who looks down, so the -ish form names that behavior as a quality.
senses.whyCN: 基础词 snob 从「普通百姓」的意思转成「看不起别人的人」，所以加 -ish 后就把这种做派说成了一种性格。

senses.title: Showing off a high opinion of oneself
senses.definition: behaving as if one is better than the people around one
senses.definitionCN: 表现得自己比身边的人更优越
senses.example: Her snobbish manner made the new team feel unwelcome.
senses.exampleCN: 她爱摆架子的态度让新来的团队觉得自己不受欢迎。
senses.why: A person who sorts the world by rank must also raise their own rank, so looking down and looking up at oneself are two sides of one tilt.
senses.whyCN: 按等级给世界排序的人，必然也要抬高自己的位置；所以「俯视别人」与「抬头看自己」是同一种倾斜的两面。

senses.title: Posing as refined
senses.definition: pretending to belong to a refined or well-informed group by using its taste as a badge
senses.definitionCN: 把某种高雅或内行的品味当成徽章，假装自己属于那个圈子
senses.example: His snobbish taste in wine had less to do with pleasure than with the label.
senses.exampleCN: 他对葡萄酒那种附庸风雅的品味，与其说关乎享受，不如说关乎标签。
senses.why: When taste becomes the marker of social rank, snobbish also describes a refinement that is worn rather than owned.
senses.whyCN: 当品味被当作社会等级的记号时，snobbish 也就用来形容那种挂在身上、并非真正拥有的高雅。

senses.title: Judging places and things by rank
senses.titleCN: 把场所、物品也分出高下
senses.definition: describing a place, school or object as having a class and a claim to status
senses.definitionCN: 把某个地方、学校或物品说成有阶级身份、有档次
senses.example: The snobbish address on the invitation told guests what kind of party it would be.
senses.exampleCN: 请柬上那个尽显身份的地址，已经告诉客人这是什么样的派对。
senses.why: Snobs sort people, but the same eye soon sorts the things around people, so schools, streets and objects pick up the same rank.
senses.whyCN: 势利眼给人们排座次，同一双眼睛很快也会给身边的物事排座次，于是学校、街道、物品都带上了同样的等级。

intro.en: Snobbish comes from snob plus the adjective suffix -ish; the origin of snob itself is uncertain.
intro.cn: snobbish 由 snob 加形容词后缀 -ish 构成；snob 本身的来源不确定。

items.en: Snob is first recorded in the late eighteenth century for a shoemaker or a person without rank, and its origin is uncertain.
items.cn: snob 十八世纪晚期首次见于记录，指鞋匠或没有身份的人，其来源不确定。

items.en: Snob then shifted to a person who despises those thought below them.
items.cn: 之后 snob 的词义转向「看不起别人的人」。

items.en: Adding -ish turns the person noun into a quality: snobbish.
items.cn: 加上 -ish 之后，指人的名词变成了形容词 snobbish。

items.en: Snobbish moves from rank alone to taste, money and manners.
items.cn: snobbish 从只看身份，扩展到品味、金钱与礼仪。

items.en: Short forms such as snobby and noun forms such as snobbery spread in everyday speech.
items.cn: snobby 这类短形式与 snobbery 这类名词形式在日常言语中通行开来。

note.en: Snobbish belongs to the snob family and sits beside words for looking down on others.
note.cn: snobbish 属于 snob 词族，与表示「看不起人」的一组词相邻。

entries.definition: the attitude of a snob

the shorter informal form of snobbish

entries.definition: showing a proud and superior attitude
believing that a small group is naturally superior
entries.definitionCN: 精英主义者的；只认同小圈子的

entries.definition: trying to seem more important or cultured than one is
entries.definitionCN: 装腔作势的；自命不凡的

entries.definition: believing oneself to be better than others

normalIntro.en: Snobbish is snob plus the quality suffix -ish, so the whole word is one person turned into a permanent manner.
normalIntro.cn: snobbish 就是 snob 加上表示性质的后缀 -ish，整词等于把一个人固定成一种做派。

normal.en: The suffix -ish in English usually means having the quality of, as in childish and selfish.
normal.cn: 英语后缀 -ish 通常表示「具有某种性质」，如 childish、selfish。

normal.en: Snobbery is the attitude, snobbish is how a person behaves.
normal.cn: snobbery 是态度，snobbish 是人的行为方式。

normal.en: Snobbish often takes about: snobbish about wine, music or clothes.
normal.cn: snobbish 常跟 about 连用，如对酒、音乐或衣服很势利。

normal.en: Snobby is the casual short form of the same word.
normal.cn: snobby 是同一个词的口语短形式。

normal.en: Compare arrogant: arrogant is about pride, snobbish is about rank and class.
normal.cn: 对比 arrogant：arrogant 讲的是骄傲，snobbish 讲的是等级与阶级。

abstract.en: Picture a chin so high that it looks over the heads of other people.
abstract.cn: 想象一个高抬到能越过别人头顶的下巴。

abstract.en: Imagine a guest counting the brands on every coat in the room.
abstract.cn: 想象一位客人把满屋外套上的牌子逐一数过。

abstract.en: Think of a wine glass held up only to be photographed.
abstract.cn: 想象一只高脚杯举起来只是为了被拍照。

examples.en: His snobbish remarks about the town were hard to forget.
examples.cn: 他对这个镇子那些势利的话让人很难忘记。

examples.en: The hotel has a snobbish reputation among young travelers.
examples.cn: 这家酒店在年轻旅客中名声势利。

examples.en: It sounds snobbish to say that cheap shoes make a person dull.
examples.cn: 说便宜的鞋子会让人显得平庸，听起来很势利。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「斯诺比许」——斯文地「诺」一声就低头，却暗「比」谁更有「许」多钱：这就是势利；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: snob 加形容词后缀 -ish（具有……性质的）。snob 十八世纪晚期首次见于记录，原指鞋匠或没有身份的人，十九世纪转指「看不起地位较低者的人」；snob 的更早来源不确定。由此派生 snobbish、snobbery、snobby。

sensesIntro.en: Snobbish starts with rank and class, then grows into self importance, then into borrowed taste, and finally into judging places and objects.
sensesIntro.cn: snobbish 先从身份与阶级开始，再长出「自命不凡」，又扩展到「借来的品味」，最后落到对场所与物品的评头品足。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a raised chin that looks over the heads of other people.
core.cn: 核心意象：高抬的下巴，目光越过别人的头顶。

branches.en: Sorting people by rank is the base sense.
branches.cn: 按等级给人排队是基础义项。

branches.en: The same tilt that looks down also keeps the self high.
branches.cn: 同一次倾斜既是俯视别人，也把自己的位置抬高。

branches.en: Rank and taste are badges people use to place others, and both can be worn rather than owned.
branches.cn: 身份与品味都是用来给别人定位置的标记，而两者都可能是挂着而非真正拥有的。

branches.en: The ranking eye moves from people to the places and objects around them.
branches.cn: 那双排座次的眼睛，从人转向了人周围的场所与物品。

branches.en: Self importance and judging an address share the same yardstick of rank.
branches.cn: 自命不凡与评判一个住址，用的是同一把身份的尺子。

intro.en: Snobbish splits cleanly into the noun snob and the quality suffix -ish, and the family spreads through snobbery, snobbishly and snobbishness.
intro.cn: snobbish 可以直接拆成名词 snob 和表示性质的后缀 -ish，词族再派生 snobbery、snobbishly 与 snobbishness。

latinIntro.en: Snobbish has no Latin source; the base word snob is of uncertain origin, so no Latin family is listed here.
latinIntro.cn: snobbish 没有拉丁语来源，基础词 snob 来源不确定，所以此处不列拉丁语同族词。
