definition_zh: 好交际的；友善的；善于社交的；适合交际的
definition_en: willing to talk to other people and enjoy being with them, and of a place or event that makes that easy
core_image: 长桌旁围坐的一圈人：杯沿相碰，身体都朝内倾
scene: 小区门口的咖啡馆总在傍晚热闹起来，邻居们端着杯子互相打招呼，谁也不急着走。Everyone agreed that this sociable café was the best place in the neighbourhood for meeting people.
sceneCN: 这里 sociable 是「适合交际的」（第 3 个义项：场所或场合让人容易亲近）；句意：大家都同意这家好交际的咖啡馆是社区里碰面交流的最佳去处。图中可辨识物件：咖啡馆、长桌、杯子、门口。

pos.zh: 好交际的；合群的；友善的
爱社交的；善于与人交往的
适合交际的；气氛融洽的

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ity 构成，义为「合群的性情；社交能力」
加否定前缀 un- 构成，义为「不爱交际的；不友善的」
由本词加 -ly 构成，义为「友善地；善于交际地」
与 sociable 同源于 socius，义为「社会的；社交的」，但侧重群体关系而非合群的性情
由同一词根 soci- 加后缀 -ize 构成，义为「社交；使社会化」

senses.title: Fond of being with other people
senses.definition: enjoying the company of other people and willing to talk with them
senses.definitionCN: 喜欢与他人相处，也愿意和人说话
senses.example: As a sociable child, she made friends within the first week of school.
senses.exampleCN: 她从小就好交际，开学第一周就交到了朋友。
senses.why: The Latin root means a companion, so a sociable person is literally the one who wants and seeks companions.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根意为「同伴」，所以 sociable 的人字面上就是渴望并寻找同伴的人。

senses.title: Friendly and easy to talk to
senses.definition: friendly and relaxed in the way one greets and receives other people
senses.definitionCN: 在与人打招呼、接待他人时显得友好而放松
senses.example: The porter was so sociable that every guest left knowing his name.
senses.exampleCN: 门房十分友善，每位客人在离开时都知道了他的名字。
senses.why: Seeking company turns outward as behavior, so the inner wish becomes a visible manner of greeting.
senses.whyCN: 「寻找同伴」的心愿向外落到行为上，于是内在的愿望变成了看得见的神情与招呼。

senses.title: Suited to company
senses.titleCN: 适合交际的；气氛融洽的
senses.definition: of a place, event or hour, suited to friendly meeting and talk
senses.definitionCN: 指地方、场合或时间适合友好见面交谈
senses.example: The wide kitchen was the most sociable room in the house.
senses.exampleCN: 这间宽敞的厨房是屋里最适合大家聚在一起说话的地方。
senses.why: If a person is the kind of company people want, then a place that invites the same company shares the same word.
senses.whyCN: 既然「会带来同伴」是人的特点，那么会把人聚到一起的地方自然也用同一个词。

senses.title: Fond of social gatherings
senses.definition: enjoying parties, dinners and other occasions when people meet in groups
senses.definitionCN: 喜欢派对、宴席以及人们成群相聚的场合
senses.example: Most sociable adults in the block came to the dinner every month.
senses.exampleCN: 那栋楼里大多数爱参加聚会的成年人每月都来赴宴。
senses.why: The companion root also names the gathering itself, so the person who loves these gatherings is described with the same quality word.
senses.whyCN: 「同伴」词根同时指相聚这件事本身，所以爱上聚会的人也沿用同一个表示性质的词。

intro.en: Sociable comes from Latin socius, a companion, through the Latin adjective socialis and its French descendant.
intro.cn: sociable 来自拉丁语 socius（同伴），经由拉丁语形容词 socialis 及其法语后裔进入英语。

items.en: Agreeing on the reconstructed root is not certain; generally it is taken to mean to follow, giving the Latin word for companion.
items.cn: 重构词根意为「跟随」，由此产生拉丁语的「同伴」。

items.en: Socius means a partner or companion, and socialis means of companions.
items.cn: socius 意为伙伴、同伴，socialis 意为「同伴的」。

items.en: French social means friendly toward others and passes into English use.
items.cn: 法语 social 表示「对他人友好的」，进入英语使用。

items.en: Sociable appears in English for life lived with companions.
items.cn: 英语里 sociable 出现，指与同伴一起过的生活。

items.en: The word widens to friendly manners, good company and suitable places.
items.cn: 这个词扩展到友好的举止、值得交往的人以及适合交流的场所。

items.en: Modern English uses sociable for people, animals, places and hours.
items.cn: 现代英语用 sociable 描写人、动物、地方与时间。

note.en: Sociable grows from the Latin companion root soci- and sits near words for openness toward other people.
note.cn: sociable 由拉丁语表示同伴的词根 soci- 长成，与一群表示「对人敞开」的词相邻。

entries.definition: relating to society and to living with other people
entries.definitionCN: 与人类社会及群体生活有关的

entries.definition: the quality of being sociable
not wanting to be with other people
to spend time with others in a friendly way
entries.definitionCN: 友善地与人共度时光；社交

entries.definition: the study of society and social relationships
entries.definitionCN: 研究社会与社会关系之学

entries.definition: behaving in a kind and pleasant way to others
confident and eager to meet other people
entries.definitionCN: 开朗主动、喜欢结识他人的

entries.definition: enjoying the company of a crowd or group
a person who draws energy from being with others
entries.definitionCN: 从与人相处中获取活力的人

normalIntro.en: Sociable is built on the Latin companion root soci-, the same root that gives social, society and associate.
normalIntro.cn: sociable 建立在拉丁语「同伴」词根 soci- 上，社会、社团、结交这些词也与它同源。

normal.en: The suffix -able means able to, so sociable is able to be with companions.
normal.cn: 后缀 -able 表示「能够的」，所以 sociable 就是「能够与人相伴」。

normal.en: Social names the group, sociable names the temper that seeks the group.
normal.cn: social 说的是群体，sociable 说的是愿意走近群体的性情。

normal.en: Compare unsociable with antisocial: the first avoids company, the second harms society.
normal.cn: 对比 unsociable 与 antisocial：前者回避交往，后者危害社会。

normal.en: A sociable hour is a fixed time set aside for tea and talk at work.
normal.cn: sociable hour 指工作场所专门留出喝茶闲聊的固定时间。

normal.en: Many ethology texts call a dog sociable when it seeks people and other dogs.
normal.cn: 在动物行为学文字里，主动找人和找同类的狗常被称作 sociable。

abstract.en: Picture a ring of chairs turned slightly inward so that the shoulders all face the middle.
abstract.cn: 想象一圈椅子微微朝内摆，每一边肩膀都朝向中间。

abstract.en: Imagine a hand raised in greeting before the door is even fully open.
abstract.cn: 想象门还没完全打开，一只手已经举起来打招呼。

abstract.en: Think of a long kitchen table where a plate is always within reach of a new guest.
abstract.cn: 想象一张长厨房桌，新来的客人总能随手够到一个盘子。

examples.en: He is sociable enough to chat with anyone at the bus stop.
examples.cn: 他很好交际，在公交站谁都能聊上几句。

examples.en: The village is quiet but its people are sociable and welcoming.
examples.cn: 这个村子很安静，但村民们友善合群、乐于待人。

examples.en: Sociability and patience help new neighbours settle in quickly.
examples.cn: 合群的性情与耐心能让新邻居很快安定下来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「搜社博」——到处「搜」话题、跟谁都能「社」交、「博」一聊：这就是好交际；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 socius（同伴、伙伴）→ socialis（同伴的）→ 法语 social → 英语 sociable，再加后缀 -able（能够……的），核心义「能与同伴相处」。同根词还有 social、society、associate。

sensesIntro.en: Sociable starts as the wish for companions, shows as a friendly manner, spreads to places and hours suited to meeting, and finally to the lover of gatherings.
sensesIntro.cn: sociable 先是对同伴的渴望，表现为友善的举止，再扩展到适合相聚的地方与时间，最后指爱参加聚会的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a ring of people around a long table, bodies turned inward.
core.cn: 核心意象：长桌旁围坐的人群，身体都朝内倾。

branches.en: Wanting to be with others is the innermost layer.
branches.cn: 愿意与人相处，是最内里的一层。

branches.en: The friendly manner is the wish made visible.
branches.cn: 友善的举止是这个愿望变得可见。

branches.en: Places and hours that invite the same company share the word.
branches.cn: 会把人聚到一起的地方与时光，也共用这个词。

branches.en: A sociable person both enjoys others and is easy to approach.
branches.cn: 好交际的人既喜欢和别人在一起，也容易让人接近。

branches.en: The sociable room and the lover of gatherings both point at the same meeting of companions.
branches.cn: 适合交际的房间与爱聚会的人，都指向同样的「同伴相聚」。

intro.en: Sociable joins the Latin root soci- for companion to the suffix -able for capable, and the family runs through social, socialize, sociability and unsociable.
intro.cn: sociable 把拉丁语词根 soci-（同伴）与表示「能够」的后缀 -able 接在一起，词族延伸到 social、socialize、sociability 与 unsociable。

latinIntro.en: Latin socius and socialis give English sociable both its companion root and its adjective shape.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 socius 与 socialis 为 sociable 提供了「同伴」词根和形容词形态。

items.example: The root soci- appears in social, society and associate.
items.exampleCN: 词根 soci- 见于 social、society 与 associate。

items.example: The suffix -able makes the root into an ability.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -able 把词根变成一种能力。

items.example: Sociable keeps the root and the suffix together.
items.exampleCN: sociable 保留了词根与后缀。

items.example: The suffix -ity forms sociability.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ity 构成 sociability。

items.example: The prefix un- forms unsociable.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 un- 构成 unsociable。

items.example: Sociably means in a sociable manner.
items.exampleCN: sociably 表示以友善好交往的方式。

items.example: Social drops the suffix and keeps the group meaning.
items.exampleCN: social 去掉后缀，保留「群体」的意思。

items.example: The suffix -ize forms socialize.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ize 构成 socialize。

items.example: The suffix -ology forms sociology.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ology 构成 sociology。

items.meaning: a set work time for tea and talk
items.meaningCN: 公司里固定的喝茶交谈时间
items.example: Sociable hour turns the adjective into a fixed occasion.
items.exampleCN: sociable hour 把形容词变成固定的场合。

definition_zh: 钠（一种银白色软金属）；钠离子；食盐中的钠成分
definition_en: a soft silver-white metal that is part of salt and is essential in small amounts for the body
core_image: 一块银亮的软金属被切开，断面很快蒙上一层白白的氧化膜
scene: 打卤面的汤面上摆着一小碟食盐，旁边的包装袋印着一个陌生的化学单词。A small dish of table salt sat beside the noodles, and the packet in front of it read sodium, the metal hidden inside the salt.
sceneCN: 这里 sodium 是「钠」（第 1 个义项：一种银白色软金属）；句意：面前放着一小碟食盐，包装袋上写着 sodium，也就是藏在盐里的那种金属。

derivatives.zh: 由 sodium 去词尾 -ium 加 -ic 构成，义为「含钠的；钠的」
同源词，义为「苏打；钠盐类化合物」
由 sodium 加 -free 构成的复合形容词，义为「无钠的」

senses.title: The metal itself
senses.definition: a soft, silver-white metallic element that reacts violently with water and must be kept away from the air
senses.definitionCN: 一种柔软、银白色的金属元素，遇水剧烈反应，必须与空气隔开保存
senses.example: Sodium is stored under oil because the air would spoil it.
senses.exampleCN: 钠保存在油里，因为空气会腐蚀它。
senses.why: The name cuts sodium into soda, read back from an old name for caustic soda, and the ending -ium, the Latin vowel sign that chemists borrowed for metals.
senses.whyCN: 名字可拆成 soda 与词尾 -ium：soda 来自旧名词「苛性苏打」的前半，-ium 是化学家们取自拉丁语的「金属元素」标记，所以钠就是「苏打里的金属」。

senses.title: The element in salt
senses.definition: the element as it appears in common salt, written sodium chloride in chemistry
senses.definitionCN: 这一元素在食盐中的存在形式，化学上写作氯化钠
senses.example: Sea salt is mostly sodium chloride.
senses.exampleCN: 海盐的主要成分是氯化钠。
senses.why: Sodium is never found loose in nature; it is always bonded as a positive ion, so in everyday speech the word simply means the sodium inside salt.
senses.whyCN: 自然界的钠从不单独存在，它总是带正电与其他离子结合，因此日常说法里 sodium 直接指「盐里的钠」。

senses.title: Sodium in the body
senses.definition: the mineral the body needs in small amounts to keep water and nerves in balance
senses.definitionCN: 人体少量需要、用来维持水分与神经平衡的矿物质
senses.example: Doctors check the sodium level in a patient blood test.
senses.exampleCN: 医生会在血液检查中测病人的钠水平。
senses.why: The body runs on charged ions, and sodium is the most common one outside cells, so the word spread from chemistry into medicine.
senses.whyCN: 身体依赖带电离子运转，而钠是细胞外最常见的离子，于是这个词从化学走进了医学。

senses.title: Sodium in food labels
senses.definition: the salt content printed on food packaging, often counted in grams or milligrams
senses.definitionCN: 食品包装上标出的含盐量，通常以克或毫克计算
senses.example: This soup is marked low in sodium, so it suits her diet.
senses.exampleCN: 这款汤标着「钠含量低」，适合她的饮食。
senses.why: Because salt is mostly sodium, food science measures the salt in a product by its sodium, turning the element into a label number.
senses.whyCN: 由于盐的主要成分就是钠，食品科学便用钠来计量产品的含盐量，把这个元素变成了标签上的数字。

intro.en: Sodium was coined in modern chemistry from soda, an older word for caustic soda and soda ash, plus the element ending -ium.
intro.cn: sodium 是现代化学造的新词，由 soda（旧称的苏打、纯碱）加元素词尾 -ium 构成。

items.en: Soda appears in herbal and alchemical writing, most likely through Arabic, for alkaline salts.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语中出现 soda，多认为经由阿拉伯语传入，指碱性盐。

items.en: Soda names the ash of certain plants used in glass making.
items.cn: 意大利语的 soda 指用于制玻璃的某些植物灰烬。

items.en: Soda enters English meaning soda ash, the impure alkali from burned plants.
items.cn: soda 进入英语，指植物焚烧后得到的纯碱。

items.en: Humphry Davy isolates the metal and gives it the new Latin form sodium.
items.cn: 汉弗里·戴维分离出这种金属，并造出新拉丁语形式 sodium。

items.en: Sodium passes into standard English as the name of the element.
items.cn: sodium 作为元素名称进入标准英语。

note.en: Sodium sits near its chemical family (soda, sodic) and near the everyday salt words.
note.cn: sodium 一边连着化学词族（soda、sodic），一边连着日常的「盐」类词。

entries.definition: sodium carbonate or a fizzy drink
containing sodium
a similar soft metal named from potash
entries.definitionCN: 钾，由「钾灰」命名，与钠同为软金属

entries.definition: a white substance used to flavour food
containing salt
a compound of chlorine that sodium forms in salt
entries.definitionCN: 氯化物，钠在食盐中与之结合

normalIntro.en: The name is a recipe: soda plus the element ending -ium makes sodium, the metal of soda.
normalIntro.cn: 这个名字像一份配方：soda 加上元素词尾 -ium 就是 sodium，即「苏打里的金属」。

normal.en: Sodium is the metal that forms the soda of soda ash, hence the -ium ending.
normal.cn: sodium 即构成苏打的金属，所以加了 -ium 词尾。

normal.en: Sodium chloride is the chemical name for common table salt.
normal.cn: sodium chloride 就是食盐的化学名称。

normal.en: Potassium shares the same soft metal ending and sits right below sodium in the table.
normal.cn: potassium 用同样的软金属词尾，在元素表里紧邻钠的下方。

normal.en: A low-sodium label means the food has little salt.
normal.cn: low-sodium 标签表示食品含盐很少。

normal.en: Sodium lamp light is the orange glow of many old street lights.
normal.cn: sodium lamp 钠灯的光就是许多老路灯那种橙黄色。

abstract.en: Picture a knife slicing a silver lump that dulls in seconds.
abstract.cn: 想象刀切开一块银亮金属，几秒钟后断面就发暗了。

abstract.en: Imagine a salt shaker with a metal piece hiding inside each grain.
abstract.cn: 想象盐罐里每一粒盐都藏着一小块金属。

abstract.en: Think of an orange lamp blinking above a lonely road at night.
abstract.cn: 想象夜里一盏橙色钠灯在空荡荡的路上闪烁。

examples.en: Sodium burns brightly when it touches water.
examples.cn: 钠遇水会剧烈燃烧、发出亮光。

examples.en: Nutritionists advise us to cut down on sodium.
examples.cn: 营养师建议我们减少钠的摄入。

examples.en: The lab keeps its sodium under a layer of oil.
examples.cn: 实验室把钠存放在一层油下面。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「苏的」——苏打（soda）里抢出来的那种金属，就是「苏的」金属；这只是谐音联想，词源实为 soda 加 -ium。

root: soda（苏打、纯碱，中世纪拉丁语 soda，一般认为经阿拉伯语而来）+ -ium（拉丁语金属词尾）；1807 年由戴维命名。

sensesIntro.en: Sodium starts as a named metal, moves into the salt people eat, then into the mineral the body needs and the number on food labels.
sensesIntro.cn: sodium 先是化学上的金属名称，再指人们吃的盐里的成分，最后延伸到身体需要的矿物质和食品标签上的数值。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a soft silver metal hidden inside a grain of salt.
core.cn: 核心意象：一粒盐里藏着的银白色软金属。

branches.en: Sense 4 builds on the same image as sense 3.
branches.cn: 第 4 个义项由第 3 个义项的意象延伸而来。

branches.en: Sense 4: the same metal now rides inside a salt crystal.
branches.cn: 第 4 个义项：同一块金属此刻藏在盐的晶体里。

branches.en: Sense 4: the salt ion is read as a mineral the body counts.
branches.cn: 第 4 个义项：把盐里的离子读成身体要计量的矿物质。

branches.en: Sense 4: the mineral turns into a printed value on packaging.
branches.cn: 第 4 个义项：矿物质变成包装上印出的数值。

branches.en: Sense 4: the number on the label now guides a daily choice.
branches.cn: 第 4 个义项：标签上的数值最终指导日常的选择。

intro.en: Sodium is a built word: soda plus the element ending -ium, with sodic and sodium-free grown from it.
intro.cn: sodium 是人造构词：soda 加元素词尾 -ium，后来长出 sodic 与 sodium-free。

latinIntro.en: Soda is a medieval Latin alkali word, and -ium is the Latin-derived ending chemists use for metals.
latinIntro.cn: soda 是中世纪拉丁语的碱类词，-ium 是化学家借拉丁语表示金属的词尾。

items.meaning: soda ash or a fizzy drink
items.example: Soda is the word sodium was made from.
items.exampleCN: soda 是造出 sodium 的基础词。

items.example: The ending -ium marks calcium and sodium alike.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ium 同样用于 calcium 与 sodium。

items.example: The suffix -ic turns soda into sodic.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ic 把 soda 变成 sodic。

items.example: Sodic describes rocks rich in sodium.
items.exampleCN: sodic 描述富含钠的岩石。

items.example: Sodium was named after soda in 1807.
items.exampleCN: sodium 于 1807 年依 soda 命名。

items.meaningCN: 两种元素构成的化合物词尾
items.example: Chlorine plus -ide gives chloride in sodium chloride.
items.exampleCN: 氯加词尾 -ide 构成氯化钠中的 chloride。

items.meaning: salt or ester of an acid
items.example: The suffix -ate forms carbonate and bicarbonate.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ate 构成 carbonate 与 bicarbonate。

items.example: Sodium chloride is ordinary salt.
items.exampleCN: sodium chloride 就是普通食盐。

items.example: The suffix -free forms sodium-free.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -free 构成 sodium-free。

items.example: Sodium itself is the headword of this family.
items.exampleCN: sodium 是本词族的中心词。

definition_zh: 逗留；旅居；暂住；短暂的停留
definition_en: a temporary stay in a place other than home, or to stay there for a time
core_image: 旅人把行李放在客栈一角的矮桌上，坐下歇一程，心里知道这里只住一阵
scene: 学者在异国的图书馆里做了几年研究，临走时写信说这段日子只是暂住。The scholar spent three years in a foreign library and wrote home that the sojourn had never felt like home.
sceneCN: 这里 sojourn 是「旅居、暂住」（第 1 个义项：在外地短期的停留）；句意：学者在异国的图书馆待了三年，写信回家说这段旅居始终不像家。

collocations.zh: 在……逗留（动词）；在……的旅居（名词）

derivatives.zh: 由 sojourn 加 -er 构成，义为「旅居者；暂住者」
由 sojourn 加 -ment 构成，义为「逗留；旅居」

senses.title: To stay for a while
senses.definition: to live in a place for a period of time as a visitor rather than as a resident
senses.definitionCN: 作为访客在一个地方住上一段时间，而不是定居
senses.example: They sojourned in Florence while he studied painting.
senses.exampleCN: 他学画期间，他们旅居在佛罗伦萨。
senses.why: The Old French verb sojourner means to pass a day, built from sous, under or for, and journee, a day, so the word is literally to spend a day somewhere.
senses.whyCN: 古法语动词 sojourner 意为「度过一天」，由 sous（在……之下、为期）与 journee（一天）构成，所以这个词字面上就是「在某地过一天」。

senses.title: A temporary stay
senses.definition: a period spent living in a place that is not home, usually short and expected to end
senses.definitionCN: 在家以外的地方居住的一段时间，通常较短且注定结束
senses.example: Her sojourn in the mountains lasted two months.
senses.exampleCN: 她在山里的暂住持续了两个月。
senses.why: From the verb came the noun: the day or days spent somewhere became the sojourn itself.
senses.whyCN: 名词由动词而来：在某地度过的那一天或那些天，就成了「逗留」本身。

senses.title: A formal word in writing
senses.definition: a stay described in formal or literary style, often with a sense of purpose
senses.definitionCN: 以正式或文学笔调描述的停留，常带有目的感
senses.example: The poet wrote of his sojourn among strangers.
senses.exampleCN: 诗人写下了他在陌生人中间的那段日子。
senses.why: Because the word is old and formal, it survives mostly in travel writing and memoir, where a stay is given weight.
senses.whyCN: 由于这个词古老而正式，它主要存活于游记和回忆录中，让一次停留显得有分量。

senses.title: A long stay away from home
senses.definition: an extended stay in another country or region, especially for study or work
senses.definitionCN: 在异国或外地较长时间的居住，尤指为学习或工作
senses.example: His sojourn abroad taught him two languages.
senses.exampleCN: 他的旅居生活让他学会了两门语言。
senses.why: When the brief day stretches into months, sojourn takes on the modern sense of an expatriate stay.
senses.whyCN: 当短暂的一天延长成几个月，sojourn 就获得了「旅外居住」的现代含义。

intro.en: Sojourn comes through Old French sojourner, to pass the day, from jours, days, which goes back to Latin diurnus, daily.
intro.cn: sojourn 经古法语 sojourner（度日）而来，源头 jours（日子）可追到拉丁语 diurnus（每日的）。

items.en: Diurnus means daily, from dies, a day; it is also the source of diurnal.
items.cn: 拉丁语 diurnus 意为「每日的」，来自 dies（日），也是 diurnal 的来源。

items.en: The Latin daily word becomes nothing but another word for a day.
items.cn: 这个拉丁词在罗曼语土壤里逐渐只剩「一天」的意思。

items.en: Journee means a day, and sojourner means to pass a day in a place.
items.cn: 古法语 journee 指一天，sojourner 指在某地度过一天。

items.en: Sojourn enters English for a temporary stay.
items.cn: sojourn 以「暂住、逗留」之义进入中古英语。

items.en: The word narrows to formal and literary use for a stay away from home.
items.cn: 现代英语里这个词收窄到正式和文学语境，指离家在外的一段居住。

note.en: Sojourn is a day word beside journey and journal, and a stay word beside visit, residence, and stopover.
note.cn: sojourn 一边是和 journey、journal 同源的「日子」词，一边是和 visit、residence、stopover 相邻的「停留」词。

entries.definition: a trip from one place to another
a daily record or periodical
happening every day or in daytime
a period of living somewhere temporarily
a short time spent with a person or in a place
the fact of living in a place, often long term

normalIntro.en: Sojourn is built on a day: French jours gives the same root as journey, so a sojourn is the days you spend somewhere.
normalIntro.cn: sojourn 建在「日」上：法语的 jours 与 journey 同源，所以 sojourn 就是你在某地度过的那几天。

normal.en: Sojourn shares its day root with journey, both going back to Latin diurnus.
normal.cn: sojourn 与 journey 共享「日」的词根，都可追到拉丁语 diurnus。

normal.en: Journal keeps the daily record made of the same root.
normal.cn: journal 保留了这个词根「每日记录」之意。

normal.en: Sojourn in a city means to stay there a while, not to settle.
normal.cn: sojourn in 某地，指在那里住一阵，而不是安家。

normal.en: A sojourner is the person making the stay.
normal.cn: sojourner 就是进行这段旅居的人。

normal.en: Compare stay, which is plain and everyday, while sojourn is formal and literary.
normal.cn: 对比 stay：stay 平实日常，sojourn 正式且带文学色彩。

abstract.en: Picture a folder marked thirty days and a room that is already packing up.
abstract.cn: 想象一个写着「三十天」的文件夹，和一间已经在收拾行李的房间。

abstract.en: Imagine a scholar with one suitcase who never buys a bookcase.
abstract.cn: 想象一位只带一只箱子、从不买家书架的学者。

abstract.en: Think of a map pin with a small clock beside it, not a flag.
abstract.cn: 想象地图上的图钉旁边挂着一个小闹钟，而不是一面旗。

examples.en: We sojourned briefly in Rome before heading south.
examples.cn: 我们在罗马短暂逗留后继续南下。

examples.en: His sojourn in the capital changed his plans.
examples.cn: 他在首都的这段旅居改变了他的计划。

examples.en: The novel describes a lonely sojourn in the Alps.
examples.cn: 这部小说描写了一段在阿尔卑斯山的孤独旅居。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「搜着」——到一个新地方，边「搜着」探店边住上一阵，就是旅居；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 diurnus（每日的，来自 dies「日」）→ 古法语 journee（一天）+ sojourner（度日）→ 英语 sojourn，核心义「在某地度过一些日子」。

sensesIntro.en: Sojourn begins as a verb for spending days somewhere, becomes a noun for the stay itself, and settles into formal writing for long stays abroad.
sensesIntro.cn: sojourn 起先是「在某地度日」的动词，转为指停留本身的名词，最后在书面语里专指旅居外地的长住。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a traveller who stays a few weeks and never fills the shelves.
core.cn: 核心意象：旅人只住几周，书架始终空着。

branches.en: Sense 2 extends the stay image of sense 1.
branches.cn: 第 2 个义项由第 1 个义项的「停留」画面延伸而来。

branches.en: Sense 2: the day spent becomes the stay itself.
branches.cn: 第 2 个义项：度过的日子变成了停留本身。

branches.en: Sense 3 extends the stay image of sense 2.
branches.cn: 第 3 个义项由第 2 个义项的「停留」画面延伸而来。

branches.en: Sense 4 extends the stay image of sense 3.
branches.cn: 第 4 个义项由第 3 个义项的「停留」画面延伸而来。

branches.en: Sense 4: a short stay is the ordinary fact with no ceremony.
branches.cn: 第 4 个义项：短暂的停留只是不带仪式感的平常事实。

intro.en: Sojourn is a short family: sojourner for the person and sojournment for the act, all on the French day root.
intro.cn: sojourn 词族不大：sojourner 指人，sojournment 指行为，都建在法语「日子」词根上。

latinIntro.en: The root is Latin diurnus, daily, from dies, day, which also gives journey and journal.
latinIntro.cn: 词根是拉丁语 diurnus（每日的），来自 dies（日），journey 与 journal 也出自这里。

items.example: The French day word jour sits inside the root.
items.exampleCN: 法语的「日」是这个词根的内核。

items.meaning: a day, a day of travel
items.example: Journee gives the day sense of the word.
items.exampleCN: journee 提供这个词的「一天」含义。

items.example: Sojourner is the verb behind sojourn.
items.exampleCN: sojourner 是 sojourn 背后的动词。

items.example: The suffix -er forms sojourner.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -er 构成 sojourner。

items.meaning: a person who stays for a time
items.example: Sojourner names the temporary resident.
items.exampleCN: sojourner 指临时的居住者。

items.example: The suffix -ment forms sojournment.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ment 构成 sojournment。

items.example: The same -ure ending appears in departure.
items.exampleCN: 同样的 -ure 词尾也见于 departure。

items.example: Diurnus is the oldest layer of the word.
items.exampleCN: diurnus 是这个词最古老的一层。

items.example: Sojourn itself names the stay the whole family describes.
items.exampleCN: sojourn 本身指这个词族所说的那段停留。

definition_zh: 请求；恳求；征求；招揽（生意）；引发（反应）
definition_en: to ask someone for something in a formal or persistent way, or to try to get business, help, or a reaction
core_image: 一个人坐立不安地来回走动，终于上前开口：能不能请您帮个忙？
scene: 开学第一天，学生会成员守在教学楼门口，请路过的同学为募捐箱投一点钱。On the first day of term, students stood by the gate and began to solicit donations from everyone who passed.
sceneCN: 这里 solicit 是「征求、募求」（第 1 个义项：正式地请求获得某物）；句意：开学第一天，学生们站在校门口，开始向每一位路过的人募捐。

derivatives.zh: 由 solicit 加 -ation 构成，义为「请求；征求；招揽」
由 solicit 加 -or 构成，义为「事务律师；推销员」
同源形容词，义为「关切的；殷切的」

senses.title: To ask for something formally
senses.definition: to ask for money, help, opinions, or information in an official or polite way
senses.definitionCN: 以正式或礼貌的方式请求得到金钱、帮助、意见或信息
senses.example: The committee solicited comments from local residents.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会征求了当地居民的意见。
senses.why: Latin sollicitare means to stir up or trouble, built from sollus, whole, and citare, to set in motion, so the image is a mind set in restless motion until it asks.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 sollicitare 意为「搅动、使之不安」，由 sollus（整个）与 citare（推动）构成，意象是一颗被搅得坐立不安、终于开口请求的心。

senses.title: To ask urgently
senses.definition: to beg or plead with someone persistently for something you urgently need
senses.definitionCN: 为急需之物坚持不懈地向某人恳求
senses.example: He solicited their help in the middle of the storm.
senses.exampleCN: 暴风雨中他恳求他们帮忙。
senses.why: From troubling someone came the sense of pressing them until they consent, which is the urgent request.
senses.whyCN: 从「使人不安」引申出「一再施压直到对方答应」，这就是急切的恳求。

senses.title: To seek business
senses.definition: to try to obtain orders or clients, often by approaching people directly
senses.definitionCN: 设法得到订单或客户，常指直接上前向人兜揽
senses.example: The hotel was warned not to solicit on the platform.
senses.exampleCN: 那家旅馆被告诫不准在站台上招揽客人。
senses.why: Commerce turned the polite request into a sales move: you solicit when you approach a stranger for money.
senses.whyCN: 商业把礼貌的请求变成销售动作：主动上前向陌生人要钱，就是 solicit。

senses.title: To invite a response
senses.definition: to cause or invite a reaction, often an unwanted one
senses.definitionCN: 引起或招来某种反应，常指不受欢迎的反应
senses.example: His comments solicited an angry reply from the crowd.
senses.exampleCN: 他的言论招来了人群愤怒的回应。
senses.why: If a request can bring something toward you, then a remark can bring a reaction too, so the word slid from asking to drawing out.
senses.whyCN: 如果请求能把东西引到自己身边，那么一句话也能引来一个反应，于是这个词从「请求」滑向了「招来」。

intro.en: Solicit comes from Latin sollicitare, to stir up or trouble, from sollus, whole, and citare, to set in motion.
intro.cn: solicit 来自拉丁语 sollicitare（搅动、使人不安），由 sollus（整个的）与 citare（推动）构成。

items.en: Sollus means whole, and citare means to call or set in motion.
items.cn: sollus 意为「整个的」，citare 意为「召唤、推动」。

items.en: Sollicitare means to agitate, harass, or plead for something.
items.cn: sollicitare 意为搅动、骚扰，也指为某事物恳求。

items.en: The adjective sollicitus means anxious or troubled, giving solicitous.
items.cn: 形容词 sollicitus 意为忧虑、不安，由此有了 solicitous。

items.en: Soliciter enters French with the sense of urging or requesting.
items.cn: 古法语 soliciter 承袭「催促、请求」之义。

items.en: Solicit appears in English for making requests and seeking support.
items.cn: 中古英语中 solicit 指提出请求、寻求支持。

items.en: Commercial and legal uses add soliciting business and legal solicitation.
items.cn: 现代英语的商业与法律用法增加了「招揽生意」和「法律上的请求」。

note.en: Solicit is one of the cit words: excite, incite, recite, and citation all push something into motion.
note.cn: solicit 是 cit 这一类词之一：excite、incite、recite、citation 都含有「推动」的意思。

entries.definition: a lawyer who advises clients or an agent who seeks orders
showing concern or care
care and anxiety for someone
to ask for something politely
to ask for something with great urgency
to make a written request to an authority

normalIntro.en: Solicit comes from sollicitare, to stir up: the same -cite as excite and incite, all about setting something in motion.
normalIntro.cn: solicit 来自 sollicitare（搅动），与 excite、incite 共有 -cite，都属于「推动起来」。

normal.en: Solicit shares the -cite root with excite, incite, and recite.
normal.cn: solicit 与 excite、incite、recite 共享 -cite 词根。

normal.en: Solicitation is the noun for the act of asking.
normal.cn: solicitation 即「请求、征求」这一行为的名词。

normal.en: A solicitor is one who solicits, either for clients or for orders.
normal.cn: solicitor 字面就是「发出请求的人」。

normal.en: Solicitous keeps the uneasy root: someone so worried for you that they fuss.
normal.cn: solicitous 保留「不安」的词根：为你担心到团团转。

normal.en: Solicit feedback is the formal way to say ask for opinions.
normal.cn: solicit feedback 是「征求反馈」的正式说法。

abstract.en: Picture someone pacing, then stopping to speak because they can wait no longer.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人坐立不安来回踱步，最后停下去开口，因为实在等不下去了。

abstract.en: Imagine a hand held out flat, palm up, waiting for an answer.
abstract.cn: 想象一只摊平伸出的手，掌心朝上，等待回应。

abstract.en: Think of a sales sign moving toward you rather than waiting for you to come.
abstract.cn: 想象一块招牌主动朝你移动，而不是等你走过去。

examples.en: The charity solicits donations every winter.
examples.cn: 这家慈善机构每年冬天募集捐款。

examples.en: She solicited advice from her former teacher.
examples.cn: 她向前任老师征求意见。

examples.en: Shops are not allowed to solicit customers inside the station.
examples.cn: 商店不得在车站内招揽顾客。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「搜 + list」——好比把需求列成一张单子去搜罗、去求人讨要；这只是拆词联想，词源实为拉丁语 sollicitare（搅动）。

root: 拉丁语 sollus（整个的）+ citare（推动、召唤）→ sollicitare（搅动、使人不安、恳求）→ 古法语 soliciter → 英语 solicit，核心义「把人搅动起来、向他讨要」。

sensesIntro.en: Solicit goes from an urgent request, to a persistent plea, to the business of seeking customers, and finally to drawing out a reaction.
sensesIntro.cn: solicit 从正式的请求出发，到急切的恳求，再到招揽生意的求人，最后延伸到「引发反应」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an unsettled mind that must finally speak and ask.
core.cn: 核心意象：心里被搅得坐立不安，终于开口求人。

branches.en: Sense 3 keeps the asking impulse of sense 2.
branches.cn: 第 3 个义项延续了第 2 个义项的「求」的动作。

branches.en: Sense 4 keeps the asking impulse of sense 2.
branches.cn: 第 4 个义项延续了第 2 个义项的「求」的动作。

branches.en: Sense 4: what was asked for comes back as a reaction.
branches.cn: 第 4 个义项：求来的东西以反应的形式返回。

branches.en: Sense 4: the same asking is now weighed by law and policy.
branches.cn: 第 4 个义项：同样的请求开始受法律与规章衡量。

branches.en: Sense 4: the stirred-up mind is quiet at last, the request made.
branches.cn: 第 4 个义项：被搅动的心终于平复，请求已经说出口。

intro.en: Solicit is built from a Latin root meaning to set in motion, and grows solicitation, solicitor, and solicitous.
intro.cn: solicit 建在拉丁语「推动」词根上，长出 solicitation、solicitor 与 solicitous。

latinIntro.en: Latin citare means to call or set in motion; sollus means whole, and together they mean to stir someone up.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 citare 意为召唤、推动，sollus 意为整个的，合起来就是「把人整个搅动起来」。

items.example: The ending -ate carries sollicitare as a verb.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ate 让 sollicitare 成为动词。

items.meaning: to stir up, to plead for
items.example: Sollicitare is the direct source of solicit.
items.exampleCN: sollicitare 是 solicit 的直接来源。

items.example: The suffix -ation forms solicitation.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ation 构成 solicitation。

items.example: Solicitation is the abstract noun of asking.
items.exampleCN: solicitation 是「请求」的抽象名词。

items.example: The suffix -or forms solicitor.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -or 构成 solicitor。

items.meaning: a lawyer or a person who seeks orders
items.example: Solicitor keeps the agent sense.
items.exampleCN: solicitor 保留了「代为请求者」的含义。

items.example: The suffix -ous forms solicitous.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ous 构成 solicitous。

items.example: The suffix -itude forms solicitude.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -itude 构成 solicitude。

items.example: Cite shares the calling root of solicitare.
items.exampleCN: cite 与 solicitare 共享「召唤」词根。

items.example: Solicit itself is the verb at the centre of the family.
items.exampleCN: solicit 是本词族的中心动词。

latinEntries.meaning: to stir up, to plead for
to call, to set in motion

definition_zh: 使凝固；变硬；巩固；确立；具体化
definition_en: to make something hard or firm, or to become hard, firm, or firmly established
core_image: 一锅温热的蜡慢慢冷却，变成一块敲得响的硬饼
scene: 她端着一盆刚熬化的糖浆走向模具，等它冷却、变硬，再切块包装。She carried the tray of melted sugar to the moulds and waited for it to solidify into hard blocks.
sceneCN: 这里 solidify 是「凝固、变硬」（第 3 个义项：从液态变成坚硬的固体）；句意：她端着糖盘走向模具，等着糖浆凝固成坚硬的块。画面里有热气、模具和一块即将定型的糖。

derivatives.zh: 由动词加名词后缀 -ation 构成，义为「凝固；巩固」
基础词，义为「固体的；坚实的；固体」
由形容词 solid 加 -ity 构成，义为「坚固；坚实」
由形容词 solid 加 -ly 构成，义为「稳固地；坚实地」

senses.title: To make a plan or idea firm
senses.definition: to make a plan, idea, or position firmer and more secure, so that it is unlikely to change
senses.definitionCN: 使计划、想法或地位更牢固、更稳固，不易改变
senses.example: The success of the first shop solidified the company as a national brand.
senses.exampleCN: 第一家店的成功使这家公司稳稳立足，成为全国性品牌。
senses.why: From Latin solidus, meaning firm or whole, solid is what holds its shape, and solidify makes a plan hold its shape too.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 solidus 意为「坚实的、完整的」，solida 就是能保持自己形状的东西，所以 solidify 也让计划保持形状、不再动摇。

senses.title: To make agreements or beliefs harder to break
senses.definition: to make a relationship, agreement, or belief stronger and more difficult to break
senses.definitionCN: 使关系、协议或信念更强、更难被打破
senses.example: Their shared work abroad solidified the friendship.
senses.exampleCN: 他们一起在海外工作，这份友谊因此更加牢不可破。
senses.why: A solid thing resists pressure, so making a bond solid means making it resist the pressures that might break it.
senses.whyCN: 固态的东西能承受压力，所以把一段纽带变得「坚固」，就是让它能顶住可能把它扯断的压力。

senses.title: To become a hard solid from liquid
senses.definition: to change from a liquid or soft state into a hard solid
senses.definitionCN: 从液体或柔软状态变成坚硬的固体
senses.example: The molten wax began to solidify as it cooled.
senses.exampleCN: 融化的蜡随着冷却开始凝固。
senses.why: This is the literal layer of the image, and the English verb means to make or become solid in the plainest physical way.
senses.whyCN: 这是核心意象最字面的一层：这个英语动词本义就是使某物「变成固体」，完全照字面讲。

senses.title: To turn an idea into a concrete form
senses.definition: to turn a rough idea or proposal into a clear, concrete plan or form
senses.definitionCN: 把粗略的想法或提议变成清晰、具体的计划或形态
senses.example: We spent the morning solidifying the proposal into a budget.
senses.exampleCN: 我们用了一上午把提案细化成一份预算。
senses.why: Just as liquid sets into a shape, a loose idea solidifies when it takes on a fixed form that others can see and use.
senses.whyCN: 正如液体冷却后固定成某个形状，松散的想法一旦有了别人看得见、用得上的确定形态，也就「凝固」了。

senses.title: To harden into a fixed habit or preference
senses.definition: to become fixed and steady, especially after a period of uncertainty, so that it is not easily changed
senses.definitionCN: 在不确定之后逐渐固定、稳定下来，不易改变
senses.example: By the end of the autumn rain, her mood had solidified into quiet gloom.
senses.exampleCN: 秋雨结束时，她的心情已经固定成一种安静的忧郁。
senses.why: The same setting image moves inward: what was fluid and shifting settles into a steady shape, and then it stays there.
senses.whyCN: 同样的「凝固」意象转向内心：原本流动不定的东西落定成一个稳定形状，之后就停在那里不再变化。

intro.en: Solidify joins the Latin adjective solidus, firm or whole, with the Latin suffix -ify from facere, to make.
intro.cn: solidify 由拉丁语形容词 solidus（坚实的、完整的）加拉丁语后缀 -ify（来自 facere，做、使）组成。

items.en: Solidus means firm, dense, or whole, with no gaps in it.
items.cn: solidus 意为坚实的、致密的、完整的，内部没有空隙。

items.en: Facere means to make or do, and -ficare becomes the verb-forming element.
items.cn: facere 意为做、使，由此形成的 -ficare 成为构词中表示「使……化」的成分。

items.en: Verbs built on the pattern of solidificare turn the adjective into an action.
items.cn: 按 solidificare 这类模式构成的动词，把形容词的「坚硬的」转成动作。

items.en: The combining stem solid- plus the suffix -ify gives a clean technical verb form.
items.cn: 构词词干 solid- 与后缀 -ify 结合，形成简洁的技术动词形态。

items.en: English uses solidify for the chemical change from liquid to solid.
items.cn: 英语用 solidify 指从液体到固体的化学变化。

items.en: Modern English widens it to plans, beliefs, and popularity.
items.cn: 现代英语把它扩展到计划、信念和人气等抽象领域。

note.en: Solidify sits in the family of solid, solidity, and solidification, and stands beside the ordinary freezing and hardening words.
note.cn: solidify 属于 solid、solidity、solidification 这一词族，并与常见的「冻结、硬化」词相邻。

entries.definition: hard and firm, not liquid or hollow
entries.definitionCN: 坚固的；实心的；非液体的

entries.definition: the process of becoming hard or of being made firm
the quality of being hard, firm, or reliable
to become or make hard and unyielding
to become a solid because of cold
to become or make stiff and less flexible

normalIntro.en: Solidify is solid plus the verb suffix -ify, so it is the act of making something solid in the physical or the abstract sense.
normalIntro.cn: solidify 就是 solid 加动词后缀 -ify，意思是把某物变得坚实，既可指物理上的凝固，也可指抽象上的巩固。

normal.en: The base adjective is solid, and -ify adds the idea of making.
normal.cn: 基础形容词是 solid，后缀 -ify 表示「使……」。

normal.en: Solidify into is the usual pattern for a liquid becoming a solid.
normal.cn: solidify into 是液体变成固体的常用搭配。

normal.en: To solidify a relationship is to make it stronger.
normal.cn: solidify a relationship 就是让一段关系更牢固。

normal.en: The noun is solidification, ending in -ation like many verbs of change.
normal.cn: 名词是 solidification，和许多表示变化的动词一样以 -ation 结尾。

normal.en: The past forms are solidified and solidifying, spelled with -ied and -ying.
normal.cn: 过去式与过去分词是 solidified，现在分词是 solidifying，分别是 -ied 和 -ying 结尾。

abstract.en: Picture a company climbing from a small shop to a national name.
abstract.cn: 想象一家公司从一家小店成长为全国品牌。

abstract.en: Picture two friends agreeing to keep in touch every week.
abstract.cn: 想象两个朋友约定每周都要保持联系。

abstract.en: Picture candle wax cooling in a glass as it becomes hard.
abstract.cn: 想象玻璃杯里的蜡烛油冷却，逐渐变硬。

examples.en: The new evidence solidified the theory in the eyes of most researchers.
examples.cn: 新证据在大多数研究者眼中确立了这一理论。

examples.en: Rock formed as the lava cooled and solidified over many years.
examples.cn: 岩浆在多年里冷却凝固，形成了岩石。

examples.en: A clear summary can solidify a vague idea into a workable plan.
examples.cn: 一份清晰的总结能把模糊的想法具体化为可执行的计划。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「搜·立得·饭」——搜一圈就能立得一顿饭，肚子先「凝固」一下；只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 solidus（坚实的、完整的）+ -ificare（使……化，来自 facere 做）→ 中世纪拉丁语动词 → 英语 solidify，核心义「使成为坚实的」。

sensesIntro.en: Solidify begins with making a plan or belief firm, extends to physical hardening and setting, and widens to ideas taking concrete shape.
sensesIntro.cn: solidify 先用来说让计划或信念变得牢固，再扩展到物理上的变硬、凝固，最后泛指想法定形为具体成果。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: warmed wax cooling into a hard, steady block.
core.cn: 核心意象：温热的蜡冷却成一块坚硬稳定的固体。

branches.en: Making a plan firm is the common business and writing sense.
branches.cn: 让计划变得牢固，是商务与写作中最常见的用法。

branches.en: Stronger bonds are the relational sense.
branches.cn: 更牢固的纽带属于关系层面的用法。

branches.en: Physical hardening from liquid is the literal base of the word.
branches.cn: 液体物理凝固变硬是这个词最字面的基础。

branches.en: Turning ideas into form is the creative sense.
branches.cn: 把想法变成形态属于创造层面的用法。

branches.en: Habits and moods that settle into a fixed shape share the cooling image.
branches.cn: 习惯和情绪落定成固定形态，共享同一个「冷却定形」的意象。

intro.en: Solidify is built from the root solid, meaning firm, and the suffix -ify, meaning to make. A few related forms show how productive it is.
intro.cn: solidify 由词根 solid（坚实的）与后缀 -ify（使……）构成，相关的派生形式显示了它的构词能力。

latinIntro.en: Latin solidus means firm or whole, and facere, which supplies -ify, means to make.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 solidus 意为坚实的、完整的，提供 -ify 的 facere 意为做、使。

items.example: The root solid- sits at the heart of the word.
items.exampleCN: 词根 solid- 位于这个词的核心。

items.meaning: to make or cause to be
items.example: The suffix -ify turns an adjective into a verb of making.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ify 把形容词变成表示「使……」的动词。

items.example: Solid wood lasts longer than veneer.
items.exampleCN: 实木比贴皮更耐用。

items.meaningCN: 表示性质或状态的名词后缀
items.example: The suffix -ity gives the noun solidity.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ity 构成名词 solidity。

items.meaningCN: 表示行为或过程的名词后缀
items.example: The suffix -ation gives solidification.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ation 构成 solidification。

items.example: The suffix -ly gives the adverb solidly.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 构成副词 solidly。

items.meaning: to make or become firm or hard
items.example: The verb keeps the making sense of -ify.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词保留了 -ify 的「使……」含义。

items.example: Solidification is the smooth process of becoming solid.
items.exampleCN: solidification 指变成固体的平滑过程。

items.example: Solidity describes the quality of being solid.
items.exampleCN: solidity 描述「坚实」这一性质。

items.example: Consolidate means to make solid together, and it shares the same root.
items.exampleCN: consolidate 意为「合在一起变坚固」，与目标词共享同一词根。

definition_zh: 独自的；单独的；喜欢独处的；唯一的；孤单的；单独监禁
definition_en: done alone or existing alone, without other people or things around
core_image: 山坡上一间孤零零的小屋，窗户亮着灯，四周没有第二户人家
scene: 雨后的山脊上只有一间小木屋，门前的泥地里留着各自的脚印。A solitary cabin stood on the ridge above the valley, its windows glowing against the dark trees.
sceneCN: 这里 solitary 是「孤独的、偏僻的」（第 3 个义项：独处而无人相伴）；句意：一座孤零零的小屋立在山谷上方的山脊上，窗子在黑影树木间发着光。画面里有雨后的山脊、一间小屋和窗里的灯。

pos.zh: 喜欢独处的；孤独隐居的
独居者；(口语) 单独监禁

derivatives.zh: 同一词根，义为「独处；孤独」
由形容词加后缀 -ly 构成，义为「独自地；孤单地」
来自意大利语，义为「独奏者」，与目标词拼写相近但词源不同

senses.title: Done alone, with nobody else present
senses.definition: done, experienced, or enjoyed by one person alone, with no one else taking part
senses.definitionCN: 由一个人独自完成、经历或享受，没有别人参与
senses.example: She takes a solitary walk along the river every morning.
senses.exampleCN: 她每天早晨沿河独自散步。
senses.why: From Latin solus, meaning alone, this is the plainest layer: one body moving through an activity with no companion.
senses.whyCN: 来自拉丁语 solus（独自），这是最直白的一层：一个人的身体走完一件事，身旁没有同伴。

senses.title: Single and only, not part of a group
senses.definition: being the only one of its kind in a place or group
senses.definitionCN: 在同一地点或群体中只此一个
senses.example: A solitary tree survived the storm in the empty field.
senses.exampleCN: 空旷的田野里只有一棵树在暴风雨中活了下来。
senses.why: A lone object has no neighbours, so being alone on a count turns into meaning simply one, with no other.
senses.whyCN: 孤立的对象没有邻居，于是「在数量上独自一个」就转成了「仅此一个、别无其他」。

senses.title: Placed far away from others
senses.titleCN: 孤独的；偏僻而无人相伴的
senses.definition: isolated or remote, with few or no other people or things around
senses.definitionCN: 孤立的、偏远的，周围没有或几乎没有其他人和物
senses.example: The lighthouse stands on a solitary rock off the coast.
senses.exampleCN: 灯塔矗立在海岸外一块孤零零的礁石上。
senses.why: The alone image extends from people to places: a place becomes solitary when it has nothing else beside it.
senses.whyCN: 「独自」的意象从人扩展到地点：一个地方旁边什么都没有，它就成了孤独的。

senses.title: Preferring to be alone
senses.definition: choosing or feeling comfortable staying away from other people
senses.definitionCN: 选择或习惯于远离他人
senses.example: By nature he is a solitary man who reads rather than talks.
senses.exampleCN: 他天生性格孤僻，宁可读书也不愿交谈。
senses.why: The same word that names the situation can name a temperament, because a person who is usually alone may be so by choice.
senses.whyCN: 指处境的同一个词也能指性格，因为常年独自一人的人，可能是自己愿意如此。

senses.title: Feeling lonely and cut off
senses.definition: making someone feel lonely, especially because of a lack of company
senses.definitionCN: 使人感到孤独的，尤指缺少陪伴时
senses.example: The long, solitary evenings in the new town wore her down.
senses.exampleCN: 新城里无数个漫长而孤单的夜晚让她身心疲惫。
senses.why: When being alone is not chosen but suffered, the image of the lone cabin turns from quiet to sad.
senses.whyCN: 当独处不是选择而是煎熬时，那间孤独小屋的画面就从宁静变成悲伤，于是有了带情感色彩的「孤单」。

senses.title: Being kept apart from other people
senses.definition: keeping a prisoner away from other prisoners as a punishment or for safety
senses.definitionCN: 作为惩罚或出于安全，把囚犯与其他囚犯隔开
senses.example: He spent two weeks in solitary confinement after the fight.
senses.exampleCN: 斗殴之后他被单独监禁了两周。
senses.why: In prison the alone condition is imposed by force, so the word names the hardest version of being placed apart.
senses.whyCN: 在监狱里，「独自」是由强制施加的处境，所以这个词命名了「与人隔开」这种处境最严酷的版本。

intro.en: Solitary comes from Latin solitarius, meaning lonely or solitary, from solus, alone.
intro.cn: solitary 来自拉丁语 solitarius（孤独的、僻静的），源于 solus（独自）。

items.en: Solus means alone, by oneself, with no companions.
items.cn: solus 意为独自、单独一人，没有同伴。

items.en: Solitarius describes people and places that are alone and apart.
items.cn: solitarius 形容人和地方孤单、僻静。

items.en: Solitariu travels through late Latin into French with the sense of lonely.
items.cn: solitariu 经晚期拉丁语进入法语，带有「孤独」的含义。

items.en: Solitary appears in English for a person living alone.
items.cn: 中古英语里 solitary 用来指独自生活的人。

items.en: Legal use gives solitary as a term for being kept apart in prison.
items.cn: 法律用法让 solitary 成为在监狱中与他人隔离的专门说法。

note.en: Solitary keeps the Latin root solus, alone, and stands beside the common words for one and for being without company.
note.cn: solitary 保留拉丁词根 solus（独自），并与表示「一个」或「无人相伴」的常见词相邻。

entries.definition: the state of being alone, often calmly and by choice
entries.definitionCN: 独处的状态，常指宁静自愿的独居

entries.definition: a speech in which a character speaks alone on stage, built from Latin solus and loqui, to speak
entries.definitionCN: 舞台上角色独自进行的独白，由拉丁语 solus 与 loqui（说）构成

entries.definition: a lawyer, only a look-alike word from solicit, with a different origin
entries.definitionCN: 律师，只是拼写相近，源自 solicit，词源不同

entries.definition: without other people present
entries.definitionCN: 独自一人，没有他人在场

entries.definition: only one, not joined with others
cut off from others

normalIntro.en: Solitary rests on the Latin root sol, seen in solo and solitude, so the family all carries the sense of being one and alone.
normalIntro.cn: solitary 依托拉丁词根 sol（独自），solo、solitude 都带这个根，整个词族都含「一个、独自」的意思。

normal.en: Sol- means alone, as in solo and solitude.
normal.cn: 词根 sol- 表示「独自」，solo 和 solitude 都如此。

normal.en: Solitary confinement is the phrase for being locked away alone.
normal.cn: solitary confinement 就是把他一人关起来的说法。

normal.en: A solitary figure is a single person seen walking alone.
normal.cn: a solitary figure 指走着的一个孤单身影。

normal.en: The noun form of the adjective is a solitaire, a lone person or a single gemstone.
normal.cn: 由这个形容词派生的名词是 solitaire，指独居者或单颗宝石。

normal.en: To choose being alone is to live a solitary life, while feeling alone is being lonely.
normal.cn: 主动选择独处叫 live a solitary life，而感到寂寞叫 lonely。

abstract.en: Picture a student finishing the whole exam in silence.
abstract.cn: 想象一名学生在一片静默中独自做完整场考试。

abstract.en: Picture one tree left standing in a stubble field.
abstract.cn: 想象收割后的田地里只剩一棵树。

abstract.en: Picture a lighthouse burning on a rock far from shore.
abstract.cn: 想象灯塔在远离海岸的礁石上亮着。

examples.en: He prefers solitary morning runs before the city wakes.
examples.cn: 他喜欢在城市醒来之前独自晨跑。

examples.en: A solitary rose was the only flower in the garden.
examples.cn: 园子里唯一的花是一枝孤零零的玫瑰。

examples.en: The island has a solitary school with fewer than twenty pupils.
examples.cn: 岛上只有唯一的一所学校，学生不到二十人。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「扫勒特里」——一个人把满地落叶扫得干干净净，只剩自己一个；只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 solus（独自）+ -arius（……的）→ solitarius（孤独的、僻静的）→ 古法语 solitaire → 英语 solitary，核心义「独自无伴」。

sensesIntro.en: Solitary starts from one person doing something alone, extends to the only one of its kind and to places apart, and then splits into chosen privacy and painful loneliness.
sensesIntro.cn: solitary 从「一个人独自做事」出发，扩展到「仅此一个」和「孤立的处所」，再分化为主动选择的清静与被迫承受的孤单。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one cabin on an empty ridge with no second roof in sight.
core.cn: 核心意象：空旷山脊上只有一间小屋，看不到第二片屋顶。

branches.en: A task done alone is the ordinary sense.
branches.cn: 独自完成一件事是日常义项。

branches.en: Being the only one is the counting sense.
branches.cn: 「仅此一个」属于计数层面的义项。

branches.en: A remote place with no neighbour is the place sense.
branches.cn: 四周没有邻里的偏远之处属于处所义项。

branches.en: The same condition can be a chosen temperament or a painful feeling.
branches.cn: 同一种处境既可能是主动选择的性情，也可能是令人痛苦的感受。

branches.en: Forced separation is the harshest form of the image.
branches.cn: 被迫隔离是这一意象最严酷的形式。

intro.en: Solitary is built on the root sol, meaning alone, and the adjective suffix -ary, meaning relating to.
intro.cn: solitary 由词根 sol（独自）与形容词后缀 -ary（与……有关的）构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin solus means alone, and -arius forms adjectives and nouns that belong to a condition.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 solus 意为独自，-arius 构成表示状态的形容词或名词。

items.example: The root sol- gives the family its meaning of being alone.
items.exampleCN: 词根 sol- 给整个词族带来「独自」的含义。

items.example: The suffix -ary turns the root into the adjective solitary.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ary 把词根变成形容词 solitary。

items.example: The suffix -ude forms the noun solitude.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ude 构成名词 solitude。

items.example: She found peace in solitude.
items.exampleCN: 她在独处中获得了宁静。

items.example: The suffix -ly turns the adjective into solitarily.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 把该形容词变成 solitarily。

items.example: A soliloquy joins sol with loqui, to speak.
items.exampleCN: soliloquy 把 sol 与 loqui（说）结合在一起。

items.meaning: a lone person or a single gem
items.example: The word solitaire survives as a name for a lone person.
items.exampleCN: solitaire 保留下来，用作独居者的名称。

items.example: The same suffix also builds nouns such as solitary used as a noun.
items.exampleCN: 同一后缀也能构成名词，如作名词用的 solitary。

items.meaning: the state of being shut in
items.example: The phrase solitary confinement adds confinement to the adjective.
items.exampleCN: solitary confinement 把 confinement 加在这个形容词之后。

items.example: Solo came to English through Italian and only feels related in form.
items.exampleCN: solo 经意大利语进入英语，与目标词只是形式相近。

definition_zh: 独奏；独唱；单独表演；独自的；单独地；单飞的
definition_en: a performance by one person alone, or something done by one person without help
core_image: 聚光灯只照在舞台中央的一个人身上，全场安静下来只听他一个
scene: 演出过半，乐队退到暗处，只留钢琴师坐在中央，一束光打在他身上。The band stepped back into the shadows, and the pianist began a quiet solo that held the whole hall.
sceneCN: 这里 solo 是「独奏、独唱」（第 1 个义项：由一个人单独完成的表演）；句意：乐队退到暗处，钢琴师奏起一段安静的独奏，让整个音乐厅屏息。画面里有舞台中央的一束光、退到暗处的乐队和全场的安静。

derivatives.zh: 由名词加后缀 -ist 构成，义为「独奏者；独唱者」
动词过去式与过去分词，义为「独自完成、单飞过」
动词现在分词，义为「正在独自完成」

senses.title: A performance by one musician
senses.definition: a piece of music played or sung by one performer, or the part played by one person within a group
senses.definitionCN: 由一位表演者演奏或演唱的乐曲，或团体中由一人担任的部分
senses.example: She played a short solo before the orchestra came back in.
senses.exampleCN: 在乐队重新加入之前，她弹了一小段独奏。
senses.why: Solo comes from Italian, the language of music, where it means alone, and its first home is the stage.
senses.whyCN: solo 来自音乐通用的意大利语，本义就是「独自」，它最早的用武之地就是舞台。

senses.title: Flying or acting without another person
senses.definition: done by one person flying or working without a teacher, partner, or crew
senses.definitionCN: 由一个人在没有教练、同伴或机组的情况下飞行或工作
senses.example: He flew solo for the first time after two months of training.
senses.exampleCN: 训练两个月后，他第一次单飞。
senses.why: Aviation borrowed the musical word for one person alone, and the meaning moved from the concert hall to the cockpit.
senses.whyCN: 航空借用了音乐里表示「一人」的词，含义便从音乐厅挪到了驾驶舱。

senses.title: A separate individual career
senses.titleCN: 单飞的；个人独立发展的
senses.definition: working or releasing work as an individual rather than as part of a group
senses.definitionCN: 以个人而非团队一员的身份工作或发表作品
senses.example: After the band broke up, she started a solo career.
senses.exampleCN: 乐队解散后，她开始了单飞事业。
senses.why: The musical sense grows outward to pop culture, where going solo means stepping out of the group.
senses.whyCN: 音乐义项向外扩展到流行文化：go solo 就是从团体里单走出来的意思。

senses.title: Alone in an activity or game
senses.titleCN: 单人模式的；独自进行的
senses.definition: designed for one player or person rather than for a team
senses.definitionCN: 为一个人而不是为团队设计的
senses.example: The new game has both a solo mode and an online team mode.
senses.exampleCN: 这款新游戏既有单人模式，也有在线团队模式。
senses.why: On a screen or a field, solo marks the version of the experience that one person completes without help.
senses.whyCN: 在屏幕或球场上，solo 标出的是「一个人无需帮助就能完成的那个版本」。

senses.title: Done with no one else and no help
senses.definition: as an adverb, doing something entirely on your own, without another person
senses.definitionCN: 作副词时指完全靠自己完成，身边没有别人
senses.example: She crossed the bay solo in a small rowing boat.
senses.exampleCN: 她独自划一条小船横渡了海湾。
senses.why: The alone sense at the heart of the word is used directly as a manner word: in a solo way.
senses.whyCN: 这个词核心的「独自」义直接用作方式词，就是「以独自的方式」。

intro.en: Solo comes from the Italian solo, meaning alone, which is itself from Latin solus, alone.
intro.cn: solo 来自意大利语 solo（独自），而意大利语这个词又源于拉丁语 solus（独自）。

items.en: Solus means alone, without others.
items.cn: solus 意为独自一人，没有别人。

items.en: Solo becomes the Italian word for alone, widely used in music.
items.cn: solo 成为意大利语中表示「独自」的词，在音乐圈广泛使用。

items.en: English borrows solo from Italian music for a passage played by one person.
items.cn: 英语从意大利语音乐中借入 solo，指由一人演奏的段落。

items.en: Solo spreads from music to aviation and other fields as a word for acting alone.
items.cn: solo 从音乐扩展到航空等领域，泛指独自行动。

items.en: Modern English uses solo for gaming modes, individual careers, and everyday choices to act alone.
items.cn: 现代英语把 solo 用于单人模式、个人事业发展以及日常独自行动的选择。

note.en: Solo is a borrowed Italian word beside the Latin family of solum words, and beside the everyday English words for being alone.
note.cn: solo 是从意大利语借入的词，与 solus 一系的拉丁词相邻，也与表示「独自」的日常英语词相邻。

entries.definition: a person who performs a solo
the state of being alone, from Latin solus like the Italian source of solo
entries.definitionCN: 独处的状态，与 solo 的意大利语来源同出拉丁 solus

entries.definition: a game for one player, or a single gemstone, built on the same alone root
entries.definitionCN: 单人纸牌游戏或单颗宝石，同样建立在表示独自的词根上

entries.definition: done or going without a companion or supporter
without other people
without relying on others

normalIntro.en: Solo is short and open, so it sounds like a single note held alone; it comes from music and now means doing anything alone.
normalIntro.cn: solo 拼写短而开阔，听起来像单独拉长的一个音；它出自音乐，如今泛指独自做任何事。

normal.en: Solo is the opposite of a duet and a trio: one is the count.
normal.cn: solo 与二重奏、三重奏相对，关键在于「一个」。

normal.en: The plural and the third person share the same form, solos.
normal.cn: 复数与第三人称单数同形，都是 solos。

normal.en: Go solo and fly solo both mean to act without a partner.
normal.cn: go solo 与 fly solo 都表示不依靠同伴独自行动。

normal.en: A soloist is the person who plays the solo in a group.
normal.cn: soloist 就是在团体里演奏独奏部分的那个人。

normal.en: The verb takes regular endings, so the past is soloed.
normal.cn: 这个动词用规则词尾，过去式是 soloed。

abstract.en: Picture a spotlight narrowing to one chair on a dark stage.
abstract.cn: 想象灯光在暗舞台上一路收窄，只留住一把椅子。

abstract.en: Picture a trainer stepping out of the cockpit and leaving a student alone with the controls.
abstract.cn: 想象教练走出驾驶舱，把操纵杆留给独自一人的学生。

abstract.en: Picture a singer walking away from the band to sign a record on their own.
abstract.cn: 想象一位歌手离开乐队，独自签约录音。

examples.en: His first solo flight lasted only twelve minutes.
examples.cn: 他的第一次单飞只持续了十二分钟。

examples.en: The cellist played a moving solo in the second movement.
examples.cn: 大提琴手在第二乐章里演奏了一段动人的独奏。

examples.en: After years with the group, she released a solo album.
examples.cn: 在团体里待了多年之后，她发行了一张个人专辑。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「搜喽」——全场灯一暗，观众四处「搜索」台上那个人，台上只有他自己；只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 solus（独自）→ 意大利语 solo（独自，音乐术语）→ 英语 solo，核心义「一人独自完成」。

sensesIntro.en: Solo starts as a musical term for one performer, spreads to flying and working alone, and finally works as an adjective, an adverb, and a verb for doing anything by oneself.
sensesIntro.cn: solo 最初指音乐上的单人表演，再扩展到单飞和独自工作，最后可作形容词、副词和动词，泛指一人独自完成。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one spotlight on one performer while the hall stays silent.
core.cn: 核心意象：一束聚光灯照在一位表演者身上，全场安静。

branches.en: A musical solo is where the word began in English.
branches.cn: 音乐上的独奏是这个词在英语里的起点。

branches.en: Flying solo takes the alone sense into the air.
branches.cn: 单飞把「独自」的含义带上了天空。

branches.en: A solo career is the individual version of the group career.
branches.cn: 单飞事业是团体艺人以个人身份发展的版本。

branches.en: Solo modes in games and sports mark the one person path.
branches.cn: 游戏与体育里的单人模式标出「一个人的路」。

branches.en: As an adverb, solo simply means in an alone way.
branches.cn: 作副词时，solo 就是把「独自」直接当方式讲。

intro.en: Solo is borrowed whole from Italian, with the derived English word soloist and several compound expressions built around it.
intro.cn: solo 整体借自意大利语，英语以它派生出 soloist，并围绕它造出若干复合说法。

latinIntro.en: The Italian solo goes back to Latin solus, alone, so this borrowed word still carries a Latin root beneath it.
latinIntro.cn: 意大利语 solo 可追溯到拉丁语 solus（独自），因此这个借来词底下仍带着拉丁词根。

items.example: The Italian word solo means alone.
items.exampleCN: 意大利语 solo 意为独自。

items.example: The suffix -ist forms the noun soloist.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ist 构成名词 soloist。

items.example: The final -o marks the borrowed Italian form.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -o 标记了借入的意大利语形态。

items.example: The soloist stood up for the second half.
items.exampleCN: 独奏者在后半段站了起来。

items.example: Many pilots solo before they get a licence.
items.exampleCN: 许多飞行员在拿到执照之前就会单飞。

items.example: The suffix -ed gives the past form soloed.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ed 构成过去式 soloed。

items.example: The suffix -ing gives soloing.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ing 构成 soloing。

items.example: A solo career means leaving the group for yourself.
items.exampleCN: solo career 意味着离开团体、独自发展。

items.example: To fly solo is to go it alone.
items.exampleCN: fly solo 就是独自去做。

items.example: To go solo is to leave the group behind.
items.exampleCN: go solo 就是离开团体独自发展。
